The samples used in this study were selected as sedimentary samples that had been previously investigated, because the applicability of the sensor was evaluated, as well as the addition of the rate data. Consequently, the DO concentration in the experimental solution decreased as previously observed. However, this decrease in DO can be primarily attributed to the consumption of DO by Fe(II)-bearing minerals in the rock samples, rather than interference from the oxygen sensor. The resulting second-order rate constants strongly support the previously reported rate data and improve reproducibility for this measurement system. These findings contribute to preliminary predictions of recovery from oxic to anoxic conditions in geologic formations and provide insight into the temporal evolution of subsurface DO in the vicinity of a repository.

title: Intrinsic alkalinity of the reactive media regulates the differential immobilization of As(V) and Sb(V) in co-contaminated groundwater
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Applied Geochemistry, Volume 209 Author(s): Wen Zhang, Kai-hua Bai, Jun Tang, Yi-long Zhao, Jun Jiang
abstract: The simultaneous immobilization of arsenic (As) and antimony (Sb) in groundwater is challenged by their competitive interactions, which are strongly influenced by pH fluctuations and complex speciation. Based on permeable reactive barrier (PRB) technology, this study demonstrates the feasibility of manipulating the intrinsic alkalinity of goethite-based fillers using cement to effectively immobilize As(V) and Sb(V) in co-contaminated groundwater. Ordinary Portland cement (OPC), slag-modified Portland cement (SPC), and sulphoaluminate cement (SAC) with distinct hydration reaction were used as binders to fabricate goethite-based fillers with varying solid-phase alkalinity gradients. Batch experiments revealed that the OPC-filler with the highest alkalinity demonstrated preferable immobilization capacity for both As(V) and Sb(V) compared with the SPC- and SAC-fillers under varying initial pH, coexisting ions, and natural organic matter conditions. Duration tests confirmed that the OPC-filler could maintain stable immobilization of both As (>98%) and Sb (>86%) under high-flow-rate accelerated conditions, whereas the other fillers showed rapid Sb breakthrough. Integrated post-test characterizations and geochemical modeling revealed a dual immobilization pathway in the filler: As(V) was primarily immobilized via adsorption onto goethite, whereas Sb(V) immobilization was enhanced by the high-alkalinity microenvironment, which promoted the precipitation of calcium with Sb(V). These findings demonstrate that engineering the intrinsic solid-phase alkalinity of goethite-based PRB filler is an effective strategy for achieving simultaneous immobilization of As(V) and Sb(V) in groundwater.

title: Dynamics and drivers of CO 2 emissions in agricultural river-ditch networks: management and wetland degradation effects
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Applied Geochemistry, Volume 209 Author(s): Xia Li, Xiao-Dong Li, Si-Liang Li, Shi-Yuan Ding, Wan-Fa Wang, Li Bai, Min Xiao, Ming-Guo Wang, Xiao-Long Liu
abstract: As a cornerstone of Northeast China's “grain basket,” the Sanjiang Plain hosts expansive irrigation and drainage networks that function as intensive biogeochemical reactors. However, their contribution to global carbon dioxide (CO2) budgets and mechanisms regulating CO2 production and emissions remains a major uncertainty. Therefore, this study examined the spatiotemporal variations of CO2 concentrations and emission fluxes (fCO2) in a representative wetland-river-ditch network in the Sanjiang Plain, Northeast China. Results revealed that most of the rivers and drainage ditches were highly supersaturated with CO2, acting as atmospheric sources. The fCO2 ranged from −20.7 to 288.9 mmol m−2 d−1 in rivers and reached up to 422.7 mmol m−2 d−1 in ditches, identifying ditches as distinct emission hotspots. Stoichiometric relationships (ΔCO2/ΔO2) and C/N ratios indicated that CO2 production was primarily associated with internal metabolic processes. Furthermore, wetland degradation and agricultural fertilization may enhance carbon export and microbial respiration, facilitating the emission of CO2. Overall, irrigation and drainage networks represent important components of agricultural carbon cycling and should be considered in regional carbon budget assessments and wetland management strategies.

title: Source of uranium (U) and rare earth elements (REE) for unconformity-related U and REE mineralization in the Athabasca Basin, Canada: Insights from accessory minerals in sandstones
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Applied Geochemistry, Volume 209 Author(s): Goktug Harmanci, Guoxiang Chi, Jeremy Powell, Janina Czas, Victoria Tschirhart, Huimin Su, Yumeng Wang, Nahanni Danylczuk
abstract: The Athabasca Basin in Canada hosts the world's largest and highest-grade unconformity-related uranium (URU) deposits, many of which are also enriched in rare earth elements (REE). There has been a long-lasting debate whether the U and REE were sourced from the basin or basement. This study investigates the potential contribution of detrital accessory minerals in the basin, particularly zircon and Ti-oxide (rutile), to U and REE mineralization. The textural and compositional characteristics of these detrital accessory minerals, as well as diagenetic minerals, including Ti-oxide (anatase), iron oxide/hydroxide (IOH) and aluminium phosphate sulfate (APS) minerals, were examined using multiple in-situ analytical methods. The results show that detrital zircon and rutile exhibit extensive dissolution and alteration features and large and irregular variations of U and REE concentrations within individual grains suggesting strong fluid-rock interactions. Large amounts of U and REE, especially heavy REE (HREE), were leached into the basinal brines, while some of them, especially light REE (LREE), were retained by diagenetic minerals. The resulting diagenetic basinal fluids are characterized by strong HREE enrichment, which broadly match the REE patterns of uraninite in the URU ores. Mass balance calculations suggest that 40 to 70 million tonnes of U and 80 to 330 million tonnes of REE, depending on the methods of calculation, could be leached from zircon and rutile. Despite the large variations and uncertainties, these estimations far exceed the amounts found in the URU deposits, implying significant potentials for further U and REE exploration. The results also highlight the vulnerability of zircon and rutile to hydrothermal alteration under certain conditions in sedimentary basins and its significance for large-scale U and REE mineralization.

title: Rheological properties of sensitive marine clays stabilised by inorganic salts - impact of anion and cation
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Applied Geochemistry, Volume 209 Author(s): Kamila Zabłocka, Mohammad Hemayati, Rene Tammen, Erika Eiser, Seyed Ali Ghoreishian Amiri, Barbara Lothenbach, Harald Justnes, Priscilla Paniagua, Klaartje De Weerdt
abstract: This study investigates (1) the applicability of parallel plate rheology for assessing quick clay stabilisation by inorganic salts and (2) the short-term stabilising effects of selected cation–anion combinations. Quick clay from the Tiller-Flotten geotechnical test site was treated with salt solutions containing Na+, K+, Ca2+ and Mg2+ paired with Cl−, OH−, SO4 2− and CO3 2− at concentrations between 0.037 and 0.6 M. A dedicated rheometer protocol enabled extraction of dynamic and static yield shear strengths and structural build-up, revealing non-Newtonian shear-thinning behaviour. Dynamic yield strength from the upwards flow curve was used as the primary parameter and showed good correlation with falling-cone shear strength, with rheology offering higher precision, reproducibility, and reduced sample size. Increasing salt concentration consistently enhanced shear strength, with clear ion-specific trends. Divalent chlorides (CaCl2, MgCl2) were most effective at low concentrations but reached a plateau near 0.2 M, while monovalent chlorides continued to increase the strength, with KCl outperforming NaCl at higher concentrations due to the smaller hydration shell and stronger adsorption of K+. Anion effects were strongly governed by pH: Cl− and SO4 2− (neutral pH) promoted flocculation at low concentrations, whereas OH− and CO3 2− (high pH) required higher cation concentrations to counteract initial deflocculation. Ca(OH)2 produced the highest shear strength overall. The geotechnical stability criterion of 0.33 kPa was reached for all K-salts and for Ca(OH)2. Overall, the results show that short-term stabilisation of quick clay is controlled by cation valence, hydration radius, and anion-dependent pH, providing a mechanistic basis for designing more efficient binders for rapid ground improvement.

title: Integrated experimental and computational investigation of Rhodamine B adsorption onto Moroccan stevensite clay: Kinetics, isotherms, thermodynamics, DSD optimization, DFT, and Monte Carlo analysis
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Applied Geochemistry, Volume 209 Author(s): Jaber Raissouni, El Houssain Chkouri, Ahmed Ait Aghzzaf, María J. Fernández-Sanjurjo, Avelino Núñez-Delgado, Esperanza Álvarez-Rodríguez, Khalid Draoui
abstract: The discharge of synthetic organic dyes into industrial wastewater constitutes a serious environmental problem due to the persistence, toxicity, and non-biodegradable nature of these pollutants. In this study, the adsorption removal of Rhodamine B (RhB), a toxic cationic dye, was investigated using natural stevensite-rich Ghassoul clay (SW) as an abundant, low-cost, and eco-friendly adsorbent. The clay was characterized using FTIR, SEM/EDS, XRD, XRF, and zeta potential analyses to determine its structural and physicochemical properties. Adsorption kinetics showed rapid RhB uptake followed by equilibrium after approximately 60 min, with an experimental adsorption capacity of 94.1 mg g−1 and 94.1% removal efficiency. The pseudo-second-order kinetic model provided the best fit (R2 ≈ 0.9996), suggesting that adsorption was controlled mainly by surface interactions and diffusion processes. Equilibrium data were analyzed using several nonlinear isotherm models. Heterogeneous models, particularly Fritz–Schluender V, Redlich–Peterson, and Sips, produced the best statistical fits (R2 ≈ 0.996), indicating adsorption on energetically heterogeneous surfaces through combined monolayer, multilayer, and pore-filling mechanisms. The nonlinear Langmuir model predicted a maximum adsorption capacity of 208.85 mg g−1. Thermodynamic analysis confirmed that adsorption was spontaneous and endothermic. The Definitive Screening Design (DSD) approach optimized operational parameters influencing adsorption performance. Complementary Density Functional Theory (DFT), topological analyses using the program Multiwfn, and Monte Carlo simulations demonstrated that electrostatic attraction, hydrogen bonding, van der Waals forces, and π–π interactions govern RhB adsorption onto stevensite surfaces.

title: Chromium mica geochemistry as a potential indicator of Au mineralization: Evidence from the Dongcaogou and Haopinggou Au deposits, Eastern Qinling, China
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Applied Geochemistry, Volume 209 Author(s): Hu Ziqi, Zhang Dexian, Xiao Dian, Zhou Jialing, He Hao
abstract: Chromium mica (fuchsite) alteration is widely developed in gold (Au) deposits across the Western Qinling and Xiong'ershan districts, yet its specific relationship with Au mineralization remains poorly constrained. This study systematically investigates the structural characteristics, major and trace element compositions, and fluid-mineral relationships of chromium mica from the Dongcaogou and Haopinggou polymetallic deposits, Eastern Qinling, China. Analytical results demonstrate systematic spatial variations in unit-cell parameters and geochemical signatures: chromium mica from shallow-level Dongcaogou display expanded cell volumes (918-941 Å3) with elevated Cr2O3 (0.01-10.07%) and K2O (3.17-6.97%), indicative of intensive alteration linked to gold enrichment, whereas deep-seated Haopinggou samples exhibit smaller cell volumes (915 Å3) of phengitic composition, reflecting high-pressure, low-strain conditions. Elemental correlations (Cr-Al-K-Fe-Zn) reveal metal-enrichment processes in ore-forming fluids, with increasing Cr content signaling key mineralization drivers including reduced oxygen fugacity, acidic pH, and intense fluid-rock interaction. These findings establish chromium mica as a valuable exploration indicator for Au mineralization in the Eastern Qinling orogenic belt.

title: Paleoclimate imprint and recharge conditions of the northwestern Caucasus groundwater: an isotopic study of the Azov-Kuban Artesian Basin
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Applied Geochemistry, Volume 209 Author(s): Igor Tokarev, Evgeny Yakovlev, Tatiana Lyubimova, Andrey Puchkov, Sergey Druzhinin, Roman Smagin, Valeriya Timoshina, Alexey Tudvachev, Artem Konkin
abstract: The article investigates the isotopic characteristics and origin of groundwater within the Quaternary and Neogene aquifers of the Azov-Kuban Artesian Basin (AKAB), Northwestern Caucasus. Isotopic analysis revealed the presence of a distinct “Late Pleistocene fossil groundwater” water component in the deeper sedimentary horizons. These groundwaters are significantly depleted in heavy isotopes, with δ18O values ranging from −17.54‰ to −12.50‰ (mean −14.76‰) and δ2H from −146.1‰ to −89.0‰ (mean −107.4‰). The total absence of tritium and radiocarbon dating results (26-34 ka) confirm that these resources are paleowaters. In contrast, modern groundwater in the recharge areas of the AKAB foothills (200-400 m a.s.l.) exhibits enriched isotopic signatures, with mean values of −10.81‰ for δ18O and −75.5‰ for δ2H. These signatures closely match the weighted mean isotopic composition of local precipitation during the recharge season (−10.7‰ for δ18O and −73.8‰ for δ2H). The presence of tritium and anthropogenic nitrate pollution in the upper geological section further validates the modern origin of these waters. A comparison between the recharge waters and the deep-seated “Late Pleistocene fossil groundwater” component indicates that the latter originated during the cold climatic stage of the Late Pleistocene. The spatial distribution of δ18O and δ2H shows that the proportion of paleowater increases with depth and distance from the foothill recharge zones. These findings provide essential evidence of paleoclimatic imprints on the regional hydrogeological system, highlighting the vulnerability of fossil groundwater reserves.

title: Strontium isotopic evidence for heterogeneous sediment-water interactions in inland groundwater of the western Bengal Basin
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Applied Geochemistry, Volume 209 Author(s): Pousali Pathak, Deependra Singh, Vineet Goswami, Prosenjit Ghosh
abstract: Evaluation of relative contributions of aquifer bulk mineral sources on groundwater chemistry remains challenging owing to heterogeneous hydrostratigraphy and seasonally variable hydrogeochemistry. The diverse geochemical composition of Ganga-Brahmaputra floodplain sediments found in inland aquifers of the Bengal Basin, and their impact on groundwater chemistry over seasonal timescales, are not well understood. This study combines seasonal groundwater geochemistry with isotope-based mass-balance modeling to constrain the controls on dissolved Sr and 87Sr/86Sr in depth-bound inland groundwater from the western Bengal Basin, India, located within the Hooghly/Ganga floodplain. To understand the spatial variations in inland groundwater compositions across the Bengal floodplain, the present database has been compared with available data from the eastern Bengal Basin (Bangladesh) located in both the Ganga and Brahmaputra drainage basins. Shallow groundwater exhibits variable hydrogeochemistry and Ca/Sr molar ratios together with relatively radiogenic 87Sr/86Sr that show limited seasonal variability, whereas dissolved solute concentrations are generally higher during the pre-monsoon period. By Comparison with available geochemical data for Ganga River bedload sediment-water, we suggest that (i) detrital carbonate dissolution accounts for an estimated 74-93% of Sr release to shallow groundwater, and (ii) localized silicate weathering contributes to heterogeneous Sr release with radiogenic 87Sr/86Sr in seasonal shallow groundwater, followed by secondary interactions with exchangeable clay-sediment fractions. Secondary interactions with exchangeable clay-sediment fractions may subsequently modify dissolved Sr concentrations and Ca/Sr ratios without substantially influencing 87Sr/86Sr. Further, we estimate that inland groundwater discharge from the western Bengal Basin delivers (8.8 ± 3.9) × 105 mol yr−1 of Sr to the Hooghly/Ganga River.

title: Germanium and its isotopes in saline and brine groundwaters (Western Carpathians, Poland): Effects of diagenetic processes
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Applied Geochemistry, Volume 209 Author(s): Dariusz Dobrzyński, Marek Duliński, Jakub Karasiński, Klaudia Tetfejer, Andrii Tupys, Marcin Stępień, Katarzyna Wątor, Lucyna Rajchel
abstract: The germanium (Ge) content and its isotope ratio (IR) in saline and brine groundwaters from the Polish Outer Carpathians and Carpathian Foredeep (southern Poland) have been investigated. The Ge IR of continental groundwater in such geological environments has not previously been studied. This study found a wide variation in Ge concentrations in the groundwaters, increasing in the order of the following chemical water types: Na-Cl brines (<0.5–2.6 μg/L), Na-Cl saline waters (<0.5–42 μg/L), and Na-HCO3 saline waters (1.1–104 μg/L). The variation in Ge concentration is due to the different formation histories of the current composition of each water, including the mixing of formation water with infiltration water. The germanium in the studied formation water is derived mainly from minerals and organic matter transformed during the diagenesis of rock formations. The mixing of formation water with infiltration water results in a lower Ge concentration. In the Na-HCO3 saline groundwater, elevated Ge concentrations are accompanied by isotopically heavier oxygen compositions (with δ18O values of up to 6.2‰) due to the presence of dehydration water, which is released during the transformation of clay minerals, mainly the illitisation of smectite. The Ge IR values, which span a wide range (δ74/70Ge from 0.97‰ to 5.21‰), exceed previously reported values for continental groundwaters (1.21‰–4.02‰; Siebert et al., 2006; Baronas et al., 2020; Dobrzyński et al., 2024) and show greater enrichment in isotopically heavy Ge than continental crustal rocks (average δ74/70Ge value of 0.58 ± 0.21‰). The enrichment of the studied waters in heavier Ge isotopes was plausibly caused by the preferential removal of light isotopes by iron oxyhydroxides and clay minerals. The Ge IR values of formation waters are changed by (1) possible mixing with infiltration water components and, in the case of the shallowest water intakes, (2) the preferential immobilization of light Ge isotopes by secondary Fe oxyhydroxides and clay minerals abundantly present in the near-surface zone.

title: Investigating iron–sulphur–phosphate transformation dynamics during redox-controlled microaeration of digested sludge towards improved resource recovery
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Applied Geochemistry, Volume 209 Author(s): Sophie Banke, Femke Deelstra, Thomas Prot, Leon Korving, Carlo Belloni, Iulian A. Dugulan, Mark C.M. van Loosdrecht
abstract: Iron is an attractive binding partner for phosphorus removal from digested sludge, with recovery as the Fe(II) phosphate mineral vivianite (Fe3(PO4)2·8H2O) representing a promising resource recovery pathway. However, sulphides compete strongly with phosphate for Fe(II), limiting vivianite formation and often requiring higher iron dosages. Because both iron and sulphur undergo redox transformations, controlled microaeration may alter the balance between iron sulphides, iron phosphates, and oxidized iron and sulphur species. This study investigated the effect of oxidation–reduction potential (ORP)-controlled microaeration (−220 to 0 mV) on Fe–S–P transformations in digested sludge. Microaeration showed contrasting effects. Mössbauer spectroscopy indicated an approximately 20% decrease in the Fe(II) associated with the vivianite fraction under all ORP conditions, while a pyrite-like iron sulphide phase remained largely unchanged. In contrast, the soluble phase showed increasing sulphur concentrations (ultimately recovered as sulphate) and a ∼70% decrease in soluble phosphorus, suggesting enhanced iron–phosphate binding or adsorption during microaeration. Although the applied aeration conditions ultimately did not lead to vivianite formation, the proposed mechanism identifies an early microaeration window that favours phosphorus removal, providing a basis for further optimization of microaeration strategies for phosphorus recovery from anaerobic sludges.

title: Coupling structural-mineralization processes in the Tudui gold deposit, Jiaodong Peninsula: Constraints from pyrite trace elements and EBSD analysis
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Applied Geochemistry, Volume 209 Author(s): Junjie Xu, Huan Li, Mohamed Faisal, Bowen Zhu, Wenbo Sun
abstract: Despite decades of research on hydrothermal gold systems, the micro-scale processes that govern the transition from initial gold precipitation to economic concentrations remain poorly understood, limiting our ability to predict ore formation. In the world-class Jiaodong gold province, the Tudui deposit provides an excellent case for investigating these processes using integrated microanalytical methods. In this contribution, we present the first integrated LA-ICP-MS trace element and electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD) microstructural analyses of pyrites from leptynites and diorite porphyry dikes in the study area to constrain the occurrence and enrichment mechanisms of gold. The pyrite Au-As relationship indicates that, in addition to previously identified visible gold, gold also occurs as invisible lattice-bound gold within pyrite. Trace element signatures suggest that the Tudui deposit is a hydrothermal gold system formed under epithermal, low-to-moderate temperature conditions, and Co/Ni ratios (0-81.1 ppm) together with Co/Sb-Se/Sb systematics are consistent with a mantle-derived fluid contribution. Discrimination diagrams based on Au-As/Sb and Se/Ge-Co/Ni demonstrate that gold precipitation was controlled by multiple coupled processes, including fluid-rock reaction, fluid boiling, and meteoric water mixing, which collectively destabilized Au(HS)2 - complexes and triggered gold deposition. EBSD results show that Tudui pyrites primarily experienced brittle deformation with subordinate plastic deformation, creating extensive microstructures and crystal defects that acted as favorable sites for gold deposition. These microstructures also established preferential pathways for trace element diffusion, enabling Au and other elements to migrate and precipitate along microfractures driven by chemical gradients between pyrite cores and rims. Overall, the Tudui deposit represents a structurally controlled, coupled metallogenic system. This study establishes an integrated macro-micro-scale model for mineralization in Jiaodong-type deposits and provides a theoretical basis for regional gold exploration in the Jiaodong Peninsula.

title: Photo-stimulated reductive dissolved Fe 2+ from epitaxial twinned goethite accelerated by fulvic acid: Insight from the band structure and photochemical activity
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Applied Geochemistry, Volume 209 Author(s): Shanshan Yang, Fei Liu, Xiao Ge, Hongrui Ding, Anhuai Lu
abstract: The photo-stimulated reductive dissolution of semiconducting iron (hydro)oxides plays a vital role in iron (bio)geochemistry processes. Epitaxial twinned goethite (Goe-Hem), a typical goethite twin composed of a hematite center with acicular goethite outgrowths, is widely distributed in natural environment. Nevertheless, studies exploring the photochemical activity of Goe-Hem remain limited. In this study, photo-stimulated reductive dissolution process of Goe-Hem were investigated in depth. Physicochemical characterization revealed that Goe-Hem consists of twinned goethite crystals with a hematite core, containing 73% goethite and 27% hematite. In the presence of fulvic acid, the concentration of photo-stimulated reductively dissolved Fe2+ (aq) from Goe-Hem was higher than that from goethite. Consequently, Goe-Hem exhibited superior photo-stimulated reductive ability than goethite. This enhanced activity was ascribed to the stronger visible light absorption, narrower band gap energy and more negative conduction band energy of Goe-Hem relative to goethite. The photo-stimulated reductively dissolved Fe2+ (aq) from Goe-Hem play a vital role in iron cycling and biological iron acquisition in nature.

title: Geochemical fractionation, mineralogical insights and environmental risk of toxic elements in mining-impacted soils of Zamfara State, Nigeria
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Applied Geochemistry, Volume 209 Author(s): Jajati Mandal, Waheed Ariyo Bakare, Effiom Oku, Barnabas Iliya Musa, Abhishek Sharma, A.S.M. Fazle Bari, Michael D. Wood, Simon M. Hutchinson, Debapriya Mondal, Mohammad Mahmudur Rahman
abstract: This study examined the concentrations, geochemical partitioning, mineralogical controls, and probable mobility of potentially toxic elements (PTEs) in mining impacted surface soils from Anka, Zamfara State, Nigeria. Soil samples (n = 50) were analyzed for physicochemical properties, total elemental burdens, and sequential extraction fractions. The soils ranged from sandy loam to clay loam and showed moderately acidic to near-neutral pH, elevated organic carbon, and high cation exchange capacity, reflecting substantial capacity for metal retention. Total elemental concentrations revealed lead (Pb) in the highest amount (1240.23 ± 92.94 mg kg−1), compared to arsenic (As), zinc (Zn), manganese (Mn), barium (Ba), and iron (Fe). Correlation studies indicated strong associations between Ba-Fe and Mn-Pb, suggesting shared mineralogical or oxide-based controls on distribution. Sequential extraction revealed marked differences in elemental mobility. Lead was primarily bound to reducible Fe-Mn oxides (∼83%), with only ∼13% in the extractable fraction. Arsenic was dominated by residual and oxidizable pools (>90%), indicating minimal mobility. However, Ba and Fe remained primarily in residual and reducible forms. In contrast, Zn was highly labile, with nearly 90% occurring in the extractable fraction displaying mixed extractable and reducible associations and reflecting its redox sensitivity. Mineralogical analyses confirmed quartz-dominant soils containing illite, muscovite, albite, galena, and Pb-As jarosite, with SEM-EDS further verifying PbS (galena), supporting the limited bioavailability of Pb in oxic conditions. Risk Assessment Code (RAC) values placed As in low-risk and Fe in the no-risk category, Ba in medium to high risk, Mn in high risk and Pb in medium risk, and Zn in very high risk (∼90%). Overall ecological risk ranking followed the order Zn > Mn > Ba > Pb > As > Fe. These findings highlight that while total Pb remains elevated, its mobility is restricted by mineralogical sinks, whereas Zn, despite low concentrations, exhibits high mobility and environmental responsiveness. These contrasting behaviours emphasize the need to interpret total elemental concentrations alongside geochemical fractionation when assessing contamination risk in mining-impacted landscapes.

title: Stable isotope fingerprints of Ni-Cu-PGE sulfide remobilization in Mesoarchean ultramafic-mafic rocks
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Applied Geochemistry, Volume 209 Author(s): Shounak Dutta, Sisir K. Mondal
abstract: The origin of enigmatic Archean breccia-hosted Ni-Cu-PGE deposits is often debated because primary orthomagmatic and secondary hydrothermal mineralization can be difficult to distinguish. In this study, we investigate the Mesoarchean Nuasahi Ultramafic-Mafic Complex (India) using integrated petrology, mineral chemistry, and S-O-H isotope geochemistry to resolve the history of metal mobilization in its breccia zone. Our results data reveal a multi-stage mineralization process. An initial magmatic stage involved the interaction of a fluid-rich gabbroic melt with ultramafic-chromitite clasts, which induced sulfide liquid immiscibility and formed a high-temperature (∼950 °C) pyrrhotite–pentlandite–chalcopyrite assemblage with a mantle-like sulfur isotope composition (δ34S ∼ 0‰). The primary assemblage was later overprinted by hydrothermal alteration, characterised by the replacement of chromite by ferrianchromite and the growth of secondary pyrite-chalcopyrite at a lower temperature. Secondary chalcopyrite is selectively enriched in 34S (δ34S ∼ 1‰) relative to the primary pyrrhotite, producing pronounced isotopic disequilibrium. Oxygen and hydrogen isotopes in coexisting chlorite (δ18O ∼2.4‰; δD ∼ −28‰) indicate that the altering fluid resembled heated Archean seawater. We propose that the infiltration of this seawater remobilized primary sulfides, concentrating mobile chalcophile elements such as Pd. At the same time, the overall mantle-like sulfur signature was retained due to the low sulfate content of the Archean oceans. Selective sulfur-isotope disequilibrium in sulfide pairs thus provides a robust tracer of cryptic seawater-driven hydrothermal remobilization in ancient ultramafic-hosted ore systems.

title: Mineralogical and geochemical controls on Co-V-Pt-Ni enrichment in manganese mineralization: evidence from the Dilli deposit, Eastern Türkiye
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Applied Geochemistry, Volume 209 Author(s): Mehmet Ali Gücer, Okay Çimen, Alican Aktağ, Serdar Keskin
abstract: The growing demand for critical minerals driven by the global energy transition and advanced technologies highlights the importance of unconventional metal reservoirs. This study investigates the Ni-, Co-, V-, and Pt-enriched Dilli manganese deposit (Kemaliye-Erzincan, Eastern Türkiye) to constrain the mineralogical, geochemical, and genetic controls on critical metal enrichment in Mn oxide mineralization. An integrated approach combining field observations, petrography, X-ray diffraction (XRD), whole-rock geochemistry, mineral chemistry, and stable C-O isotope analysis was applied to better understand the potential origin of critical mineral enrichments. The mineralization is dominated by Mn4+-bearing oxides, principally pyrolusite and hollandite, accompanied by minor rhodochrosite. High MnO (39-64 wt%) and very low Al2O3 and Fe2O3 contents indicate chemical precipitation with negligible detrital input. Discrimination diagrams and trace-element systematics consistently support a structurally controlled hydrothermal origin. Chondrite-normalized REE patterns display low total REE and very low Nd contents comparable to typical hydrothermal deposits, whereas neutral to slightly positive Ce anomalies and non-chondritic Y/Ho ratios suggest limited oxidative interaction with surface-derived fluids rather than primary marine hydrogenetic growth. Stable C–O isotope compositions of co-genetic calcite are inconsistent with a purely marine depositional environment and indicate precipitation from low-to moderate-temperature hydrothermal fluids. Mineral chemistry reveals strong phase-specific partitioning: hollandite preferentially incorporates V and Ba, whereas pyrolusite is enriched in Ni. Cobalt occurs in both phases, whereas Pt may also be present in both Mn oxide phases, suggesting that trace-element distribution is influenced by both crystallochemical and physicochemical controls. The enrichment of Ni, Co, and Pt is most plausibly linked to hydrothermal fluid circulation through ultramafic units, which likely acted as the primary metal source prior to precipitation. The Dilli deposit thus represents a structurally controlled hydrothermal Mn system enriched in critical metals, emphasizing the exploration relevance of Mn oxide mineral chemistry in identifying alternative sources of critical metals in Türkiye.

title: Relative kinetics of precipitation of barium chromate and barite in groundwater
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Applied Geochemistry, Volume 209 Author(s): Abhas Singh, Mainak Bhattacharya, Ashwini Kumar Mohapatra
abstract: Water-soluble and carcinogenic hexavalent chromium [Cr(VI)] poses serious health risks due to its potential migration in aquifers and interaction with naturally present barium [Ba] to form sparingly soluble colloidal barium chromate [BaCrO4(s)]. However, Ba may also react with other solutes predominantly present in many groundwaters like dissolved sulfate [SO4], causing precipitation of barite [BaSO4(s)]. The eventual fate of Cr(VI) in such groundwaters may be governed by the relative rates of formation of these two solids, which are currently not known. In this contribution, simultaneous formation of BaCrO4(s) and BaSO4(s) in groundwater matrix and their relative kinetics were investigated through continuous flow stirred tank reactor experiments. Chromium-free Ba-spiked SO4-containing groundwater was introduced into the reactor, preloaded with Ba-free Cr(VI)-spiked SO4-containing groundwater, at a flow rate of 0.2 mL min−1. Aqueous samples were collected with time and analyzed for Cr(VI), SO4, Ba, and pH till steady-state was attained. Geochemical analysis of solute data and characterization of the precipitated solids confirmed rapid formation of a solid solution of ∼86 mol% BaCrO4(s) and ∼14 mol% BaSO4(s). Solution saturation indices with respect to BaCrO4(s) gradually decreased over time, but persistent supersaturation with BaSO4(s) suggested conditions favorable for formation of BaSO4(s). Time-dependent Cr(VI), SO4, and Ba concentrations were modelled with process-based mass balance equations. Optimized surface area normalized precipitation rate constants of BaCrO4(s) and BaSO4(s) were obtained as 6.3-8.6 × 10−8 mol m−2 s−1 and 1.3 × 10−8 mol m−2 s−1, respectively, indicating that BaCrO4(s) precipitates approximately five times faster than BaSO4(s). Determination of these constants would help in accurate prediction of Cr(VI) transport in contaminated aquifers rich in Ba and possibly similar co-solutes.

title: XAS evidence for Sb(V)-ferrihydrite reduction into Sb(III)-magnetite during anoxic incubation of stormwater road basin sediments
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Applied Geochemistry, Volume 209 Author(s): Areej Adra, Maëva Philippe, Pierre Le Pape, Georges Ona-Nguema, Gautier Landrot, Ludovic Delbes, Elora Bourbon, Katell Quénéa, Sophie Ayrault
abstract: Antimony (Sb) presents versatile chemical forms in urban (sub)surface environments, the identity of which being driven by local redox conditions. Due to its use as additive in products for its flame-retardant properties, urban environments such as the Parisian area (Paris, France) are particularly subjected to Sb contamination. This is particularly observed in stormwater basin sediments, collecting Sb from runoff on road surfaces. Here, we used these sediments as a reactive ecosystem for aging Sb-bearing ferrihydrite, standing as a classical Sb carrier phase of surface environments and as possible input phase to the basins. Batch experiments were performed by mixing stormwater pond sediments plus Sb(V)-bearing ferrihydrite (Fh-Sb(V)) and were aged up to 210 days under a water column in oxic or anoxic conditions. For each series, an individual batch sample was sampled at 1, 7, 28 and 210 days of aging. Liquid samples were analyzed by ICP-MS, while Fe and Sb speciation were studied by X-ray absorption spectroscopy (XANES/EXAFS) to study Sb release to surface waters and the temporal evolution of Sb speciation. Whatever the experimental conditions, Sb release into solution remains below one percent of the initial stock introduced in the sediment, decorrelated of Fe(II) release and organic matter consumption during reduction processes. Under anoxic conditions, XANES data at the Fe K-edge show the transformation of ferrihydrite into magnetite. From EXAFS analysis at the Sb K-edge, we unambiguously identify a novel reaction route, Sb(V)-bearing ferrihydrite reduction into Sb(III)-bearing magnetite, likely resulting from anoxic aging in a biotic medium. In the oxic experiment, diffusion of air through the initially anoxic water column resulted in the late oxidation of the newly Sb(III)-magnetite formed into Sb(V)-bearing phases. This study shows the strong geochemical reactivity of Sb when submitted to redox fluctuations and that iron-reducing activity likely drives Sb speciation in the presence of available Fe from poorly-crystalline ferrihydrite (Fh). Thus, the fundamental knowledge we bring here could help to define conditions propitious to limiting soluble Sb release from the solid phase in contaminated sediments submitted to redox fluctuations.

title: Differential responses of vanadate reduction to soil aggregate types
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Applied Geochemistry, Volume 209 Author(s): Zhenhan Li, Song Wang, Fengyuan Zhuang, Qinghao Zhang, Baogang Zhang
abstract: Different soil aggregate fractions create distinct biogeochemical microhabitats, driving divergent ecological adaptations and functional traits. In this study, different aggregate fractions from a vanadium-contaminated soil were inoculated into the reactors to evaluate their differences in pentavalent vanadium [V(V)] reduction capacity. Micro-aggregates (MiA) achieved the highest V(V) removal efficiency of 96.2 ± 0.12% and the fastest first-order removal kinetics (rate constant 0.06 h−1), followed by medium aggregates, small aggregates, and large aggregates. The microbial consortia from aggregate could transform toxic soluble V(V) into less mobile tetravalent vanadium [V(IV)] precipitates, thereby contributing to the remediation of vanadium-contaminated soil. During the V(V) reduction process, microbial communities underwent significant changes, exhibiting lower richness and diversity and forming a distinct cluster compared to the initial samples. Meanwhile, the relative abundance of metal-reducing genera increased from 5.29 ± 0.79% to 39.2 ± 12.3%. Co-occurrence network analysis revealed tight microbial collaboration, whereas larger aggregate fractions were associated with lower V(V) removal efficiency. Metagenomic analysis further revealed that V(V) reduction genes were potentially associated with reductive metabolism and electron transfer genes. The microbiome in MiA exhibited the highest cytochrome c levels and the strongest expression of potential V(V) reduction genes of omcB and narG, highlighting microorganisms derived from MiA-aggregates as primary drivers of vanadium detoxification in contaminated soils.

title: Molecular compositions and source identification of organic aerosols in the highly polluted city: Dhaka, Bangladesh
description: Publication date: Available online 21 September 2026 Source: Applied Geochemistry Author(s): Mosammat.J.Fardus Jui, Md. Mozammel Haque, Mohammad Lokman Hossain, Masum Billah, Md. Farhan Ahmed, S.M.Mostahidul Hasan, Abul Kalam M. Lutfor Rahman
abstract: Organic aerosol (OA) represents a fundamental component of atmospheric particulate matter and is widely acknowledged as a critical contributor to ambient air degradation and climate change. Dhaka, among the most polluted cities globally, experiences alarmingly poor air quality. Aerosol samples collected in Dhaka, Bangladesh, during the winter of 2020 (from 10 January to 10 February), were examined to determine their carbonaceous fractions, organic constituents, and stable carbon (δ13C) and nitrogen (δ15N) isotopic compositions of total carbon (TC) and total nitrogen (TN) in fine particulate matter (PM2.5). The measured organic content, calculated as the sum of all quantified target organic compound concentrations (n-alkanes, PAHs, hopanes, and steranes), was considerably higher at night (avg. 768 ± 501 ng m-3) compared to the daytime (349 ± 506 ng m-3). This disparity is likely attributable to the presence of atmospheric inversion layers and elevated nighttime emissions from heavy-duty vehicles. N-Alkanes were the prevalent compounds (mean total: 454 ng m-3), followed by polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) (80.4 ng m-3), hopanes (9.38 ng m-3), and steranes (2.61 ng m-3). The low carbon preference index (CPI) of n-alkanes (mean: 1.30) indicates a predominantly anthropogenic origin. The PAH profile was primarily composed of high molecular weight (HMW) PAHs (4-ring and 5-ring compounds), constituting over 75% of the total, emphasizing the significant health risks posed by Dhaka's aerosols. Diagnostic ratios (DRs) suggest that HMW PAHs were primarily associated with fossil fuel combustion, and hopanes were linked to traffic emissions. The δ13C and δ15N isotopic signatures suggest that human-related activities, particularly the combustion of fossil-based fuels, including coal and petroleum products, and biomass burning, are the predominant sources of carbonaceous and nitrogenous aerosols. Positive Matrix Factorization (PMF) was applied to identify and quantify the key sources of PM2.5 in the study area, revealing significant contributions from coal combustion, traffic, and biomass burning emissions. The health risk assessment highlights a substantial carcinogenic threat from airborne PAHs, with risk levels far exceeding the World Health Organization’s (WHO) recommended standards. These findings point out the urgent need for local and regional pollution control measures to reduce excessive anthropogenic aerosol emissions in South Asia.

title: Differential Effects of Continuous Rainfall on Iron-Bound Organic Carbon within Subtropical Red Soil Aggregates
description: Publication date: Available online 20 September 2026 Source: Applied Geochemistry Author(s): Qianyu Long, Degen Zhu, Weizhi Chen, Xiang Liu, Jiyuan Cai, Hu Wang, Yuanlong Li, Wenlin Wu, Liankai Zhang
abstract: Climate change has increased the frequency of persistent extreme rainfall events in subtropical regions, altering red-soil aggregate structure and carbon cycling. Fe-bound organic carbon (Fe-OC) contributes to the long-term stabilization of soil organic carbon (SOC) in red soils, but extreme rainfall may alter Fe-OC stability. We combined continuous rainfall simulations with δ13C isotope tracing, synchrotron radiation Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy (SR-FTIR), and scanning electron microscopy coupled with energy dispersive spectroscopy (SEM-EDS) to investigate Fe-OC stability in red soil aggregates under continuous rainfall. Continuous rainfall reorganized soil structure and reduced the proportion of macroaggregates by 12.38%. Fe-OC showed size-dependent differences, increasing by 102.53% in macroaggregates but decreasing by 28.02% in microaggregates. Feo increased by 5.08% in macroaggregates and 5.36% in microaggregates. SR-FTIR and SEM-EDS indicated that continuous rainfall promoted associations between Fe oxides and OC in macroaggregates but weakened them in microaggregates. δ13C tracing showed that the added carbon source increased Fe-OC formation in silt+clay and improved aggregate stability. These results indicate contrasting aggregate responses: Fe-OC stabilization was maintained in macroaggregates but declined in microaggregates. External carbon input may therefore enhance SOC stability by promoting Fe-OC formation in the fine fraction. This study provides a new mechanistic perspective for understanding the formation and stabilization of organic carbon in red soils under the combined effects of extreme rainfall and external carbon input in the context of global climate change.

title: Galena as a recorder of metal sourcing and sulfur evolution in a rift-related sediment-hosted Pb–Zn system: Insights from the Gunga deposit, Pakistan
description: Publication date: Available online 17 September 2026 Source: Applied Geochemistry Author(s): Muhammad A. Gul, Huishan Zhang, Mohamed Faisal, Zahid Imran, Nosheen Akhtar, Rizwan Sarwar Awan, Xiaoyong Yang
abstract: Galena is one of the most robust recorders of ore-fluid Pb isotope compositions in sediment-hosted Pb–Zn systems; however, coupled sulfur–lead isotope systematics in galena remain underexplored in many deposits. This study presents the first integrated major-element and in situ sulfur–lead isotope dataset for galena from the Gunga Pb–Zn deposit, a rift-related sediment-hosted system developed along the western margin of the Indian Plate. Galena from the Lower Mineralization Zone (LMZ) and Upper Mineralization Zone (UMZ) is chemically homogeneous and close to ideal PbS stoichiometry, with Pb 85.6–87.2 wt.% and analytical totals of 99.06–99.87 wt.%. These features are consistent with precipitation from low-temperature basinal brines and indicate effective preservation of primary compositions. Galena defines a remarkably narrow Pb isotope field (206Pb/204Pb = 18.541–18.554; 207Pb/204Pb = 15.682–15.692; 208Pb/204Pb = 38.705–38.727; n = 32), consistent with a compositionally homogeneous or well-mixed upper-crustal Pb reservoir. In contrast, sulfur isotope compositions vary strongly with mineralogy and stratigraphic position. Galena ranges from −1.0 to +4.9‰ overall, whereas sphalerite ranges from −10.5 to −0.7‰ in the LMZ and +3.0 to +5.6‰ in the UMZ, and pyrite ranges from −15.0 to +20.0‰ and −23.5 to +26.2‰, respectively. The apparent zone-scale δ34S difference between sphalerite and galena changes from −5.7‰ in the LMZ to +3.1‰ in the UMZ. Inter-mineral sulfur isotope relationships indicate pronounced disequilibrium in the LMZ, consistent with open-system fluid flow and kinetically controlled sulfide precipitation. In the UMZ, restoration of the expected sphalerite > galena ordering indicates a greater approach toward isotopic equilibration under more focused and chemically buffered conditions. Together, the narrow galena Pb-isotope field and zone-dependent sulfur-isotope patterns reveal a clear contrast between comparatively homogeneous metal-source information and evolving sulfur-system conditions during mineralization. These results demonstrate that galena provides a robust quantitative record of primary ore-fluid Pb isotope signatures and, when interpreted with coexisting sulfides, offers critical insight into sulfur evolution in multi-stage sediment-hosted Pb–Zn systems.

title: Elemental and isotope geochemistry of Smackover Formation brines in Alabama and Arkansas: Implications for fluid mixing and water-rock interaction
description: Publication date: Available online 11 September 2026 Source: Applied Geochemistry Author(s): Kelly Kreitzer, Ming-Kuo Lee, Haibo Zou, Yang Wang, Andrew L. Masterson, Ann Sullivan Ojeda, Zeki, M. Billor, Natalia Malina, Gregory M. Guthrie, Bonnie McDevitt, Ann Arnold, Demi Durham
abstract: This study investigates the geochemical characteristics of brines within the Upper Jurassic Smackover Formation in Alabama and Arkansas through elemental and isotopic analyses and geochemical modeling to reveal the extent and nature of fluid mixing and water-rock interactions. Smackover Formation brines exhibit Na-Cl-Ca hydrogeochemical facies and sulfate depletion relative to seawater. Lower sulfate concentrations, coupled with high H2S concentrations in some brines (0-364 mg/L) at temperatures >80°C, suggest that thermochemical sulfate reduction occurred. Cl/Br and Na/Br ratios indicate that salinity was controlled by the mixing of meteoric water with evaporated seawater that had reached halite saturation, rather than by halite dissolution. The δ18O and δ2H values of the brines also suggest mixing between meteoric water and evaporated seawater that had reached gypsum and halite saturation. Geochemical modeling of seawater evaporation predicts a Cl-Na or Cl-Mg facies after halite saturation, contrasting with the observed Cl-Ca dominance of the Smackover Formation brines. The Ca-enriched brines may have evolved from Cl-Mg-dominated evaporated seawater through dolomitization of limestone. The 87Sr/86Sr ratios range from 0.70740 to 0.71048, higher than the average of Jurassic seawater (0.707). The non-linear relationship between 87Sr/86Sr and 1000/Sr suggests alteration of brine geochemistry by fluid mixing or by inputs from Sr and 87Sr-enriched rock sources. Lithium concentrations are positively correlated with 87Sr/86Sr ratios and TDS in brines enriched in these constituents. These correlations suggest deeper-seated geogenic sources and have implications for Li exploration in the northern Gulf Coast basin. Normal faults associated with the pre-Jurassic topography may have provided potential pathways for brine migration into the Smackover Formation under the influence of overpressure or thermohaline convection in the Gulf Coast.

title: Gibbs energy modeling of low-temperature bornite phases: Calculation of phase equilibria in the vicinity of Cu 5 FeS 4
description: Publication date: 5 December 2026 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 725 Author(s): Peter Waldner
abstract: Thermodynamic modeling of two low-temperature bornite phases with the stoichiometry Cu5FeS4 is performed at a total pressure of 1 bar. Two Gibbs energy expressions as a function of temperature are modeled, taking into account experimental data from the literature, such as heat capacities, enthalpy of transformation and Gibbs energies of formation, as well as phase equilibria data. Alongside recently reported thermodynamic models of neighboring phases, such as high-temperature bornite and chalcopyrite, it is now possible to perform phase equilibria computations around the composition Cu5FeS4 for the first time in the low-temperature regime of the Cu-Fe-S system. A topological analysis under consideration of binary CuS phase relations is conducted to investigate the consistency between predicted and experimental equilibria by calculating joins according to CuxS5 – Cu5FeS4 with x = 9.0, 9.2 and 9.3. Phase diagram analysis of the digenite-bornite join can now be supplemented from a thermodynamic point of view. A computed phase diagram section along the join Cu2S – CuFeS2 from ambient to liquidus temperatures provides a broader perspective on the phase relations around the composition Cu5FeS4.

title: Release and recapture: Limited carbon mobilization in sediment adjacent to Central Atlantic Magmatic Province sills, Florida, USA
description: Publication date: 5 December 2026 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 725 Author(s): Lindsi Allman, E.M. Stewart, Kanwa Sengupta, Mainak Mookherjee, Miles Kelsey, Paul Hackley, Ryan McAleer, Aaron M. Jubb, Rebecca Stokes
abstract: Large Igneous Provinces (LIPs) are associated with dramatic changes to the Earth system; their rapid release of carbon may initiate catastrophic climatic changes causing mass extinction. This carbon release is often associated with volcanic emissions, yet metamorphic carbon production is poorly constrained. Metamorphic carbon devolatilization occurs as intrusions interact with host sediment, potentially releasing substantial sedimentary carbon. While this process has been modeled, few studies use an observational approach. Here, we apply geochemical analysis, petrographic analysis, Raman spectroscopy, vitrinite reflectance, and thermodynamic modeling to understand carbon devolatilization in sediment adjacent to Central Atlantic Magmatic Province basaltic intrusions using two boreholes that penetrate the Florida basement. We find geochemical and petrographic evidence for CO2 release from carbonates below a 10 m thick sill, with upward fluid transport and recapture of mobilized CO2 at the top of the sill. Ultimately, we estimate 220 mols/m2 to 9900 mols/m2 of carbon were mobilized from sedimentary carbonate. Uncertainties in the extent of re‑carbonation suggest that anywhere from 0 mols/m2 to 7100 mols/m2 may have escaped to the surface. We find little evidence of organic carbon mobility, due partly to the increased activity of CO2 from carbonate devolatilization. Discrepancies between measured temperatures and 1D thermal models suggest complexities in heat transport through aqueous pore fluid flow and short (hundred to thousand year) heating timescales. These results highlight that further field-based study can help clarify the roles that heating timescales, fluid flow, sediment chemistry, and other factors play in releasing and capturing carbon during LIP emplacement.

title: Age and origin of the Bynoe Li-Cs-Ta Pegmatite Field, Northern Territory, Australia; a multi-isotopic dating approach
description: Publication date: 5 December 2026 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 725 Author(s): Samuel Chalmers, Carl Spandler, Jarred Lloyd
abstract: Through multi-mineral geochronology, this study investigates the age and evolution of Li-Cs-Ta (LCT) pegmatites in the Bynoe Pegmatite Field, Northern Territory, Australia. In situ, LA-ICP-MS based radiometric dating techniques utilised for pegmatite geochronology include U–Pb of zircon, apatite, cassiterite and columbite-group minerals, Lu–Hf of apatite, and Rb–Sr of muscovite. Additionally, migmatites of the Welltree Metamorphics, adjacent to the pegmatites, were dated by zircon U–Pb and apatite Lu–Hf to constrain the timing of anatexis within the region. Zircon U–Pb dating proved to be ineffective due to significant metamictisation of individual grains. Apatite Lu–Hf and cassiterite U–Pb give respective crystallisation ages for the pegmatites of ca 1750–1745 Ma and 1755–1740 Ma. Uranium–Pb dating of columbite-group minerals returned reversely discordance data of poor precision, though a broadly accurate age of 1754 ± 27 Ma (n = 18, MSWD = 3.3) was calculated. Apatite U–Pb ages of 1700–1670 Ma and muscovite Rb–Sr ages in the range of 1680–1620 Ma are interpreted as preserving either an extended cooling history or later-stage hydrothermal events. This research has conclusively shown that the timing of emplacement of LCT pegmatites within the Bynoe Pegmatite Field occurred at ca 1755–1740 Ma, demonstrating the successful application of numerous geochronometers to LCT pegmatite style Li deposits. We also show that the formation of these pegmatites post-dates the currently recognised extent of plutonism in the Pine Creek Orogen, challenging the theory that they formed by fractional crystallisation of a local granite. Instead, a previously unrecognised crustal melting event that was coeval with pegmatite formation gives credence to a possible anatectic origin for the pegmatites.

title: Decoupling of gallium and aluminum in bauxite deposits: Constraints from simulation experiments and Ga isotopes
description: Publication date: 5 December 2026 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 725 Author(s): Yuxu Zhang, Haifeng Fan, Kunyue Ling, Chuanwei Zhu, Hong Yang, Shengjiang Du, Hanjie Wen
abstract: Given the chemical and crystallochemical similarities between gallium (Ga) and aluminum (Al), Ga is typically enriched in Al-bearing minerals (e.g., aluminum hydroxides and clay minerals) via isomorphism, resulting in a strong Ga-Al correlation in Al-rich sedimentary rocks such as bauxite. Bauxite is generally enriched in Ga and serves as the primary industrial source, contributing ∼90% of global Ga production. However, some bauxites with substantial Ga enrichment exhibit notable Ga-Al decoupling, the mechanism of which remains unclear. Here, a comprehensive study was carried out on the Houcao bauxite deposit in Zunyi, Central Guizhou, SW China, which displays decoupled Ga and Al contents. Ga/Al ratios of samples from the H1 profile and the upper part of the H2 profile range from 2.30 × 10−4 to 2.93 × 10−4, broadly consistent with the range of potential source rocks (shales and carbonate rocks with ratios of 2.47–3.43 × 10−4). In contrast, samples from the lower part of the H2 profile show a gradual increase in Ga/Al ratios from 3.35 × 10−4 to 5.54 × 10−4, with the five lowermost, Ga-rich samples (Ga/Al = 4.35–5.54 × 10−4) exhibiting pronounced Ga-Al decoupling. These decoupled samples uniquely contain pyrite intergrown with illite, indicating an acidic depositional environment. Soaking experiments show that Al is more readily leached and mobilized than Ga at pH ∼6. Furthermore, the leachate is enriched in heavy Ga isotopes compared to the residues. A negative correlation between δ71Ga and Ga content in the two studied profiles suggests that isotopically heavy Ga was released during bauxite formation, leaving lighter Ga in the residual bauxites. We conclude that environmental pH is a key control on Ga-Al decoupling, with acidic conditions (pH < ∼5.5) favoring Ga enrichment and neutral to alkaline conditions promoting Ga depletion, providing a new framework for understanding Ga enrichment mechanisms in bauxite deposits.

title: Vanadium isotope fractionation in the bimodal volcanic rocks from the Hailar Basin, NE China
description: Publication date: 20 November 2026 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 724 Author(s): XiaoYu Lin, XiuHong Peng, JiaLong Liu, Xin Ding, Fang Huang
abstract: Vanadium (V) isotopes provide significant potential for tracing magmatic evolution processes, yet their fractionation in continental crustal magmas remains poorly constrained. This study reports V isotope compositions of bimodal volcanic rocks from the Hailar Basin (NE China) to investigate V isotope fractionation during mafic and felsic magma differentiation. The samples comprise relatively primitive mafic rocks (ca. 160 to 140 Ma) and highly evolved felsic rocks (ca. 136 to 124 Ma). In the Hailar suite, δ51V varies from −0.72‰ to +0.19‰, with generally higher values in the highly differentiated felsic rocks. δ51V also tends to increase with SiO2, but decrease with MgO, FeOT, TiO2, V (9.8 to 223.9 ppm), Sc, Ni, and Cr. Mafic rocks exhibit relatively limited δ51V variability (−0.72‰ to −0.48‰), consistent with generation by partial melting of a relatively oxidized mantle source and only minor modification during early-stage fractional crystallization. In contrast, the felsic rocks show a much wider δ51V range (−0.59‰ to +0.19‰), with generally heavier values in relatively evolved compositions, consistent with late-stage fractionation involving Fe-Ti oxides and biotite. The evolved felsic rocks exhibit elevated δ51V, δ56Fe, and δ49Ti relative to the mafic rocks, indicating that crystallization involving Fe-Ti oxides played an important role in driving isotope fractionation during felsic magma evolution. Collectively, these results highlight the importance of mineral-controlled differentiation in interpreting V isotope variations in evolved continental crustal magmas.

title: Dual sea-level and climatic forcing of detrital Hf-Nd isotope decoupling during marginal-sea sediment transfer: Insights from the Japan Sea
description: Publication date: 20 November 2026 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 724 Author(s): Ruxi Dou, Jianjun Zou, Aimei Zhu, Baohua Han, Xinru Xue, Haonan Zhu, Xuguang Feng, Junyao Li, Yanguang Liu, Xuefa Shi
abstract: Hafnium (Hf)–neodymium (Nd) decoupling is well documented in global sedimentary systems, yet the processes governing its evolution during source-to-sink sediment transfer in marginal seas remain poorly constrained. Here, we combine high-resolution Pb-Hf isotope and elemental data from the <63 μm detrital fraction of sediment core KCES1 in the southwestern Japan Sea with published Nd isotope and grain-size records to investigate the mechanisms controlling Hf-Nd decoupling over the past ∼30 ka BP. Coupled Pb-Nd isotope systematics demonstrate a persistent first-order East Asian continental affinity, despite minor temporal changes in sediment routing and source contributions. In contrast, εNd values vary by only ∼1.5 ε units, whereas εHf values span ∼8 ε units, indicating that Hf isotope variability was dominated by post-source fractionation rather than provenance change. During the glacial–deglacial interval (30–14 ka BP), strong covariations among ΔεHf Terr. (defined as the vertical offset from the Terrestrial Array at a given εNd value), Nb/Zr, and sortable-silt mean grain size indicate that zircon-controlled hydrodynamic sorting exerted the primary control on Hf isotope compositions. Zircon enrichment peaked during 18–14 ka BP, when rapid sea-level rise likely remobilized zircon-bearing sediments stored on the exposed East China Sea shelf during the preceding glacial lowstand. After 14 ka BP, the sortable-silt–ΔεHf Terr. relationship weakened, whereas higher CIA, ΔεHf Terr. values and Nb/Zr ratios indicate increased delivery of zircon-depleted, weathering-derived silt-size sediments under intensified postglacial monsoon runoff and continued sea-level rise. These results demonstrate that sea-level and climate changes drove a transition in the dominant mechanism of Hf-Nd decoupling, from hydrodynamic sorting during cold lowstands to chemical weathering during warm highstands. Our study highlights marginal seas as dynamic filters that substantially modify continental Hf isotope signatures during source-to-sink sediment transfer.

title: Tourmaline as a geochemical indicator of tin mineralization in the Baiyinchagan deposit, northeastern China
description: Publication date: 20 November 2026 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 724 Author(s): Zhenhua Zhou, Xinkai Chen, Rolf L. Romer, Xin Chen, Chenming Zhang, Jiaqi Zhao, Jingwen Mao
abstract: The partitioning of ore elements during late-stage, fluid-melt phase separation and fluid-rock interaction largely controls the mobilization and precipitation of ore elements and, thus, whether a deposit may form. We use the texture and chemical composition of tourmaline to trace fluid evolution during formation of the giant, cassiterite-bearing hydrothermal vein system of the Baiyinchagan Sn-polymetallic deposit (0.35 Mt. Sn, 9.4 kt Ag) hosted by an Early Cretaceous tourmaline leucogranite and Permian metasedimentary rocks. There are three generations of Fe-rich, alkali group tourmaline: late-magmatic, granite-related (Tur 1); pre-ore, vein- or breccia-associated (Tur 2); and syn-ore, vein-related (Tur 3). Tin contents increase systematically from Tur 1 (avg 305 ppm) to Tur 3 (avg 1114 ppm), tracking Sn enrichment that eventually led to cassiterite precipitation. Decreasing Li, Zn, Nb, and Ta contents, increasing Sr, Co, V, Cr, and HREE contents, progressively lower (Eu/Eu⁎)CN values and V/Sc ratios from Tur 1 to Tur 3 together with δ11B values ranging from −12.56‰ to −7.29‰, collectively indicate fluid exsolution from a granitic source and extensive interaction of this fluid with country rocks. The higher Sr, Cr, Co, V, and Sn contents in syn-ore Tur 3 reflect acid-consuming, feldspar-biotite dissolution in the wall rocks, implying that reaction-induced changes of the fluid composition triggered ore deposition. The V/Sc ratio of tourmaline seems to be a particularly reliable indicator for tin enrichment, as this ratio is high also in other sediment-hosted Sn deposits, reflecting fluid-rock interaction that eventually leads to Sn precipitation.

title: Ca isotope evidence for melting of deeply subducted carbonated sediments: insights into REE cycling beneath cratonic margins
description: Publication date: 20 November 2026 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 724 Author(s): Yang Yu, Xianlei Geng, Shihong Tian, Lu Chen, Wei Xu, Zhengwei Liang, Wenjie Hu
abstract: Carbonatites and associated alkaline silicate rocks provide key insights into deep carbon cycling and the formation of rare-earth-element (REE) deposits. However, whether and how recycled carbonate-rich crustal materials contribute to their mantle source, and the role of this process in forming giant REE deposits, remain debated and poorly understood. Here we present high-precision Ca isotope data for the genetically associated lamprophyres, syenites and carbonatites from the Cenozoic Mianning-Dechang belt (southwestern Yangtze Craton), a post-collisional setting hosting giant to large REE deposits. Except for five samples with anomalously high δ44/40Ca (up to 1.09‰), the Ca isotopes of these samples were not significantly affected by radioactive decay of 40K, low-temperature alteration, and crustal assimilation. The remaining lamprophyres, syenites and carbonatites exhibit systematically lower δ44/40Ca values of 0.42‰ –77 ‰ (N = 33) relative to the bulk silicate Earth (0.94 ± 0.10 ‰, 2SD) and mid-ocean ridge basalts (0.85 ± 0.09 ‰, 2SD). Such light Ca isotope composition can be taken as the pristine signature of the primary melts, as no significant Ca isotope fractionation occurred during magmatic differentiation (including fractional crystallization and carbonate-silicate liquid immiscibility) of these rocks. The light Ca isotope signature cannot be explained simply by fractionation during mantle melting, but requires a mantle source with lower δ44/40Ca (0.70 ± 0.20‰, 2SD). Combined with trace element and Sr-Nd-Pb-Li isotope signatures of these samples, our Ca isotope data provide key natural evidence for melting of subducted carbonated sediments at high pressures (>4 GPa) during slab subduction. This process can efficiently transport carbon and REEs from subducted sediments into the overlying subcontinental lithospheric mantle and promote the formation of giant post-collisional carbonatite-associated REE deposits at cratonic margins.

title: Trace element heterogeneity and crystallization history of the Plešovice zircon: Implications for its use as a U Pb LA-ICP-MS reference material
description: Publication date: 20 November 2026 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 724 Author(s): Jana Kotková, Urs Schaltegger, Alexey Ulianov, Sean P. Gaynor, Daniel B. Parvaz, Jiří Sláma
abstract: Zircon crystals from Plešovice hyperpotassic granulite (HPG) have been widely used as a reference material for LA-ICP-MS dating. Detailed cathodoluminescence (CL) imaging and trace element analysis reveal a complex internal structure of Plešovice zircon linked to extreme chemical heterogeneity, which allows us to distinguish different zircon domains formed during its crystallization: (i) rare low-CL cores enriched in U, Nb, HREE and Y; (ii) dominant sector-zoned to oscillatory-zoned domains, and (iii) CL-bright rims poor in trace elements. Relic fine oscillatory zoned areas are chemically homogeneous, whereas coarsened and blurred areas, and CL-dark replacement domains, are heterogeneous. Based on these data we suggest a complex and protracted zircon evolution: (i) crystallization of metamorphic zircon in anatectic calc-alkaline granulite; (ii) magmatic zircon crystallization at high temperature and pressure in a dry ultrapotassic melt at presence of peritectic garnet; (iii) coupled zircon dissolution-precipitation processes triggered by percolating hydrous residual melt; and (iv) coarsening and replacement of the pre-existing zircon due to prolonged exposure to a reactive fluid/hydrous melt. New CA-ID-TIMS UPb dates between 337.167 ± 0.080 and 337.840 ± 0.080 Ma confirm crystallization age for HPG zircon at around 337.4 Ma and suggest that previously published dates of 336.37 Ma were biased by non-mitigated lead loss. We thus confirm the U/Pb homogeneity of Plešovice reference zircon despite its chemical heterogeneity. We further discuss the implications of using the chemically extremely heterogeneous Plešovice reference zircon as primary or secondary standard for in-situ LA-ICP-MS geochronology, in particular for quantification of the chemical matrix-dependence of the relative sensitivity factor (β) of laser ablation.

title: Tracing thermal structure and fluid evolution of the Mariana forearc subduction channel and mantle wedge using in situ serpentine δ 18 O
description: Publication date: 20 November 2026 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 724 Author(s): Palash Kumawat, Maria Rosa Scicchitano, Thomas Frederichs, Walter Menapace, Charles Geoffrey Wheat, Elmar Albers, Wolfgang Bach
abstract: Serpentinization in the Mariana forearc controls redox conditions, volatile production, and the energy landscape for subsurface ecosystems, yet the temperatures remain poorly defined. We present in situ oxygen isotope (δ18O, VSMOW) measurements of serpentine from three serpentinite mud volcanoes across the forearc: South Chamorro, Pacman, and the newly discovered trench-proximal Haga’ I Tasi. Combined with published bulk and pore fluid δ18O datasets, we identify systematic changes across the forearc, with δ18O of serpentine and pore fluid mutually increasing, while the difference in δ18O between serpentine and pore fluid decreases, with greater distance from the trench. To reconcile the existing low- and high-temperature oxygen isotope fractionation calibrations, we introduce a hybrid serpentine–fluid geothermometer (K26) valid from 25 to 450 °C. Applied to the Mariana forearc, K26 resolves a coherent mantle wedge thermal gradient from cold, trench-proximal to progressively hotter, deeper-slab conditions, and provides first-order constraints on deep formation-fluid δ18O, which are systematically heavier than summit pore fluids while preserving the monotonic forearc trend as observed in δ18O composition of pore fluids. These results provide quantitative bounds on the thermal structure and fluid evolution of a shallow subduction channel, with implications for redox budgets and carbon cycling in forearc settings.

title: Controls on Zn isotope variations in serpentinized abyssal peridotites: The important role of spinel alteration
description: Publication date: 20 November 2026 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 724 Author(s): Jia-Wei Xiong, Chuan-Zhou Liu, Yin-Zheng Lin
abstract: Zinc isotopes are increasingly used to trace deep material cycling. However, their reliable application requires better constraints on the Zn isotope composition of altered oceanic lithosphere. Published δ66Zn values for serpentinized abyssal peridotites range from the mantle value (∼0.18‰) to distinctly heavier compositions (up to ∼0.62‰), yet the controlling processes remain debated. Here we investigate a comprehensive suite of relatively fresh, strongly serpentinized and carbonate-bearing abyssal peridotites from the ultraslow-spreading Gakkel Ridge. By integrating bulk-rock geochemistry, sequential leaching and petrographic observations, we assess the respective contributions of magmatic inheritance and multistage seafloor alteration. We find that fresh peridotites retain BSE-like δ66Zn, consistent with the preservation of primary magmatic signatures. In carbonate-bearing serpentinites, neither Zn contents nor δ66Zn values correlate with carbonation indices. Sequential leaching steps operationally designed to extract Zn from carbonates and secondary hydroxides released minor Zn fractions, averaging 17.3% and 18.4%, respectively. The residues have δ66Zn similar to or slightly lower than those of the corresponding bulk rocks. These results suggest that carbonates and secondary hydroxides may host an isotopically heavy but subordinate Zn pool that is unlikely to dominate the whole-rock Zn budget. In contrast, elevated δ66Zn values are associated with more extensive replacement of primary spinel by ferritchromite and magnetite. Petrographic observations and in situ geochemical mappings support this replacement sequence and record Zn redistribution during spinel alteration. Rayleigh-type endmember calculations indicate that the loss of isotopically light Zn into Cl-bearing fluids during spinel replacement can generate isotope shifts comparable in magnitude to the observed increase in δ66Zn. Together, these observations identify spinel alteration as an important mineral-scale control on Zn isotope fractionation, although quantitatively separating its contribution from that of silicate serpentinization will require future phase-specific studies. More broadly, seafloor alteration can impart heavy Zn isotope signatures to the oceanic mantle, and this pre-subduction heterogeneity should be considered when evaluating Zn isotope anomalies in mantle-derived magmas.

title: High-spatial-resolution 207 Pb/ 206 Pb age mapping of zircon domains by VUV-TOF-MS: Paleoarchean metamorphic overprints of the > 4.0 Ga Idiwhaa unit in the Acasta Gneiss Complex
description: Publication date: 20 November 2026 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 724 Author(s): Yixuan Li, Haoyu Shi, Peng Wang, Da Wang, Yuxiang Mo
abstract: Zircons preserve micron-scale records of magmatic and metamorphic processes, but their geochronology is often limited by the spatial resolution and low statistics of conventional spot techniques (SIMS, LA-ICP-MS), which may not accurately date thin (<10 μm) overgrowths. Here, we apply high-speed, high-spatial-resolution VUV-TOF-MS to conduct high-statistics domain analysis of 16 zircons from the oldest igneous unit on Earth, the Idiwhaa unit of the Acasta Gneiss Complex (AGC). This approach generates comprehensive 207Pb/206Pb age maps by acquiring ∼1000 individual analyses per grain at a rate of 3 s per analysis and < 2 μm spatial resolution. The resulting datasets for individual age domains enable robust determination of 207Pb/206Pb ratios, yielding precisions of 0.2–1% (2σ) and revealing discrete age domains as thin as ∼5 μm that are difficult to date with traditional in-situ methods. The mapped Acasta zircon grains show clear core-rim structures with cores and rims dated at 4.0–3.9 Ga and 3.3 Ga, indicating primary magmatic crystallization and metamorphic overprint, respectively. The 3.3 Ga metamorphic event is consistent with the complex-wide SmNd resetting event indicated by the whole-rock SmNd isotopes, which indicates that the oldest unit in the Acasta Gneiss Complex was affected by the regional metamorphism. Additionally, the age mapping results of several whole zircon grains in the Idiwhaa unit lack dates between 3.7 and 3.5 Ga. This observation suggests that the oldest magmatic rocks in Acasta were likely unaffected by the magmatic events between 3.7 Ga and 3.5 Ga. In summary, this study demonstrates the potential of VUV-TOF-MS as a new tool in geochronology, particularly for micrometer-scale age mapping of complex, ancient zircons. Beyond the Acasta Gneiss Complex, this approach offers a general solution for resolving fine-scale PbPb age domains in zircon grains to isolate thin (<10 μm) overgrowths or altered zones.

title: Isotopically heavy barium discharge from an arc hydrothermal system: Potential sources and processes
description: Publication date: 20 November 2026 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 724 Author(s): Xue-Gang Chen, Jia-Yi Wu, Yuping Guo, Zhouling Zhang, Martin Frank, Chen-Tung Arthur Chen
abstract: Barium (Ba) and its isotopes are important biogeochemical tracers in the ocean. However, the marine Ba budget is underexplored and the sources and behavior of Ba in hydrothermal systems at subduction zones (SZ) are essentially unknown. Here, we collected vent fluid and related seawater samples for Ba and stable Ba isotope measurements (expressed in the δ138Ba notation) from the Lutao hydrothermal field at the North Luzon arc, typical of SZ hydrothermal settings. Measured δ138Ba values fall in a range of 0.35–0.51 ‰. Barium and Ba isotopes were mainly controlled by subcritical phase separation in the reaction zone, with the brine phase (δ138Ba = 0.44 ± 0.03 ‰) having significantly higher δ138Ba values than the vapor phase (0.35 ± 0.04 ‰). The primitive vent fluid before phase separation is characterized by a δ138Ba of 0.43 ± 0.06 ‰. The isotopically heavy Ba in the Lutao vent fluids cannot be fully explained by host rock leaching, but plausibly additionally sourced from subduction fluids. The elevated δ138Ba values were probably triggered by barite dissolution from the subducting slab and subsequent secondary barite precipitation before phase separation. Our results highlight the importance of SZ hydrothermal systems in the recycling of subduction materials back to Earth's surface. Furthermore, the isotopically heavy Ba discharge from SZ vent fluids indicates that we are still missing isotopically lighter Ba sources to balance the marine Ba isotope budget.

title: The late shoulder season modifies the mobility of iron and dissolved organic carbon in rivers from distinct permafrost regions
description: Publication date: 20 November 2026 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 724 Author(s): Maëlle Villani, Catherine Hirst, Eléonore du Bois d'Aische, Cécile Osy, Maxime Thomas, Philippe Roux, Erik Lundin, Justin Ledman, Edward A.G. Schuur, Sophie Opfergelt
abstract: Rivers are important suppliers of iron (Fe) and dissolved organic carbon (DOC) from land to sea. While elemental transport in Arctic rivers has been studied mainly during summer, their mobility during the late shoulder season (i.e., the transition between the end of summer and the beginning of winter) remains poorly constrained. Here, we investigate how Fe and DOC mobility evolve during the late shoulder season in two rivers from distinct permafrost regions and hydrological conditions (in Alaska, USA and Abisko, Sweden). Iron and DOC were characterized using their concentrations, percentage of colloidal Fe, and indirect Fe-oxides tracers (Ce anomaly and δ30Si). We show two contrasting processes: (i) in Alaska, progressive river ice formation coincides with a shift toward groundwater-dominated river input, suggesting aggregation of Fe as particles (>0.22 μm), evidenced by a decrease in Fe concentrations in the filtered water (<0.22 μm) over the late shoulder season; the concurrent higher negative Ce anomaly, and the decrease in DOC concentrations, further suggest the aggregation of particulate Fe-oxides associated with DOC; (ii) in Abisko, warmer and near-stagnant river conditions sustain soil pore water-river connectivity over the late shoulder season, enabling lateral transfer of Fe, evidenced by increase Fe concentrations; the increase in the percentage of colloidal Fe, the lower negative Ce anomaly, the slight decrease in δ30Si, and the increase in DOC concentrations, further suggest an increase in colloidal Fe-oxides associated with DOC (1 nm- 0.22 μm) in the river. These contrasting Fe size ranges have direct implications for Arctic DOC export.

title: Periodic SiO 2 mineralization dated by LA–ICP–MS and ID–TIMS, an example from Golobradovo agate, Rhodopes, Bulgaria
description: Publication date: 20 November 2026 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 724 Author(s): Armin Zeh, Jens Götze, Marion Tichomirowa, Alexandra Käßner, Maximilian Mrozik
abstract: Agates from Oligocene acidic volcanic rocks in the Eastern Rhodopes (Bulgaria) were investigated by combined mineralogical and radiometric methods. Petrographic–CL-spectroscopic observations reveal distinct SiO2-rich zones made up by cristobalite, celadonite, zeolite, opal-CT, chalcedony, and quartzine with U contents up to 67 μg/g.
