The SWAT-PP model was applied and tested in the Dongwan Polder (DWP) within China’s Chaohu Lake Basin. Results showed that SWAT‑PP effectively simulated field‑scale hydrology and nutrient dynamics (R2 > 0.6, NSE > 0.5, PBIAS 0.5, NSE > 0.4, PBIAS < 15%). Water balance analysis indicated that irrigation contributed nearly 30% of total inflow, with about 17% of diverted water returning to ditches as tailwater. Nutrient source apportionment revealed that external river diversion and sediment resuspension each accounted for roughly 10% of total TN/TP loads, while ponds retained approximately 80%–90% of nutrients from residential runoff. SWAT-PP provides a promising tool for simulating coupled hydrological and water quality processes in polder systems, supporting improved water management and NPS pollution control in these vulnerable agro-hydrological settings.

title: Leveraging deep learning and kernel density representations for transformation-based regional flood frequency analysis
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 680, Part A Author(s): Sukhsehaj Kaur, Sagar Rohidas Chavan
abstract: This paper leverages deep learning (DL) and kernel density representations to determine design flood estimates at ungauged or sparsely gauged sites through transformation-based regional flood frequency analysis (T_RFFA) approach. A critical preliminary step in conventional RFFA approaches is to identify an appropriate regional frequency distribution through an effective regional goodness-of-fit (GOF) test. However, conventional regional GOF tests involve sample mean–based normalization of at-site peak flow data, which can violate key assumptions of RFFA. To address this, the proposed method reformulates regional GOF test as a classification problem wherein peak flow data from each site are transformed into a dimensionless space using mathematical transformations. Kernel density estimator (KDE) plots are then generated and used as inputs to a pre-trained Deep Neural Network (DNN) classifier that selects the most suitable regional distribution among the five widely recognized peak flow distributions, viz., Generalized Extreme Value, Generalized Pareto, Generalized Logistic, Generalized Normal, and Pearson Type 3 distributions. The DNN classifier achieved classification accuracies of 95.09% and 94.86% on training and test datasets, respectively. The effectiveness of the proposed DL-based RFFA approach is evaluated through Monte Carlo simulation experiments and real-world applications to catchments in the United States and peninsular India. Results demonstrate that the proposed approach yields comparable or better design flood estimates relative to conventional T_RFFA approach. Furthermore, the proposed DL-based GOF test is observed to be approximately 18 to 27 times faster than the conventional L-moment-based approach, offering a computationally efficient and robust alternative for RFFA.

title: Multi-scale mapping of GDEs from remote sensing and field surveys in the Urumqi River–Chaiwopu Basin
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 680, Part A Author(s): Ye Zhihao, Zhou Qiang, Zheng Mingxia, Zhang Peng, Sun Hao, Zhang Xiaoyu, Zhou Xin, He Liansheng, Huang Longhao, Meng Rui
abstract: Groundwater-Dependent Ecosystems (GDEs) are widely distributed in arid and semi-arid regions and provide critical ecological services. However, their precise identification and mapping remain challenging due to insufficient integration of geospatial technologies with field measurement techniques. This study selected the terminal year of a prolonged drought and the most recent year for analysis, covering the period 2001–2023. We employed key indicators including Fractional Vegetation Cover (FVC), the difference between evapotranspiration and precipitation (ET-P), the Terrain Wetness Index (TWI), and the Vegetation Groundwater Accessibility Index (VGUI). The K-means clustering algorithm was applied for classification, and spatial overlay analysis was conducted in the Urumqi River–Chaiwopu Basin in Xinjiang, China, to assess the spatial distribution and temporal variations of GDEs. The results were validated by integrating wetland distribution data with field investigations. The findings indicate that areas classified as “likely” or “very likely” GDEs are predominantly concentrated around Dongdao Haizi, Chaiwopu Lake, the salt lakes, and adjacent regions, covering 45.4% of the potential area (4,197.89 km2). Wetland-based validation yielded a producer’s accuracy of 84.1%. Over time, the area classified as “unlikely” or “very unlikely” for GDEs showed an increasing trend. After incorporating VGUI, the likelihood class decreased across 41.0% of the typical areas, with cultivated and built-up land accounting for 64.9% of this decrease. By incorporating field-based VGUI data, the study reduced interference from anthropogenic factors such as irrigation in the identification of GDEs within typical areas, enabling refined mapping.

title: Controls on carbon and nutrient transport in a tidal creek across a coastal forest-marsh transition under sea-level rise
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 680, Part A Author(s): Nathaniel Spicer, Brian Moyer, Dannielle Pratt, Holly A. Michael, Ashleigh R. Montgomery, Angelia L. Seyfferth, Katherine Tully
abstract: Sea level rise (SLR) and saltwater intrusion (SWI) drive ecological and biogeochemical changes in coastal forests that alter solute fluxes between marshes and estuaries. Tidal creeks mediate transport of carbon (C), iron (Fe), and nitrogen (N) during flood and ebb tides, yet quantifying elemental fluxes is challenging due to bidirectional tidal flow and frequent bank overtopping. We quantified surface-water transport of C, Fe, and N during spring tides and storm events (2022–2023) in a tidal creek draining a transitioning coastal forest along the Delaware Bay. Discharge was estimated using a novel rating-curve model that incorporates bank overtopping dynamics. Groundwater wells and redox probes along a marsh-to-forest transect monitored water table elevation, salinity, and redox potential. We observed net imports of dissolved organic carbon (DOC), dissolved organic nitrogen (DON), dissolved Fe, and ammonium (NH4-N). DOC hourly loads were positively correlated with dissolved Fe loads, suggesting microbial dissolution of C-bearing Fe oxides during flood tides, and re-precipitation and C retention on ebb tides. Plant uptake and nitrification drove NH4-N and DON imports, as plant uptake during high tide could remove N from the water column. There was no import or export of nitrate (NO3-N), but NO3-N hourly loads were positively correlated with marsh redox potential, consistent with denitrification under reduced conditions. As the coastal zone responds to accelerating SLR, dissolution of Fe protected C will inhibit C sequestration and marsh loss to SLR could increase N delivery to coastal waters as plants uptake less N, with downstream implications for eutrophication.

title: Dual urban runoff response to urbanization and contradictory precipitation trends driven by climate change
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 680, Part A Author(s): Raz Nussbaum, Moshe Armon, Efrat Morin
abstract: Urban flooding poses a growing threat to cities worldwide, driven by the compounding effects of climate change and urbanization. This study examines the effect of urbanization and contradictory precipitation trends, defined as increasing storm intensity and decreasing total precipitation, on urban runoff. Analyzing CMIP6 projections, we show that contradictory precipitation is projected to impact 26% of urban areas globally. To examine how these trends manifest at finer scales, we analyze changes in heavy precipitation events at both regional and catchment scales using convection-permitting WRF simulations. Their hydrological implications are then assessed using a calibrated SWMM urban runoff model driven by an ensemble of over 5,300 spatially shifted simulations. We find that future storms become more spatially confined while their short-duration maximal intensities increase at both regional and catchment scales. Consequently, from a catchment-scale hydrological perspective, weak runoff peaks become weaker, while strong peaks become stronger, a pattern that is amplified by urbanization. Furthermore, peak runoff is increasingly governed by short-duration rainfall intensities under future conditions, an effect amplified by urbanization. Additionally, we suggest a mechanism whereby more compact future storms suppress runoff when they miss the catchment, yet amplify peaks when they overlap with it. Concurrently, drier antecedent conditions suppress runoff from weak events while intense bursts rapidly exceed infiltration and storage capacities. This contrasting urban hydrological response to climate change poses a critical challenge for urban flood management.

title: Spatial heterogeneity and drivers of PFASs distribution in an arid-semiarid city waters system
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 680, Part A Author(s): Xuemei Zhu, Wenjing Sun, Ying Sun, Xiaotao Fu, Bing Sun, Yihan Li, Changwei Lü, Shenghu Zhang, Xin Wang, Chengmei Liao
abstract: Investigating the occurrence of emerging per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFASs) in diverse urban surface water bodies of Hohhot, a representative arid and semi-arid city, is essential for understanding their environmental behavior and potential ecological risks under water-scarce conditions. This study systematically characterized the occurrence, spatial distribution, compositional profiles, and environmental factors associated with the spatial heterogeneity of PFASs. The concentrations of ΣPFASs exhibited pronounced spatial heterogeneity (6.3–81.4 ng/L), with elevated levels observed in water bodies more strongly influenced by anthropogenic activities. PFASs compositional profiles differed among water body types, with short-chain PFASs constituting a substantial proportion of the overall PFASs composition. Long-chain PFASs nevertheless remained widely detectable across the studied waters. PFASs covaried with multiple hydrochemical characteristics, but these associations weakened after accounting for functional water-body type, highlighting water-body differentiation as an important context for PFASs spatial heterogeneity. Despite the higher concentrations of short-chain PFASs in several water bodies, ecological risk was primarily associated with residual long-chain PFASs, particularly perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA) and perfluorooctanesulfonic acid (PFOS). Collectively, these findings highlight the need for source-oriented monitoring and region-specific PFASs management in arid–semi-arid urban watersheds, while the potential influence of hydroclimatic conditions requires quantitative hydrological validation.

title: Understanding hydrological drought recovery patterns in a changing environment: Insights from a non-stationary multivariate analysis
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 680, Part A Author(s): Yeting Chen, Tao Peng, Vijay P. Singh, Ji Liu, Xiaohua Dong, Qingxia Lin, Jiali Guo, Chao Song, Changwen Li, Yinghai Li, Dan Yu, Chong Wei, Yan Huang
abstract: Understanding hydrological drought recovery under non‑stationary conditions is critical for water management in a changing environment, yet remains poorly quantified. This study presented a novel grid‑based, daily‑scale framework that integrated non‑stationary drought identification, multivariate probabilistic recovery assessment, and machine learning driver analysis. Applied to the four sub‑basins of the Dongting Lake basin (DLB), a non‑stationary Standardized Runoff Index (NSRI) was constructed using the GAMLSS framework with large‑scale climate indices as covariates. Drought recovery characteristics, including recovery time, water requirement (WR), and recovery probability, were estimated using run theory and a copula‑Bayesian approach, with random forest (RF) used to rank the influencing factors. Results showed that NSRI captured drought onset and peak more sensitively than the stationary SRI. The average recovery time ranged from 83.5 days in the Zi River (ZR) to 97.3 days in the Li River (LR), revealing notable spatial heterogeneity across the basin. WR increased sharply under severe and extreme drought conditions, while recovery probability dropped below 0.61 for extreme drought. Human activities, particularly water use and population density, dominated drought recovery in three sub‑basins, whereas climate and vegetation factors controlled recovery in the fourth. This framework enhances the accuracy and spatial resolution of drought recovery assessments and provides quantitative support for adaptive water management under a changing environment.

title: Strategies for correcting nonstationary resistivity–water content relations in time-lapse electrical resistivity tomography
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 680, Part A Author(s): Jianguo Liu, Simone Gelsinari, Andrew van de Ven, Matthias Leopold, Sally Thompson
abstract: Time-lapse Electrical Resistivity Tomography (ERT) provides an attractive framework for quantifying spatially distributed water-content dynamics, yet quantitative interpretation remains limited by uncertainty in the petrophysical relationship between resistivity ( ρ ) and volumetric water content ( θ ). This uncertainty is distinct from that associated with lithological heterogeneity, measurement resolution, or inversion artefacts, and can arise from temporal variability in the ρ – θ relationship itself. We examine two approaches for representing this nonstationary behaviour: a particle-filter data-assimilation framework that requires continuous or periodic co-located water-content observations from an independent sensor system to dynamically calibrate time-varying petrophysical parameters, and a machine-learning model that predicts θ from resistivity-based predictors together with auxiliary environmental information, including surface water content and contact resistance, after training. Synthetic experiments indicate that the imposed time-varying petrophysical scaling coefficient, a ( t ) , and saturation exponent, b ( t ) , can be recovered with low trajectory error across the tested ranges of parameter amplitudes, frequencies, and resistivity-noise levels. Applications at two sandy vadose-zone sites in Western Australia show that data-assimilation-based dynamic calibration of the petrophysical relationship substantially improves consistency between ERT-derived water-content reconstructions and the co-located water-content observations assimilated by the particle filter. The particle-filter reconstructions should therefore be interpreted as assimilation-constrained dynamic reconstructions that evaluate the benefit of updating the ρ – θ relationship through time relative to a stationary petrophysical calibration. The data assimilation framework provides a direct depiction of how the relationship evolves through time, capturing gradual seasonal shifts as well as extended periods of relative stability. Machine learning offers a practical alternative when sufficient and representative data are available. The observed variability in the effective petrophysical relationship covaried with near-surface environmental and electrode-contact conditions, as indicated in part by contact-resistance diagnostics. We interpret these associations as empirical and installation-specific, rather than as evidence that contact resistance is an intrinsic soil property or an independent causal control. Accounting for temporal variability in the petrophysical relationship improves the interpretability and reliability of quantitative time-lapse ERT analyses.

title: A digital twin framework for real-time probabilistic forecasting of permeable pavement performance
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 680, Part A Author(s): Jose Brasil, Marcus Nóbrega Gomes Jr., Drew W. Johnson, Athanassios T. Papagiannakis, Eduardo Mario Mendiondo, Marcio Hofheinz Giacomoni
abstract: Low Impact Development (LID), such as permeable pavements, mitigates some of the urban runoff effects. Their hydrologic response can be enhanced with real-time forecasting and management. Digital Twins (DT), which integrate physical models with sensor data, offer a solution, yet require methods to handle uncertainties in model inputs and observations. This study presents a DT framework for permeable pavement systems that couples a one-dimensional, explicit-state hydrologic model with a Particle Filter (PF) data assimilation scheme. The framework assimilates real-time underdrain outflow observations to refine model states and provide probabilistic forecasts. Uncertainty characterization revealed that sensor measurement error depends on the underdrain outflow, while rainfall forecast error from the High-Resolution Rapid Refresh model is a function of the magnitude of the rainfall event. The DT framework was evaluated against a baseline model using field data from four permeable pavement types. The data assimilation approach reduced the ensemble forecast error by an average of 20%, as measured by the Continuous Ranked Probability Skill Score (CRPSS), with positive skill scores in 96.2% of forecast events. The deterministic performance of the PF ensemble median, evaluated by Nash-Sutcliffe Efficiency (NSE) and Root Mean Square Error (RMSE), also exceeded that of the baseline model. The data assimilation framework yielded more accurate forecasts than a deterministic modeling approach and is computationally efficient for operational deployment. However, outflow forecast accuracy is constrained by the structural limitations of the baseline model, evidenced by poor prediction interval coverage during some high-intensity events, highlighting areas for future model development.

title: Improving and evaluating the performance of change detection methods for soil moisture retrieval using Sentinel-1A over a forest-dominated mountainous study area in Beijing, China
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 680, Part A Author(s): Haotian Cai, Nan Ye, Rui Tong, Fuqiang Tian, Jingan Lin, Yao Zhuang
abstract: Surface Soil Moisture (SSM) plays a crucial role in the development of natural disasters over mountainous areas, particularly in triggering flash floods caused by precipitation following antecedent rainfall. Numerous spaceborne SSM products can be used in flood models for forecasting and early warning of flash flood events. In recent decades, passive microwave remote sensing has been widely acknowledged as the most accurate technique for global SSM mapping. However, its spatial resolutions are limited to the order of 10 km from space. While Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) and optical sensors onboard satellites can enhance the spatial resolution of passive microwave SSM data or directly retrieve high-resolution SSM, the accuracy of SSM products is adversely affected by ground geometry and vegetation coverage over mountainous areas. In this study, the Advanced Change Detection method for Mountainous areas (ACD_M) was developed as an attempt to adapt the ACD framework for high-resolution SSM retrieval over forest-dominated mountainous areas using multi-temporal repeat orbit Sentinel-1A SAR data. ACD_M incorporates two key adaptations into the ACD framework. First, the Helsinki University of Technology (HUT) forest backscattering model was introduced to consider volume scattering in the ACD_M. Second, the SMAP passive microwave 9-km SSM product was downscaled, and pixel-wise SSM constraints were derived from local spatial variability to account for mountainous heterogeneity. The ACD_M was evaluated over a forest-dominated mountainous study area in northern Beijing, China. SSM with a spatial resolution of 25 m was retrieved from Sentinel-1A L1 radar backscatter data and subsequently validated using time series of ground SSM measurements from a monitoring station network for the period from January 2020 to May 2024. The ACD_M was also inter-compared with the existing short-term change detection methods, demonstrating superior overall retrieval accuracy. Compared to ACD, the ACD_M demonstrated higher and more stable retrieval accuracy, with an increase of 0.011 in R and a reduction of 0.022 cm3/cm3 in Bias. Furthermore, the potential for further enhancing the retrieval accuracy of the ACD_M by optimizing model constraints was explored. For instance, the mean R increased by 0.018 and the RMSE decreased by 0.008 cm3/cm3 after introducing a statistical relationship between geographical factors and SSM in the upper constraints. ACD_M showed limitations under high SSM conditions, indicating that caution is required when applying the retrieved SSM to near-saturated or flash-flood-related hydrological conditions.

title: A graph-based surrogate modeling framework for large-scale spatial optimization of low-impact development layouts in urban pluvial flood mitigation
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 680, Part A Author(s): Qiming Cheng, Jiayue Zhu, Ye Rao, Zhen Liu, Fei Liu, Yixin Mu, Kaifeng Wang, Yao Chen
abstract: The increasing frequency of extreme weather events, coupled with anthropogenic modifications to urban land surfaces, has significantly exacerbated urban flooding. Low-impact development (LID) strategies have therefore been widely advocated as a primary approach for mitigating urban pluvial flood, the effectiveness of which highly dependents on the spatial layout of LID facilities and their construction costs. However, this multi-objective optimization approach faces formidable challenges. Existing approaches to LID spatial allocation optimization often fail to effectively balance cost-benefit heterogeneity across diverse configurations and become computationally intractable when applied to urban drainage systems characterized by numerous sub-catchments, complex hydraulic network topologies, or both. To address these challenges, we propose the GraphicSWMM framework, a deep learning surrogate model driven by real-world physical priors. Trained via an end-to-end architecture, this framework integrates a novel sampling strategy with advanced dimensionality reduction techniques. These methodological innovations collectively alleviate the dimensionality bottlenecks inherent in large-scale spatial optimization tasks. Empirical validation across two real-world urban regions confirms that GraphicSWMM consistently outperforms existing approaches and exhibits potential for transferability to regions with different climatic conditions. In urban catchments characterized by high-resolution drainage networks and constrained budgets, the proposed model achieves a 481.1-fold acceleration in computational efficiency compared to conventional workflows, while simultaneously reducing flood discharge volumes by 45.0% and inundation areas by 38.3%. This framework serves as a robust decision-support tool that balances flood mitigation performance with construction costs, facilitating more resilient urban drainage systems.

title: A knowledge-constrained improved Mean Flow method for planar sedimentary facies interpretation
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 680, Part A Author(s): Xu Yang, Shaoqun Dong, Xu Bai, Junkun Quan, Tao Xu, Sai Yao, Lianbo Zeng, Mingxuan Han, Naiyang Sun, Huangshuai Kong
abstract: Planar sedimentary facies interpretation conditioned on well data remains challenging because the limited spatial coverage of wells makes lateral continuity difficult to preserve. To address this, a knowledge-constrained improved Mean Flow (K-iMF) method is proposed, integrating data-driven velocity-field learning, variogram-regularized training, and variogram-guided candidate selection. Multi-directional variogram discrepancies regularize velocity-field learning during training. During inference, the fixed U-Net maps independently sampled latent variables in parallel and retains the candidate with the lowest discrepancy score. The method was evaluated on a fluvial facies dataset from the Hailar River system and a delta-front microfacies dataset from the Songliao Basin. Among the evaluated methods, K-iMF achieved the highest accuracy and F1-score on both datasets. Relative to iMF, K-iMF increased accuracy from 95.7% to 97.0% and F1-score from 90.9% to 93.8% on the fluvial dataset. On the delta-front dataset, accuracy increased from 84.5% to 88.8% and F1-score from 67.2% to 77.4%. The anisotropic variograms more closely reproduced the reference ranges and sills, while pixel-wise variance remained non-zero along facies boundaries, indicating that spatial consistency was improved without collapsing the stochastic realizations. Compared with the diffusion model, K-iMF achieved higher predictive performance while requiring less than 1/290 of its testing time. In blind well tests, the method achieved accuracies of 80% and 78% for the two datasets, respectively. Predictive performance improved and variability decreased as the number of conditioning wells increased, with both trends more pronounced for the delta-front dataset. Overall, K-iMF improves predictive performance and directional spatial consistency while retaining stochastic variability and efficient inference.

title: Enhancing river flow prediction accuracy in data scarce catchments using a time varying ensemble deep learning approach
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 680, Part A Author(s): Angel I. Tumushabe, Seith N. Mugume, Johanna Sörensen
abstract: Ensemble deep learning (EDL) methods offer an effective way to reduce model structural uncertainty and improve the reliability of river flow predictions, especially in catchments with limited data. This study evaluated the performance of a Time-Varying Dynamic Model Averaging (TV-DMA) ensemble for integrating heterogeneous machine learning and deep learning architectures, including FFNN, 1D-CNN, LSTM, CNN-LSTM and Diff-FFNN-LSTM models, for river flow prediction in two hydrologically distinct, data-scarce tropical catchments in the Upper White Nile Basin. Results show that the heterogeneous, first-order differential processing Diff-FFNN-LSTM model consistently achieved the highest individual-model river flow predictive performance (NSE ≥ 0.980), due to its ability to stabilise non-stationary river flow time series by mitigating boundary effects associated with decomposition methods, thereby improving representation of rapid flow transitions. Additionally, the TV-DMA resulted in more superior performance in both the Semliki (NSE = 0.910; PBIAS = −0.42%) and Tochi (NSE = 0.831; PBIAS = −0.34%) catchments when compared to the Bayesian Model Averaging (BMA) ensemble (Semliki: NSE = 0.848; PBIAS = −0.20% and Tochi: NSE = 0.710, PBIAS = −18.86%). BMA and TV-DMA also improved computational efficiency by 98–98.4% and 77–81%, respectively, relative to the process-based HEC-HMS model. The findings highlight the principal value of TV-DMA’s dynamic update of individual model weights based on predictive error distributions, which enhances river flow predictive performance, particularly in the rainfall-runoff-dominated Tochi catchment. This EDL approach can improve the accuracy and efficiency of river flow modelling and support the development of flood forecasting and early warning systems in data scarce regions.

title: Emergence of macroscopic hydraulic behaviors from data: a hybrid physics-AI universal differential equation framework for spatio-temporal soil moisture dynamics
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 680, Part A Author(s): Wenrui Yuan, Shi Hu, Chaoyang Du, Chesheng Zhan
abstract:  HPA-UDE addresses point-to-grid scale mismatch via learned macroscopic relationships  Macroscopic constitutive relationships and thresholds emerge directly from data  Mass-conserving Neural ODE reveals hidden fluxes and climate-human impacts

title: Water quality data imputation based on spatial neighborhood-aware and error-adaptive dynamic fusion model
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 680, Part A Author(s): Xinwei Fang, Zhonglian Jiang, Lei Liu, Xuejun Feng, Jianqun Guo
abstract: Marine water quality data frequently suffer from missing values, undermining the reliability of data analysis and the scientific basis for environmental management decisions. To enhance the completeness and accuracy of water quality data imputation, a Spatial Neighborhood-aware and Error-Adaptive dynamic Fusion (SN-EAF) imputation model has been proposed. It improves the spatial perception capability by constructing enhanced spatial neighborhood information features, employs multiple base imputation models with error predictors to assess sample-level prediction errors, and eventually achieves personalized data fusion through dynamic weighting. Experimental results demonstrate that, for salinity indicator, the proposed model achieved mean R 2 values of 0.913 (Missing Completely at Random) and 0.868 (Continuous Block Missing), while the RMSE was reduced by 12.1%–28.2% and 17.4%–30.1% approximately, compared with the best-performing base model. The model adaptively adjusts the weights of base models according to the spatial distribution characteristics of water quality parameters, with error-prediction R 2 values ranging from 0.759 to 0.909 for three representative base models under two data missing scenarios. It consistently outperforms the contrast methods across four additional water quality indicators (Dissolved Oxygen, Total Nitrogen, Particulate Organic Carbon and Chlorophyll-a) and 19 distinct data missing scenarios. The results verify its robustness in complex marine monitoring applications and provide a promising tool for intelligent imputation of marine water quality indicators. The present study shares valuable insights into the data imputation and marine environmental management.

title: Moderate litter biomass benefits soil water replenishment in semiarid grasslands
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 680, Part A Author(s): Yang Luo, Kemiao Li, Jie Zhang, Bingcheng Xu
abstract: Litter plays a crucial role in rainfall redistribution and hydrological cycles, and understanding its hydrological effects is of great significance for ecological management and restoration. Decades of vegetation restoration on the Loess Plateau have resulted in accumulated litter, which has further influenced regional ecohydrology and sustainable grassland restoration. To elucidate grassland litter interception capacity and its role in regulating runoff and infiltration, plot-scale experiments were conducted using immersion and simulated rainfall (10, 20, and 40 mm) methods. Three ground litter types (Bothriochloa ischaemum, Stipa bungeana, and Artemisia gmelinii) and the standing litter of A. gmelinii were evaluated across four biomass gradients (0, 100, 200, and 300 g m−2). The results showed that the interception capacity quantified via simulated rainfall was 2.54 to 6.82 times higher than that of immersion method. Litter type, biomass, and rainfall amount significantly influenced the proportion of interception, runoff, and infiltration. Ground litter of A. gmelinii exhibited significantly higher interception and infiltration proportions than B. ischaemum and S. bungeana. As litter biomass increased, the interception proportion rose consistently, whereas the soil infiltration proportion increased initially, then decreased. Increases in rainfall amount were partitioned mainly into the proportion of surface runoff. Litter thickness was the strongest predictor of interception, whereas soil bulk density and initial soil water storage were the main predictors of runoff and infiltration. Among the tested levels, approximately 100 g m−2 produced the greatest soil water replenishment, whereas higher biomass increased litter interception. These findings suggest that litter accumulation during long-term restoration may reduce effective rainfall and that maintaining moderate litter biomass could improve soil water replenishment in semiarid grasslands.

title: Predicting root-zone soil moisture using a small sample deep learning approach
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 680, Part A Author(s): Yalin Xie, Jing Tian, Yongqiang Zhang, Xuanze Zhang, Longhao Wang, Haoshan Wei, Xian Wang, Zixuan Tang
abstract: Estimating root-zone soil moisture (RZSM) under sparse in-situ observations is closely related to the broader Prediction in Ungauged Basins (PUB) challenge. This study introduces a novel application of the Tabular Prior-data Fitted Network (TabPFN) for predicting RZSM using small sample sizes (fewer than 10,000) and evaluates its robustness under extreme data sparsity conditions. Using five-fold spatial cross-validation conducted at the grid-cell level, TabPFN was trained on sampled data, while the baseline models (RF, XGBoost, CatBoost and Tabular ResNet) were trained on both sampled and full datasets. All models were evaluated on full test sets to ensure a consistent benchmark. Our results indicate that under extremely sparse training conditions (one sample per grid), TabPFN achieves the highest prediction accuracy (R = 0.726 ± 0.002; RMSE = 0.069 ± 0.0004; MAE = 0.053 ± 0.0003), improving correlation by 2.5–9.2% and reducing prediction errors by 2.6–9.8% compared to benchmark models. In time-specific modeling, where separate models were constructed for each day, week, and month, its performance advantage was broadly maintained across changing hydro-climatic states and under consistent temporal aggregation. Its performance also remained relatively stable as training grid density decreased, including when fewer than 40% of the available training grids were used. These results demonstrate that TabPFN enables robust RZSM prediction using small samples and provides a practical tool for drought monitoring and water assessment in data-scarce or poorly monitored regions.

title: Organic carbon dynamics in a subtropical watershed: hydrological processes and land use controls
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 680, Part A Author(s): Guan-Zhou Lin, Li-Chi Chiang
abstract: Land use and hydrological processes jointly influence soil organic carbon (SOC) storage and riverine organic carbon (OC) export in subtropical watersheds. This study employed the SWAT-C model to quantify SOC storage and the export of dissolved organic carbon (DOC) and particulate organic carbon (POC) in the Wu River Basin, Taiwan, during 2012–2017. Model calibration against observed total organic carbon (TOC) fluxes achieved robust performance (NSE ≥ 0.7), supporting its applicability for representing watershed-scale and seasonal carbon transport in high-energy, data-scarce basins. Simulations estimated mean annual DOC and POC exports of 10.4 and 6.9 kg ha−1 yr−1, respectively, with SOC stocks ranging from 155 to 294 t ha−1 (mean: 224 t ha−1), based on soil profile depths defined by the soil-layer data incorporated into the SWAT-C model. The results reveal pronounced spatiotemporal heterogeneity, with annual OC export varying by more than one order of magnitude across subbasins. Irrigated paddy fields functioned as significant carbon sinks, whereas bare land and rainfed croplands on steep slopes emerged as major POC source areas. More than 60% of annual OC export occurred during the wet season (June–September), and the peak export months (July–August) contributed over 30% of annual POC export and over 20% of annual DOC export. These results indicate that wet-season hydrological conditions strongly regulate seasonal carbon mobilization, without implying precise event-scale simulation. Overall, the findings demonstrate how hydrological routing and land-use intensity interact to modulate SOC retention and riverine OC export. This study offers a scientific basis for targeted erosion control and enhanced SOC sequestration to strengthen watershed resilience and sustainable management in subtropical monsoon regions.

title: Artificial interventions temporarily influence bacterial community spatial patterns along a natural river continuum
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 680, Part A Author(s): Han Gao, Yujia Zhai, Yanci Zhang, Hongjie Wang, Baoshan Cui
abstract: River networks increasingly connect natural and engineered reaches, yet spatial variation in nearshore sediment bacterial communities across these connected habitats remains poorly resolved. This study investigated the spatial dynamics of bacterial communities in nearshore surface sediments along the natural-artificial continuum of the Daqing River Basin during the dry season. Alpha diversity was 22.58% lower at the estuary than in the upstream reach. Assembly metrics, network topology, and source assignments also varied among sampled reaches. At the confluence, the median source assignment to the engineered channel was 24.2%, compared with 15.1% assigned to the upstream river; farther downstream, the upstream river was the largest identified source (38.4%). This study elucidates bacterial community dynamics in complex river–lake systems and supports prioritizing natural hydrological connectivity conservation for ecosystem health in the Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei region.

title: Long-term monitoring of lake dynamics across the Yangtze River Basin using multi-source altimetry fusion
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 680, Part A Author(s): Yong Wang, Yulin Gong, Yinghong Jing, Xiaojun She, Shanlong Lu, Yao Li
abstract: The Yangtze River Basin (YRB) contains numerous natural lakes whose water level fluctuations are typically an order of magnitude smaller than those of managed reservoirs, posing a major challenge for high-resolution, long-term monitoring. To address this limitation, we developed a multi-source satellite altimetry fusion algorithm to enhance the detection of subtle water level variations and integrated it with long-term optical observations to enable consistent basin-scale monitoring. These resulting records are compiled into the YRB Lake Dynamics (YLD) dataset, which provides monthly time series of lake area, water level, and lake water storage variations from 1990 to 2023. The YLD dataset delivers an enhanced water level product derived from multi-source altimetry fusion for 883 lakes (accounting for >99% of total lake area). It establishes robust area–elevation (A–E) relationships for 440 lakes (>90% of total lake capacity), with a mean coefficient of determination (R2) of 0.76. Validation against in situ observations from 12 lakes demonstrates strong agreement in reconstructed dynamics, with a mean correlation coefficient (CC) of 0.73, a mean root-mean-square error (RMSE) of 0.73 m, and a normalized RMSE (NRMSE) of 14.05%. Over the past three decades, approximately 70% of large lakes within the basin have contracted, driving declines in total lake area and water storage at rates of 16.07 ± 6.95 km2 yr⁻1 and 144.28 ± 44.11 Mm3 yr⁻1, respectively. In contrast, about 61% of small lakes have expanded, accompanied by a mean water level rise of 1.65 ± 0.50 cm yr⁻1. Spatially, a distinct pattern of “shrinkage in the middle reaches and expansion in the upper and lower reaches” emerges, indicating the combined influence of climate change and human activities across different hydrological regions. Overall, this study demonstrates the effectiveness of multi-source altimetry fusion for high-resolution monitoring of lakes with subtle water level variations, thereby providing a transferable methodological framework and a long-term dataset for investigating lake dynamics in similar systems worldwide.

title: Coupled thermal-hydraulic model of the continental subsurface: theory, regimes, and reduced solver
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 680, Part A Author(s): Masoud Rostami, Bijan Fallah, Farahnaz Fazel-Rastgar, Li-Yun Fu
abstract: The thermal regime of the continental subsurface is shaped by the interplay of atmospheric forcing, groundwater flow, and solid Earth heat. While many existing models couple groundwater flow and heat transport, and in some cases incorporate freeze-thaw or thermo-hydro-mechanical processes, representing the full spectrum of two-way feedbacks often remains challenging. This paper has two components and keeps them distinct throughout. The first is theoretical: a continuum formulation that explicitly couples two-way thermal-hydraulic feedback with a smooth freeze-thaw treatment. From first principles, we derive the governing equations for mass and energy and perform a scaling analysis that yields nine dimensionless numbers, including a newly identified thermal-hydraulic coupling metric ( Γ N α ). These numbers quantify the competition between pressure diffusion, saturation storage, thermal expansion, conduction, advection, and latent heat, and they define quantitative regime diagrams for the three interfaces (land surface, subsurface, crust-mantle). We reduce the full three-dimensional system to a closed one-dimensional vertical column suitable for basin-scale applications. The second component is a reduced thermal-hydraulic numerical implementation, narrower than the theory. This open-source finite-volume solver (implicit time stepping, upwind advection, apparent-heat-capacity freeze-thaw) carries the thermal-expansion feedback, Darcy advection and freeze-thaw, but omits the phase-change mass source, the poroelastic porosity evolution, the skeleton momentum balance, and the gas phase. The solver reports its own mass- and energy-budget residuals, and those diagnostics show that the omitted source is a first-order wherever the freezing point is crossed. The solver is cross-verified against an independent finite-difference Crank-Nicolson code and passes six analytical benchmarks (Carslaw-Jaeger, Stefan, Theis, Terzaghi, undrained thermo-poroelastic ratio, Bonacina), most of which are operator verifications. Four canonical 1-D case studies (permafrost, geothermal reservoir, arid basin, thermo-poro coupled) demonstrate consistency between the designed inputs and the proposed theoretical classification, and a 2-D extension explores lateral basin recharge-discharge and permafrost edge effects. The open-source solver, within its applicability domain, equipped with a test suite and conservation diagnostics, provides a computational tool for attributing subsurface thermal anomalies to their physical drivers and for projecting future thermal evolution under changing environmental conditions.

title: Overcoming phosphate scarcity in summer: DOP bioavailability mediates nutrient cycling in the Yellow Sea
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 680, Part A Author(s): Peiyun Wu, Yingxue Qu, Dongdong Zhu, Zhengqing Chai, Wen Liang, Su Mei Liu
abstract: Phosphorus (P) limitation is pervasive in the summer Yellow Sea (YS), where strong stratification restricts vertical nutrient supply and shapes the cycling of dissolved and particulate P species. This study investigated nutrient dynamics and P speciation during summer, with an emphasis on the potential bioavailability of dissolved organic phosphorus (DOP) under P-depleted conditions. Our findings reveal that nutrient partitioning was principally regulated by physical stratification and the Yellow Sea Cold Water Mass (YSCWM), resulting in distinct vertical gradients in P speciation that also varied spatially across the study region. DOP dominated the total dissolved P pool in the surface layer (67%), reflecting active biological uptake of DIP and subsequent organic matter transformation. In contrast, bottom waters were characterized by DIP as the dominant fraction (75%), driven by microbial degradation and adsorption–desorption processes. Low-molecular-weight DOP (< 3 kDa) dominated the DOP pool (52% of total DOP), and was found to exhibit greater bioavailability compared to higher molecular weight fractions. Incubation experiments revealed that up to 20% of DOP could be utilized by heterotrophic bacteria under P scarcity, with microbial growth sustained at a DOP concentration as low as 0.101 μmol L−1. The minimum DIP concentration required to sustain bacterial growth was approximately 0.014 μmol L−1. In addition, terrestrial inputs and sediment resuspension influenced the particulate P dynamics in the YS. This study also highlights the interplay between physical transport processes (e.g., stratification and water mass mixing) and biological transformations in regulating of P cycling. Our results emphasize the critical role of DOP in maintaining the stability of ecosystems in P-limited marine environments.

title: A spatiotemporal decomposition–coordination optimization method for multi-objective real-time flood-control operation of cascade reservoir systems
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 680, Part A Author(s): Mengxue Ben, Ping-an Zhong, Feilin Zhu, Bin Wang, Yukun Fan, Juan Chen, Yu Han, Zixin Song, Bin Xu, Sunyu Xu
abstract: Cascade reservoir systems involve close upstream–downstream hydraulic connections and complex spatiotemporal interactions with flood-control sections, leading to a high-dimensional and strongly coupled model for real-time joint flood-control operation. To address this issue, this study proposes a spatiotemporal decomposition–coordination optimization framework based on recursive excess water volume. By introducing the concept of recursive excess water volume, the framework transforms the spatiotemporally coupled flow constraints into a spatially coordinated water-volume allocation problem. It then establishes a decomposition structure integrating spatial allocation, temporal operation, and feedback coordination, thereby enabling structural decoupling and efficient solution of the complex joint operation problem. Multi-scenario numerical experiments are conducted for the cascade reservoir system in the lower Jinsha River. The results show that: (1) The proposed framework reduces the coordination complexity of joint operation under strong spatiotemporal coupling and enables decomposition-based solution of high-dimensional spatiotemporal optimization problems, with the computation time (CT) for a single operation scheme remaining below 1 s. (2) The proposed framework exhibits strong adaptability to different scenarios and satisfies the requirements of joint flood-control operation, with the safety constraint deviation (SCD) at the primary control section remaining within 2% and the coefficient of variation (CV) of reservoir risk indices remaining below 0.02. (3) Compared with conventional multi-objective evolutionary algorithms, the proposed framework generates trade-off solution sets with superior overall performance and produces more balanced and interpretable risk-sharing solutions among reservoirs. The proposed framework provides methodological support for real-time flood-control operation of cascade reservoir systems.

title: Explainable method for advanced early-warning of hypoxic events in estuaries: coupling Kolmogorov-Arnold networks with self-attention mechanism
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 680, Part A Author(s): Xingda Chen, Chenyao Zhao, Xingming Liao, Anxiang Di, Jinyue Chen, Mengjun Ku, Zhenyu Gao, Zhen Zhang, Qianling Ci, Yida Lu, Lili Wen, Shuisen Chen, Peijian Zeng
abstract: Hypoxic events are increasingly threatening estuarine ecosystems, leading to the formation of dead zones and drastic shifts in ecosystem structure. However, existing dissolved oxygen (DO) predictions often struggle to capture long-term trends and achieve early-warning, and lack interpretability into driving factors. To address these limitations, this study proposes a novel interpretable deep learning method to forecast DO and capture hypoxic events, that was named as KTDO, which couples Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KAN) with a self-attention mechanism and training with noise-robust strategy (NRS). The method enables powerful global dependency modeling and enhanced capability of catching up the extreme hypoxic events (DO < 2 mg/L). Experiments are conducted based on 114,174 measurements from typical estuaries along coastal China, and (1) the KTDO has better performance than other eight state-of-the-art (SOTA) benchmarks in numerical DO prediction (mean R2 = 0.954, RMSE = 0.293 mg/L) and hypoxic events early-warning (Probability of Detection (POD) = 85.09%). (2) Ablation studies confirm the key role of the Kolmogorov-Arnold Spline Module (KASM) in capturing biogeochemical processes and the training strategy of NRS in improving generalization across heterogeneous estuaries (models with KASM and NRS have highest R2 and lowest RMSE in most estuaries). Further evaluation between KTDO and the Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average (ARIMA) model reveals the advantage of integrating both DO autocorrelation and supplementary water quality information, maintaining robust performance across all estuaries and time horizons (1-, 3-, 5-, and 7-day); notably, when the dominant DO_lag1 feature is removed, KTDO retains stable accuracy while ARIMA degrades sharply, confirming that this robustness stems from multivariate information fusion rather than reliance on the most recent DO observation. (3) Global interpretability analysis reveals a strong autocorrelation in the DO and lag features in time series and identifies two dominant prediction patterns: one driven by a few key features with huge contribution, and another by synergistic multi-feature interactions·NH3-N and pH contribute to DO prediction more frequently than other water quality parameters (WQPs) and the canonical WT-DO relationship is context-dependent and can be obscured in dynamic estuaries with high variability. (4) Deconstruction of model decision-making process in predictions with largest errors indicates that confounding effects among WQPs often mislead the direction of model output. (5) Cross-basin experiments further show that KTDO generalizes well at short lead times but degrades over longer horizons, underscoring the need to integrate multi-basin and multi-station information in future work. By providing accurate and interpretable numerical prediction together with hypoxia early warning, KTDO offers a potential solution for science-informed DO management.

title: Straw return enhances groundwater nitrate attenuation by fueling subsurface carbon–nitrogen coupling: Evidence from field monitoring and metagenomics
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 680, Part A Author(s): Shuo Gong, Jia Xin, Kang Yue, Linna Jia, Yueqi Wang, Xiaoxi Yu, Wenlin Ren, Hang Fu, Jie Dong
abstract: Excessive nitrate contamination of groundwater from agricultural activities is a global concern, yet natural attenuation is often limited by insufficient bioavailable organic carbon. Straw return has the potential to stimulate nitrate attenuation by supplying labile carbon; however, carbon–nitrogen coupling mechanisms across the unsaturated–saturated zone continuum remain unclear. Here, a field experiment compared straw return with low nitrogen fertilization (SL) and conventional fertilization (CK), integrating hydrological monitoring, geochemical analysis, dual nitrate isotope tracing, and metagenomics. Straw return significantly increased dissolved organic carbon (DOC) in soil and groundwater, with 32% higher peak soil DOC in SL. Groundwater NO3 −-N stock was consistently lower under SL, resulting in net removal (5.50%), whereas CK showed net accumulation (−30.98%). Dual isotope signatures (δ15N and δ18O of NO3 −) indicated that moderate denitrification occurs in groundwater. Metagenomics further revealed that straw-derived DOC selectively enriched heterotrophic denitrifiers and organic matter degraders. The carbon–nitrogen functional gene network in SL groundwater showed higher connectivity, suggesting enhanced metabolic coupling. Structural equation modeling identified DOC as the primary regulating factor, mediating a shift in nitrogen transformation pathways by promoting denitrification while concurrently suppressing nitrification. Collectively, these results reveal a mechanistic framework in which exogenous carbon inputs facilitate nitrate attenuation by strengthening microbial metabolic coupling, reorganizing biogeochemical pathways toward reductive nitrogen processes, and ultimately driving net nitrate removal in groundwater systems. These findings provide mechanistic insights and practical support for developing sustainable in situ remediation strategies for agricultural nitrate pollution in groundwater.

title: Integrating SWOT data and machine learning for high-resolution river surface velocity retrieval in data-scarce headwater regions
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 680, Part A Author(s): Pengfei Zhan, Kai Liu, Jiaming Na, Tan Chen, Jinkai Guo, Chunqiao Song
abstract: River surface velocity is a critical hydrodynamic variable governing flood wave propagation, sediment transport, and aquatic ecosystem stability, yet it remains poorly observed in data-scarce headwater rivers of the Tibetan Plateau (TP). While the Surface Water and Ocean Topography (SWOT) mission provides high resolution observations of water surface elevation, it does not directly measure river surface velocity. To address this gap, this study develops a hydraulically informed machine learning (ML) framework that integrates SWOT Level-2 Pixel cloud data with in-situ velocity measurements to retrieve spatially continuous river velocity fields in data-scarce alpine environments. We constructed a high-fidelity dataset with 212 paired samples from seven representative field sites, encompassing diverse hydraulic conditions. Among four candidate ML algorithms, the XGBoost model enforced with longitudinal water surface slope (WSS), river width, and discharge as mandatory hydraulic predictors, demonstrated superior performance. The final model achieved strong independent testing skill (R2 = 0.80, MAE = 0.09 m/s, RMSE = 0.17 m/s, MAPE = 8.44%), maintaining robustness even in low-velocity conditions (< 1 m/s). SHAP-based interpretability analysis indicates that longitudinal WSS was the dominant predictor (35.51%), while temperature (25.88%) and NDVI (8.51%) provided additional information as hydroclimatic and riparian context proxies. We further applied the optimal model to generate reach-aggregated surface velocities for 5,434 2-km river reaches across the eastern TP, spanning 0.87–1.70 m/s (median 0.95 m/s; IQR 0.92–1.46 m/s). Across the study basins, the mapped reach-scale velocities exhibit spatial contrasts in both central tendency and spread. The Qaidam Basin shows persistently low and spatially coherent velocities, whereas the upper Yangtze and upper Yellow River basins display wider distributions and stronger spatial heterogeneity, including contiguous fast-flow corridors and localized low-velocity zones. These findings demonstrate that integrating SWOT altimetry with ML models offers a scalable pathway for monitoring river hydrodynamics in ungauged high-altitude river systems.

title: Moderate microplastic pollution and ecological risks in the Yellow River Basin
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 680, Part A Author(s): Shun Wan, Guoce Xu, Yahong Fan, Xin Chen, Zhanbin Li, Mengyao Tuo, Mengyuan Zhao, Kang Fang
abstract: The Yellow River is one of the major rivers transporting microplastics (MPs) to the ocean in China, yet basin-wide information on MP distribution, sources, and ecological risks remains limited. Therefore, this study systematically investigated MPs across the entire Yellow River Basin. MP contamination was widespread throughout the Yellow River basin. The average abundances of MPs were 5.10 ± 0.68 items/L and 137.16 ± 20.11 items/kg in surface water and sediments, respectively. Small (<1 mm) and white MPs were the predominant categories, accounting for 86.9–91.2% and 57.0–65.5%, respectively. The morphology and polymer composition of the MPs in surface water were primarily characterized by polypropylene and polyethylene fibers, whereas those in sediments were predominantly characterized by pellet-shaped particles and polyester. Spatial analysis revealed significant differences in MP abundance and composition among media and river sections (P < 0.05). However, no significant differences were observed in MP abundance or composition between the mainstream and tributaries in the surface water or sediments. Anthropogenic factors, particularly the proportion of built-up land and population density, were identified as the key drivers of MP distribution in surface water. In contrast, the MP distribution in sediments was influenced by both natural (e.g., annual precipitation and annual mean temperature) and anthropogenic factors. Source apportionment indicated that wastewater treatment plant effluent, agricultural soils, and road dust were the primary MP sources, contributing 48.7%, 34.1%, and 17.0%, respectively. The ecological risk assessment based on species sensitivity curves suggested that the overall MP pollution in the basin posed a moderate ecological risk.

title: Land-use regulation of coupled carbon–nitrogen–phosphorus cycling and carbon-sink stability in karst surface water–groundwater systems: synthesis from the Shawan water–carbon cycle experimental test site, SW China
description: Publication date: November 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 680, Part A Author(s): Pan Tao, Mingyu Shao, Sibo Zeng, Zaihua Liu, Qian Bao, Yikun Jia, Mohamed Aboueldahab, Hailong Sun, Liangxing Shi, Min Zhao, Xu Wang, Junyao Yan, Hang Li, Yirun Zhang
abstract: Karst inland waters receive substantial inputs of weathering-derived dissolved inorganic carbon (DIC), which can support aquatic primary production and the formation of autochthonous organic carbon. However, how land-use change alters the coupled delivery of DIC, nitrogen, and phosphorus, thereby regulating carbon sequestration potential and eutrophication risk, remains poorly understood. Here, we review previous studies and long-term observations from the Shawan Water–Carbon Cycle Experimental Test Site in Southwest China to evaluate how contrasting land-use types regulate coupled C–N–P cycling in karst aquatic systems. We propose a mechanistic framework linking land use, soil CO2 production, carbonate weathering, DIC export, nutrient stoichiometry, aquatic biological uptake, and sedimentary carbon–phosphorus preservation. The synthesis indicates that bare rock and bare soil systems generally have weak carbon-sink potential because limited vegetation cover reduces soil CO2 production, carbonate weathering, DIC delivery, and aquatic productivity. Cropland, in contrast, often increases nitrogen and phosphorus export disproportionately relative to effective inorganic carbon supply, promoting phytoplankton proliferation, cyanobacterial risk, and less efficient carbon preservation. Ecological restoration, especially grassland and shrubland recovery, can enhance soil CO2 generation and carbonate weathering while reducing nutrient export, creating high-DIC but relatively nutrient-constrained conditions. Under suitable hydrological and light conditions, this favors submerged macrophytes, epiphytic algae, and non-cyanobacterial autotrophs, thereby strengthening biological DIC utilization, autochthonous organic carbon production, phosphorus immobilization, and sedimentary carbon burial. Overall, land-use change regulates karst aquatic carbon sinks not only by altering DIC export but also by reshaping C–N–P stoichiometry and biogeochemical pathways across the land–water continuum. These findings highlight ecological restoration as a potential strategy to coordinate carbon sink enhancement with eutrophication control in karst waters. Future studies should integrate replicated mesocosm experiments, natural-water validation, and long-term regional monitoring to determine how land-use-driven C–N–P coupling regulates the transformation and long-term preservation of weathering-derived DIC in aquatic carbon pools after accounting for remineralization and CO2/CH4 losses.

title: Contrasting effects of arsenic and cadmium on PFAS transport in soils: Mechanistic insights and mathematical models
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 679, Part C Author(s): Wei Zhang, Yajing Wang, Xueqi Zhang, Boyun Ma, Yuting Wang, Bingyue Guo, Dongmei Zhou, Qiming Xian
abstract: PFAS and heavy metals (HMs) coexist in contaminated sites mainly due to chemical production and waste disposal. This study comprehensively investigated the transport behaviors PFOS, PFOA, and PFHxS under coexisting As(V)/Cd(II) in water-saturated soils. Combining batch experiments, column tests, and Hydrus-1D, the retention and transport dynamics of PFAS were examined. Sorption affinity followed the order: PFOS > PFOA > PFHxS, while the opposite order was observed for desorption and transport. At 500 μg/L, breakthrough curves (BTC) of PFOA and PFHxS are generally symmetric, but the BTC of PFOS displays a nonideal transport. Critically, As(V) accelerated PFOS transport by 9.4–34.9% through pH-induced repulsion and site competition, while Cd(II) enhanced PFOS retention by 61.6–86.8% through electrostatic attraction and cation bridging. Hydrophobic interactions, electrostatic forces, and HMs speciation play critical roles in determining the fate of PFAS. Furthermore, multiple PFAS transport datasets were used to validate a mathematical model incorporating advection–dispersion and chemical nonequilibrium sorption, and the model was applied for the first time to simulate the PFAS transport in the saturated zone affected by HMs. Long-term simulation (50 years) showed that As(V) accelerates PFOS migration to groundwater (5 m), whereas Cd(II) restricts its penetration to a depth of 0.2 m. Given weak sorption, PFOA and PFHxS quickly leach downward and threaten groundwater safety within 10 years. This study developed predictive frameworks for PFAS-HMs transport and risk assessment in industrial sites, enhancing priority management and remediation strategies based on the characteristics of co-contaminants to protect the soil environment and groundwater sources.

title: Self-similarity criticality of the world’s large river systems
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 679, Part C Author(s): Zhenqi Li, Yichu Wang, Jinren Ni
abstract: River networks, as hierarchical conduits of material transport and energy conversion, exhibit self-similar structural patterns that are fundamental to hydrological processes. Yet, the mechanisms constraining their self-similarity boundaries remain elusive. Here, by analyzing 66 global large river basins (≥ 100,000 km2) using HydroATLAS data, we define a self-similar validity ratio (SVR) to quantify the normalized stream-order domain over which scale-invariant organization persists. River networks converge at low-to-medium stream orders (1–5) but diverge at higher orders (6–10), with the global SVR distribution having a dominant range of 0.57–0.67 that statistically aligns with the golden-ratio conjugate (φ = 0.618). This motivates classification of three self-similar criticality regimes, i.e., sub-golden, golden-aligned, and supra-golden rivers. By further constructing a self-similar criticality framework supported by three domain-guided composite hydrogeomorphic indices, validated against an energetic response index derived from the criticality thresholds at the self-similar collapse boundary, we reveal that the three regime types of rivers respectively correspond to energy-limited, energy-balanced, and energy-surplus states, and the alignment between SVR and φ marks a stable equilibrium state of hierarchical energy redistribution within river networks, where hydrological carrier capacity, geomorphic potential energy, and network geometry coordinate well to maintain long-term self-similar organization. These findings transform self-similarity from structural descriptions into physically based energetic analysis, which advances predictive tools for basin resilience under climate change, enabling optimized flood-hazard screening, erosion risk diagnosis, sediment management, and strategic hydropower planning.

title: Well-balanced lattice Boltzmann modelling of the depth-averaged age equation and its correlations with environmental indicators in a typical urban flood retention area
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 679, Part C Author(s): Fei Leng, Haifei Liu, Fan Zhang, Shan He, Liyun Zhang, Yujun Yi
abstract: With the increasing tension on urban spatial resources, urban flood retention areas, as valuable multi-functional spaces integrating flood control, water regulation and ecological conservation, are still plagued by prominent water environment and ecological problems, such as long hydraulic retention time, low water quality and insufficient utilization of ecological space. Water age, as a key indicator reflecting the renewal capacity and hydrodynamic characteristics of water bodies, has a direct and profound impact on water quality parameters (e.g., dissolved oxygen, nutrients, and organic matter) by regulating material cycling and activities of aquatic organisms. This study aims to conduct the refined simulation of water age and clarify its correlations with multiple environmental indicators in a typical urban flood retention area, providing scientific support for sustainable water management. In this study, a well-balanced lattice Boltzmann method (LBM) was developed to simulate the water age distribution of the flood retention area under controlled hydrological conditions. Meanwhile, a year-round comprehensive monitoring program was implemented to collect water environmental data, including ammonia nitrogen (NH3-N), total phosphorus (TP) and dissolved oxygen (DO). By integrating numerical simulation results and in-situ monitoring data, the correlation between water age distribution and environmental indicators in the flood retention area was systematically analyzed. The results indicate that there is a significant nonlinear correlation between water age and these three indicators, with prolonged water age leading to the increasing concentrations and eutrophication risk. Based on these findings, targeted management suggestions are proposed, including optimizing the water dispatch mode to shorten the average water age, constructing ecological corridors to enhance water connectivity, and establishing a dynamic monitoring system combining numerical simulation and in-situ observation.

title: Numerical modeling of redox-sensitive transformations in a dynamic capillary fringe
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 679, Part C Author(s): Xin Liu, Zengyu Zhang, Alex Furman
abstract: Subsurface contamination is a significant problem due to excessive fertigation and wastewater discharge. However, depth and spatial extent often make it difficult to understand the nature of contaminant spread and its attenuation. Numerical modeling is an essential tool for exploring less-understood processes. However, there is a gap in the systematic simulation of the relationship between biogeochemical processes and redox potential, a relatively straightforward measure of subsurface biochemical state. Thus, a model is needed to facilitate an understanding of subsurface processes and provide a further theoretical basis for practice. This research aims to simulate subsurface biogeochemical dynamics and their correlation with redox potential. Water flow and biogeochemical dynamics are considered in both physical and biogeochemical models, incorporating the biogeochemical cycles of C, N, O, Mn, Fe, and S. The physical and biogeochemical models are coupled with the redox potential model addressed by the Butler-Volmer equation. A synthetic case study that mimics the conditions in a dynamic capillary fringe under a soil-aquifer treatment (SAT) facility was used to demonstrate the model. We demonstrate that the redox potential can reflect redox species concentrations (e.g., oxygen and nitrate) and reaction rates (i.e., nitrification, denitrification, and DOC aerobic oxidation), because the intrinsic mechanism of this model is superior to traditional simplified models. In our mechanistic model, both redox reactions and potentials are governed by multiple redox species and parameters, and the simulation can be adjusted by varying these parameters, making it more suitable for dynamic systems. This is especially important when saturation conditions change frequently. Further, we demonstrate that nitrification, denitrification, and DOC oxidation coexist at different depths, and that flow dynamics can dictate reaction rates and the depths at which they occur.

title: Optimizing evapotranspiration products by merging multi-source datasets with three no-prior-knowledge methods over China
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 679, Part C Author(s): Dayang Wang, Dagang Wang, Xiaogang Shi, Shaobo Liu, Mingfei Ji, Ya Huang, Zequn Lin, Kaihao Long, B. Larry Li, Haoyu Wang
abstract: Accurate quantification of evapotranspiration (ET) is critical for understanding the hydro-climatologic processes and the interactions of the Earth system. Due to considerable uncertainties in single algorithm-based ET products, data fusion provides a promising pathway for improving ET estimation. In this study, we proposed a data fusion framework for optimizing ET products by merging four ET datasets (i.e., ERA5-Land, GLDAS, GLEAM and SiTH) using three fusion methods (i.e., ensemble mean (EM), Bayesian-based three-cornered hat (BTCH) and extended triple collocation (ETC)) without prior knowledge. Twelve fused ET datasets were generated, and their performances were comprehensively evaluated at both site and basin scales. Results show that merged ET datasets generally demonstrate better performances than the original ET datasets in most sites and basins, with lower mean bias error (MBE) and relative root mean square error (RRMSE), and higher coefficient of determination (R2) and Kling-Gupta efficiency (KGE). At the site scale, the greatest improvement occurs at cropland and barren sites, whereas the modest modification appears at forest and grassland sites. At the basin scale, the overestimation in the Songhua River Basin (SHRB) and Liao River Basin (LRB), and the underestimation in the Huai River Basin (HRB) are also reduced by merging ET. Among the ET candidates, SiTH is the dominant ET dataset with the highest fusion weights, while GLDAS has the lowest fusion weights in most triplets. Overall, BTCH and ETC exhibit comparable ET fusion performances and are both superior to the EM method. Additionally, the two methods yield broadly consistent spatial patterns of fusion weights and dominant ET for most triplets. However, BTCH tends to generate more stable weights than ETC when applied to the same triplet. As for the triplet, triplet-1 (ERA5-Land, GLDAS and GLEAM) and triplet-3 (ERA5-Land, GLEAM and SiTH) generally show more outstanding performances than the other triplets for most sites and basins. The fused ET results are more sensitive to the input triplet composition than to the selection of fusion method. The findings of this study can provide valuable insights into the ET data fusion without prior knowledge.

title: A generalized three-dimensional manifold for the Budyko hypothesis: analytical derivation and structural stability in open hydrological systems
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 679, Part C Author(s): Chandra Mohan Shakya, Rajib Kumar Bhattacharjya
abstract: The classical Budyko framework assumes hydrological closure, limiting its applicability to basins influenced by glacier melt, groundwater depletion, reservoir regulation, or inter-basin water transfers. This study presents the ShakyaQX (SQX) manifold, a three-dimensional extension of the Budyko framework that represents hydroclimatic partitioning as a surface in (x, φ, E/P), where x = PET/P is the aridity index and φ = 1 + ΔS/P is a non-rescaled openness coordinate. Unlike input-rescaling approaches, SQX preserves the climatic coordinate while representing basin openness through a separate, non-rescaled dimension, relocating the associated input-rescaling singularity to the boundary of the admissible domain (φ → 0) and providing a single continuous formulation across storage-gain and storage-loss states. The formulation reduces exactly to the Mezentsev–Choudhury–Yang curve when φ = 1. Applied to the Brahmaputra Basin (2002–2021), SQX shows no annual-scale predictive advantage over the classical closed-system formulation (NSE = − 1.407 versus − 0.601) for this basin, where annual φ ranges only from 0.92 to 1.09. At the monthly scale, however, SQX substantially outperforms the classical baseline for the 63 admissible months (NSE = 0.650 versus − 0.005), with performance retained under leave-one-out cross-validation and GRACE Monte Carlo uncertainty propagation. Independent application to seven GRDC-gauged basins in the monsoon-dominated Irrawaddy–Chindwin system shows that SQX does not outperform the classical formulation in six of seven basins. Diagnostic analyses attribute this to numerical conditioning of φ under low dry-season precipitation, rather than to basin size, measurement noise, or failure of the openness concept, thereby defining an explicit boundary condition for the present implementation.

title: Investigating streamflow dynamics in heterogeneous catchments through sensitivity function analysis
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 679, Part C Author(s): Simon Rusjan, Klaudija Lebar, Mojca Šraj
abstract: Comprehending hydrological responses in heterogeneous catchments poses a considerable challenge, primarily due to the spatial variability and complexity of rainfall-runoff processes. This study investigates the streamflow recession behavior within the Vipava River catchment in southwestern Slovenia. The catchment is characterized by contrasting hydrogeological regions, including karst plateaus and impermeable flysch valleys. The analysis focuses on comparing the karst spring-fed upper Vipava river and the torrential Branica stream draining flysch areas. An analysis of long-term daily discharge data was conducted to extract information on streamflow recession. The catchment sensitivity functions were derived to discern discrepancies in hydrological response under varying antecedent conditions. The karst spring sensitivity function exhibits sustained discharge, with activation of underground karst conduits during periods of high flow. Conversely, the flysch-dominated Branica stream demonstrates rapid increases and fast recession, leading to extremely low flows and possible drying out during extended rainless periods. The results highlight the information content of discharge recession data for identifying spatial heterogeneity and distinct flow mechanisms in catchments with different storage characteristics. When expressed through catchment sensitivity functions, this recession-derived information can be incorporated into diagnostic hydrological simulations to compare the hydrological responses of heterogeneous catchments and improve understanding of their functioning under contrasting antecedent conditions.

title: P-FLOOD: a probabilistic framework for flood hazard mapping in levee-protected floodplains
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 679, Part C Author(s): T. Lazzarin, A. Domeneghetti, R. Vacondio, M. Marani, D.P. Viero
abstract: The paper presents a probabilistic framework for mapping hazard induced by river floods in levee-protected floodplains. Large-scale hazard maps of water depth (or any other hazard variable) are derived from the corresponding cumulative probability distributions, estimated throughout the domain from a set of flood simulations that combine different inflow hydrographs and multiple levee-failure scenarios. For each simulation, levee breach probabilities are estimated using fragility functions conditioned on the local hydraulic loading. By accounting for the joint probability of hydrological and breaching events, the method enables a probabilistic characterization of hazard metrics and produces hazard maps associated with any exceedance probability, without being constrained by the discrete return periods of the hydrological inputs. Flood simulations require integrated two-dimensional hydrodynamic models to include flood routing, breach formation, and ensuing floodplain inundation. To limit the computational load, a scalable parent–child strategy is proposed to reduce the number of simulations while retaining acceptable accuracy in the estimated probability field. Moreover, the available simulations can be reused to recompute hazard maps at negligible cost to consider changes in the probability of hydrological and/or breaching events (due to climate change, levee reinforcements, etc.). The framework is applied to a pilot case study in the Adige River (Northern Italy), considering fragility functions for overflow-induced failures and a flood-prone area of ∼100 km2. The results suggest that, if supplied with realistic estimations of levee fragility, P-FLOOD can provide improved hazard predictions compared with traditional approaches, especially for frequent flood events, thereby supporting more informed flood risk management and planning.

title: On non-axisymmetric flow near circumferentially partially clogged artesian wells with mixed boundary conditions
description: Publication date: October 2026 Source: Journal of Hydrology, Volume 679, Part C Author(s): Jiong Li, Yingjun Liu, Hongbin Zhan, Shuo Zhang, Yuefei Huang, Peipeng Wu
abstract: Conventional models of well hydraulics assume a fully penetrating well screen, imposing axisymmetric flow at the well face. In practice, partial clogging can restrict the hydraulic connection to only a portion of the circumference, creating a non-axisymmetric flow field that existing radially symmetric models cannot describe. In this study, we develop a non-uniform flux (NUF) semi-analytical model for transient groundwater flow to and from a circumferentially partially clogged well in a confined aquifer. A mixed boundary condition, consisting of an impermeable condition on the non-screened section and a uniform-drawdown condition on the screened section, allows well-face flux to vary angularly. We solve the resulting initial-boundary value problem with mixed boundary conditions by discretising the screened section into piecewise-uniform flux segments, sequentially applying the Laplace transform and finite Fourier cosine transform, and performing time-domain inversion using the Stehfest algorithm.
