Olivine diffusion chronometry records rejuvenation-to-eruption timescales from week-scale to multi-year, with the longest estimates approaching ∼ 4 years. Micro-computed tomography reveals that antecrystic domains comprise 44–67 vol% of the analyzed macrocryst cargo. Subtraction of the antecryst contribution from bulk-rock compositions produces negligible change in SiO2, but decreases MgO and CaO by ∼ 13% and ∼ 5%, respectively, and increases total alkalis by ∼ 8%, relative to bulk-rock values. This correction partially reconciles bulk-rock and glass/matrix compositions, showing that recycled mush components can measurably affect major-element systematics in mafic alkaline magmas. These results highlight how integrated 2D–3D crystal analysis, combined with temporal anchoring of crystal histories, can improve reconstructions of magma plumbing systems, the processes that prime and sustain mafic eruptions, and the chemical influence of mush-derived crystal cargoes.

title: Pervasive and rapid enrichment of nitrogen in newly erupted oceanic basalt
description: Publication date: 1 October 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta, Volume 430 Author(s): Juan Felipe Bustos-Moreno, Tobias B. Weisenberger, Ryoji Tanaka, Hiroshi Kitagawa, Gray E. Bebout
abstract: The alteration of oceanic crust by seawater is a critical sink in the global nitrogen (N) cycle, yet the mechanisms and timescales of N enrichment remain poorly constrained. We present N concentrations and isotope compositions from a 192-meter drill core (SE-02b) retrieved from the then 50-year-old Surtsey Island in Iceland, a pristine analog for rapid alteration of young oceanic basalt. The altered basaltic tuffs show significant N enrichment (average 11 ± 8 μg/g), relative to unaltered Icelandic basalt glasses (0.028 ± 0.026 μg/g) and MORB (∼1.1 to 1.5 μg/g), matching the global average for altered oceanic crust (11 μg/g; ranging in ages from 5 to 170 Ma). Nitrogen isotope compositions (δ15Nair = −1.7 ± 4.6‰) are primarily consistent with incorporation of seawater- and meteoric-derived ammonium (NH4 +), more likely into secondary K-minerals, palagonitized glass and smectites throughout the core. To a lesser extent, N could be incorporated into Na/Ca-minerals such as analcime in the meteoric water altered zone and sulphates such as anhydrite and gypsum when present. Incorporation of NH4 + into secondary phases occurs with little isotope fractionation consistent with equilibrium fractionation between clay and aqueous NH4 +. We demonstrate that seawater-rock interaction alone can produce the ubiquitous background N enrichment of the oceanic crust without the addition of remobilized N from sedimentary sources. Such magnitude of enrichment is also observed via meteoric water alteration. Localized high enrichments in N in areas of enhanced fluid flow at core SE-02b with exceptionally low δ15N values (as low as −20.1‰), are attributed to abiotic reduction of dissolved N2 under anoxic conditions and/or microbial activity. We propose that N incorporation into the oceanic crust can occur rapidly in days to decades rather than at a constant rate over geologic time. This has major implications for N transfer in subduction zones, N exchange between the oceanic crust, seawater and the atmosphere and for planetary habitability.

title: The impact of the stability of white mica on 40 Ar diffusion during laboratory incremental heating: implications for the interpretation of 40 Ar/ 39 Ar step-heating dates
description: Publication date: 1 October 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta, Volume 430 Author(s): Vidar Jakobsson, Richard Spikings, Stefan Farsang
abstract: White mica thermochronology is founded on the assumption that white mica remains stable during high temperature in vacuo furnace step-heating and hydrothermal experiments, rendering down-temperature extrapolation of laboratory-derived diffusion parameters accurate. However, numerous experiments have shown that white mica dehydroxylates at temperatures exceeding 700°C, although no direct comparisons between dehydroxylation and the degassing behaviour of Ar isotopes during step-heating experiments have been published. We combine Raman spectroscopy with in vacuo incremental step-heating to directly assess whether inflections in Arrhenius space correspond to dehydroxylation. Additionally, we test whether milled white mica with grain sizes 740°C). We argue that the spatial correlation of Na with a reduction in 40Ar/39Ar date occurs because Ar loss is accelerated by cationic interdiffusion or shared pathways during heating.

title: Zn isotope fractionation during sorption on alumina mediated by humic acid
description: Publication date: 1 October 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta, Volume 430 Author(s): Wenxian Gou, Xiaoyu Li, Ying Chen, Lan Jiang, Zhaofeng Zhang, Yi Huang
abstract: Dissolved organic matter (DOM) is ubiquitous in surface environments, yet its influence on Zn stable isotope fractionation at mineral–water interfaces remains poorly constrained, impeding a thorough understanding of Zn isotope behavior in natural systems. This study uses humic acid (HA) as an operational analogue of DOM to investigate HA effects on Zn isotope fractionation during sorption onto γ-alumina. High-precision Zn isotope analyses, combined with X-ray diffraction, transmission electron microscopy, and X-ray absorption fine-structure spectroscopy, reveal that the HA effect is pH-dependent and closely associated with molecular-scale Zn surface speciation. Under acidic conditions, Zn is retained as ≡AlOZn inner-sphere complexes, and HA has little effect on either Zn surface speciation or isotope fractionation. At circumneutral to alkaline pH, however, HA suppresses Zn-Al layered double hydroxide (LDH) formation and redirects Zn toward ≡AlOZn inner-sphere complexation, increasing Zn isotope fractionation from near zero in HA-free systems to 0.44 ± 0.03‰ in HA-rich systems. This increase is consistent with the greater bonding reorganization required to form tetrahedral ≡AlOZn complexes from aqueous Zn than to incorporate Zn into octahedral Zn-Al LDH structures. The HA-based findings may capture, to a first order, DOM effects in systems dominated by carboxyl and phenolic hydroxyl groups, as salicylic acid substitution experiments indicate that organic ligands with similar O-bearing functional groups exert similar controls on interfacial Zn isotope fractionation. These results define a mechanistic end-member constraint for DOM-Al oxide interactions and their role in Zn isotope systematics in organo-mineral and soil–river weathering systems.

title: Aluminium drives hydrogen incorporation in pyrolitic lower mantle: Constraints from a combined FTIR-ERDA-nanoSIMS analysis
description: Publication date: 1 October 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta, Volume 430 Author(s): Siddharth Khan, Nathalie Bolfan-Casanova, Maximilien Verdier-Paoletti, Hélène Bureau, Hicham Khodja, Ana E. Pradas del Real, Denis Andrault
abstract: Hydrogen is present as hydroxyl (OH) defects in the crystal lattices of the nominally anhydrous minerals (NAMs) composing the Earth’s mantle. The NAMs comprising the lower mantle: bridgmanite, ferropericlase, and davemaoite are the three most abundant minerals on Earth, and thus their combined hydrogen solubility exerts a first-order control on the planetary H2O capacity and overall H2O cycle. In this study, we equilibrated the three principal NAMs with hydrous melt at the adiabatic geotherm and pressure corresponding to the shallow lower mantle. The H2O content of the coexisting NAMs is quantified by nanoSIMS using matrix-matched standards characterized by Fourier Transform Infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy combined with Elastic Recoil Detection Analysis (ERDA). Our results show that bridgmanite, ferropericlase, and davemaoite incorporate ∼0.030, ∼0.16, and ∼0.18 wt% H2O, respectively. Our data further suggests that hydrogen is primarily incorporated via Al3+-H+ insertion at the Si4+ (octahedral) site in perovskite-type structures and at the metal (octahedral) site in ferropericlase. Finally, we refine a maximum H2O content of 0.058 (0.009) wt% H2O in a pyrolitic-shallow lower mantle, which is equivalent to ∼1.26 (0.19) ocean masses when extrapolated to a chemically homogeneous lower mantle.

title: The solubility of NdPO 4 and DyPO 4 and stability of Nd and Dy chloride and hydroxyl complexes as a function of pH and salinity to 450 °C
description: Publication date: 1 October 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta, Volume 430 Author(s): Sarah E. Smith-Schmitz, Nicole C. Hurtig, Alexander P. Gysi, Daniel Harlov
abstract: The mobility of rare earth elements (REE) in geological systems is often controlled by the stability of monazite and xenotime, which are important hosts for the light and heavy REE. These REE phosphates constitute important resources and provide information on ore formation conditions and timing due to their uses as geothermometers and geochronometers. While the thermodynamic properties for these minerals are well-established up to high temperature and pressure, the properties for the aqueous REE complexes are not well constrained with limited information up to 300 °C. In this study, the solubility of synthetic NdPO4 and DyPO4 endmembers were measured in hydrothermal sub- to supercritical NaCl-bearing aqueous solutions from 350 at saturated water vapor pressure to 450 °C at 700 bar. The speciation of Nd and Dy was determined in acidic to alkaline solutions (pH25 °C values from 2 to 10), and indicates that the hydroxyl species REE(OH)2 + and REE(OH)3 0 predominate at low salinity (0.01 mol/kg NaCl) with some contribution of REE chloride species REECl2+ and REECl2 + in acidic fluids. The REE phosphate solubility measured in these experiments is up to two orders of magnitude higher than predicted using existing thermodynamic properties from literature for aqueous species extrapolated from lower temperature data to supercritical conditions. To address this discrepancy, the thermodynamic properties of the REE aqueous species were optimized using GEMSFITS to derive the formation constants for the REE chloride (β Cl) and hydroxyl (β OH) complexes in the studied temperature range. This study highlights the importance of the hydroxyl species REE(OH)2 + and REE(OH)3 0 over a wide range of pH and temperature. The revised thermodynamic properties for Dy and Nd chloride and hydroxyl species more accurately predict the solubility of NdPO4 and DyPO4 and provide insight into the speciation and mobility of the light and heavy REE in hydrothermal supercritical fluids in the crust.

title: Selenium isotope constraints on sediment–oceanic crust interaction during slab deserpentinization
description: Publication date: 1 October 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta, Volume 430 Author(s): Juan Muñoz-Alfaro, Stephan König, Claudio Marchesi, Romain Tilhac, María Isabel Varas-Reus, José Alberto Padrón-Navarta, Vicente López Sánchez-Vizcaíno, Ronny Schoenberg, Carlos J. Garrido
abstract: Arc magmas acquire their subduction-component signature through mantle-wedge metasomatism by slab-derived fluids and melts sourced in variable proportions from altered oceanic crust (AOC) and metasediments. At subarc depths, deserpentinization of slab mantle promotes this transfer by releasing large volumes of fluids that mobilize AOC- and sediment-derived components into the mantle-wedge source of arc volcanism. To constrain subarc fluid–rock interactions during slab deserpentinization, we present new selenium (Se) isotope data for rocks from the Cerro del Almirez ultramafic massif (Nevado–Filábride Complex, Betic Cordillera, southern Spain) formed in a subarc paleo-subduction setting. We report Se isotopes, radiogenic strontium (Sr) isotopes, and fluid-mobile element concentrations in metaserpentinites (antigorite-serpentinite), their subarc dehydration products (chlorite-harzburgite), interbedded metarodingites, and associated metasediments. Relative to the primitive mantle (δ 82/76Se = − 0.03 ± 0.07‰), metaserpentinites have heavier Se isotope compositions (with δ 82/76Se ranging from − 0.04 to + 0.99‰), whereas metaharzburgites are isotopically lighter (δ 82/76Se between − 0.80 and − 0.01‰). The lower δ 82/76Se values of metaharzburgites relative to metaserpentinites and primitive mantle cannot be attributed to magmatic inheritance, as magmatic processes do not fractionate Se isotopes. Similarly, variations in seafloor serpentinization degrees cannot account for the sharp isotopic shift observed. Decreasing δ 82/76Se with higher fluid-mobile element-to-Ce ratios and lower 87Sr/86Sr in metaharzburgites indicate equilibration with fluids derived from a mixed metasedimentary–AOC source during slab deserpentinization. To evaluate the relative roles of sediment-derived fluid infiltration and reaction with AOC within a deserpentinizing slab, we developed an open-system dehydration numerical model. The model indicates that open-system dehydration of a heterogeneous slab including metaserpentinites, AOC and metasediments produces fluids with AOC-like unradiogenic 87Sr/86Sr, and sediment-like light Se isotope compositions, thereby accounting for the trends observed in Cerro del Almirez metaharzburgites. These results imply that intra-slab reactive infiltration of sediment-derived fluids during deserpentinization of an AOC-bearing slab modulates the relative sediment–AOC contributions to subduction-zone fluids that flux the mantle-wedge source of primitive arc magmas.

title: The fragile memory of the early Earth: Decoding the Sm-Nd systematics in Eoarchean Greenland gneisses
description: Publication date: 1 October 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta, Volume 430 Author(s): J. Hammerli, A.I.S. Kemp, M.J. Whitehouse, M. Boyet, M.A. Kusiak, J.D. Vervoort, M.P. Roberts
abstract: Microanalytical studies have shown that Archean gneisses, which underwent high-grade metamorphism, record evidence for 147Sm-143Nd isotope disturbance on a mineral scale. This highlights the necessity to assess isotopic system integrity when interpreting Nd isotope data from metamorphosed Archean terranes in the context of crust-mantle evolution and geodynamic processes in the early Earth. Here, we apply an integrated whole-rock analysis and microanalytical approach to two ∼3.82 Ga Amitsôq tonalitic gneisses from a low-strain zone in southern West Greenland to test for 147Sm-143Nd isotope resetting and rare earth element (REE) mobility in comparatively less metamorphosed Eoarchean (≥3.6 Ga) rocks than those examined in previous studies. Both samples display distinctive whole rock Nd isotope signatures shared by other tonalitic gneisses from Greenland, with strongly positive μ142Nd values of +18 and +13, as well as superchondritic ε143Nd(3.82 Ga) values of +2.5 and +2.1. These characteristics have been interpreted to indicate a depleted mantle source that formed during the Hadean (>4.0 Ga). Zircon U-Pb populations indicate magmatic protolith ages at ∼3.82 Ga, but near-chondritic zircon εHf(3.82 Ga) values do not support derivation from a depleted mantle reservoir for the Lu-Hf system at that time. Allanite in both gneiss samples shows petrographic evidence for partial metamictization and migration of REE into cracks surrounding these grains. In situ 147Sm-143Nd data from allanite and apatite from both samples define linear arrays on an isochron diagram that imply equilibration at ∼2.7 Ga and possibly during older metamorphic events. These accessory minerals register the thermal effects of ∼2.7 Ga amphibolite facies metamorphism, causing open system processes at the mineral-scale and the breakdown of REE-bearing minerals. Our observations underscore the vulnerability of the 147Sm-143Nd isotope system to disturbance, even in early Archean meta-igneous rocks considered to be well preserved. The positive μ142Nd anomalies require Sm-Nd fractionation that also enhances production of radiogenic 143Nd. Because the Hf isotope signatures of the studied samples are chondritic and show no evidence for large-scale crust extraction, the positive μ142Nd values are interpreted as vestiges of early silicate differentiation, potentially linked to Hadean magma-ocean crystallization, rather than to voluminous extraction of continental crust from the ancient mantle. Mineral-scale evidence and poorly defined whole-rock Sm-Nd isochrons from the low-strain zone suggest that post-magmatic disturbance of the 147Sm-143Nd system can amplify Hf-Nd isotope decoupling and be misinterpreted as evidence for extensive crustal extraction.

title: Constraints of integrated Fe and Li isotopes on fractional crystallization and fluid-magma interaction in the formation of unzoned Li-mineralized pegmatites
description: Publication date: 1 October 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta, Volume 430 Author(s): Shuaijie Liu, Mona-Liza C. Sirbescu, Bin Chen, Wenjing Li, Mei-Fu Zhou
abstract: The roles of fractional crystallization and fluid–magma interaction in the genesis of unzoned Li-mineralized pegmatites remain debated. Because Fe and Li isotopes fractionate differently among melts, crystals, and fluids, their combined systematics offer a powerful means to discriminate between these processes. In this study, we report major and trace elemental and O, Fe and Li isotopic data for the Li-mineralized and barren pegmatites and associated leucogranites in the Ke’eryin field, Songpan–Ganzi orogenic belt, eastern Tibet. Lithium-mineralized pegmatites have TFe2O3, REE, and K/Rb lower than those in barren pegmatites, and both are lower than those in leucogranites. These correlations are consistent with origin of Li-mineralized pegmatites as products of more extreme fractional crystallization. Additionally, both Li-mineralized and barren pegmatites have stronger tetrad effects (TE1,3 > 1.1), lower Nb/Ta (< 5) and Zr/Hf (< 26) than leucogranites, indicating fluid involvement in their evolution. Both pegmatite types have δ56Fe values (0.13–0.20‰ and 0.00–0.28‰, respectively) similar to those of leucogranites (0.04–0.23‰). Lithium-mineralized pegmatites have δ7Li values (−0.8–+1.8‰ vs. −1.8–+1.9‰) similar to those of leucogranites, whereas barren pegmatites show higher δ7Li values (−1.5–+5.4‰). Nevertheless, both pegmatite types display a negative correlation between Li contents and δ7Li values. No correlation is observed between O and Fe isotopes or between O and Li isotopes in either Li-mineralized or barren pegmatites, indicating that external fluids and wallrocks did not modify their isotopic signatures. Our Rayleigh fractionation and fluid-melt mixing modelling demonstrate that fractional crystallization of granitic melts depletes Fe and enriches Li and increases δ56Fe and δ7Li values in the evolved melts. Fluid–magma interaction within melts decreases δ56Fe, resulting in similar δ56Fe values among Li-mineralized pegmatites, barren pegmatites, and leucogranites. This interaction also depletes Li but increases δ7Li, thus producing negative correlations between Li and δ7Li in pegmatites. The limited increase in δ7Li in Li-mineralized pegmatites during fractional crystallization would require extremely low partition coefficients for Li between fractionated phases and granitic melts. Such low partition coefficients can lead to significant enrichment of Li. Importantly, fluid-magma interaction may also explain the negative correlation between δ56Fe and δ7Li values observed in pegmatites based on currently available datasets, possibly indicative of a process of general significance. Our study demonstrates that even starting with initial Li-rich melts, extremely high degrees of fractional crystallization (fraction of remaining melt, F = 0.15) are needed for Li-mineralization. Such extreme fractional crystallization is facilitated by the presence of fluid and other fluxes (Li, B, F, and P) in viscous granitic melts. This study shows that combined Fe-Li isotopic systematics can effectively distinguish the effect of fluid-magma interaction from fractional crystallization during the formation and mineralization of unzoned pegmatites.

title: Calcium isotopic compositions of the lower continental crust estimated from lower-crustal xenoliths and Archean terrain
description: Publication date: 1 October 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta, Volume 430 Author(s): Huange Ren, Ganglan Zhang, Chunfei Chen, Lanping Feng, Zhenyi Liu, Frédéric Moynier, Yongsheng Liu
abstract: We present high-precision stable Ca isotope data for lower-crustal rocks from the North China Craton (NCC), including 29 granulite xenoliths and 9 granulites from Archean terrain, to constrain the behavior of Ca isotopes during lower-crustal processes and the Ca isotopic composition of the lower continental crust (LCC). These samples have a wide compositional range, from ultramafic to felsic (SiO2 content: 37.7 wt.% to 73.0 wt.%). Overall, the δ 44/40Ca values range from 0.08‰ to 1.26‰, whereas meta-igneous granulites exhibit limited δ 44/40Ca variation, with most values clustering between 0.65‰ and 0.92‰. In general, the δ 44/40Ca values display no correlation with H2O, 87Sr/86Sr, CaO/Al2O3, and Eu/Eu*, indicating negligible effects from fluid metasomatism, assimilation of Precambrian lower crust, or mineral accumulation. Intermediate-mafic granulite xenoliths show higher MREE/HREE ratios and lower δ 44/40Ca than Archean terrain granulites, which can be explained by the source mineralogy and residual garnet heterogeneity. Based on lower-crustal xenoliths hosted by Neogene basalts, the average LCC δ 44/40Ca is 0.71 ± 0.03‰ (2SE), which is slightly (∼0.13‰) lower than that of Mid-Ocean Ridge Basalt (MORB). In contrast, granulites from the Archean terrain yield a MORB-like average LCC δ 44/40Ca of 0.85 ± 0.03‰ (2SE), implying potential Ca isotopic evolution from the Archean to the Neogene. The slight difference between the LCC Ca isotope estimates is potentially related to the delamination of the lower-crustal fraction formed in the Archean, but sampling bias cannot yet be excluded. Further research with larger and more spatially constrained datasets is required to better constrain the role of delamination and crustal evolution using Ca isotopes.

title: Internal water and organic matter increase calcite clumped isotope reactivity
description: Publication date: 1 October 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta, Volume 430 Author(s): Zeyang Sun, Jingxiang Cheng, Sarbajit Banerjee, Ethan L. Grossman
abstract: Carbonate clumped isotope (Δ47) thermometry based on temperature-dependent 13C–18O bonding preference is widely applied from paleotemperature reconstruction to basin evolution analysis. Our confidence in these climate records depends on understanding Δ47 resetting rates at elevated temperatures through solid-state 13C–18O bond reordering and exchange with internal water and organic matter. However, the effects of water-bearing components on Δ47 reactivity remain poorly understood. Here, using optical calcite, stalagmite, and fossil and modern brachiopods, we show that Δ47 resetting is facilitated by high internal water and organic matter contents and slows with dehydration. Rates obtained for optical calcite and the fossil brachiopod are similar, confirming that dehydration and organic matter degradation of shells with taphonomic alteration ensure their suitability as paleoclimate archives. By considering the co-evolution of Δ47 reactivity and of internal water and organic matter in bio-carbonates, more accurate Δ47 temperatures can be produced helping to resolve debates surrounding temperatures during biodiversification of marine animal life (e.g., the Great Ordovician Biodiversification Event (GOBE)).

title: Hematite and siderite nanocrystals in ∼3.48 Ga Dresser Formation jaspilite: Implications for early atmospheric O 2 and CO 2
description: Publication date: 1 October 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta, Volume 430 Author(s): Tianyu Zhou, Huifang Xu, Seungyeol Lee, Eric E. Roden
abstract: Decoding the origin of Precambrian iron formations is essential for evaluating how these rocks record the evolution of early Earth’s surface environment. The ∼ 3.48 Ga jaspilite from Unit A3 of the lower Dresser Formation, Pilbara Craton, Western Australia, provides an exceptional insight to address this challenge based on the intimate association of redox-sensitive Fe(III) oxide (hematite) and Fe(II) carbonate (siderite). This study integrates petrographic observations and geochemical (PHREEQC) modeling to investigate the genesis of hematite and siderite embedded in chert. Nanoscale hematite crystals preserved within hematite-quartz clots formed through ferrihydrite dehydration with limited diagenetic overprinting. Their nanoscale morphology and the absence of relict Fe(II)-silicate (greenalite) precursors support an early authigenic origin rather than secondary oxidation. Two distinct siderite populations in the most Fe-rich jasper layers—partially dissolved crystals left within euhedral micron-scale voids and intact nanoscale rhombs sealed within chert—reflect two different recrystallization stages based on their spatial relationship with hematite-quartz clots. We propose that Dresser Unit A3 jaspilite formed during episodic hydrothermal discharges delivering dissolved Fe-Si, represented by Fe(H3SiO4)2 as a working aqueous metal complex supply, accompanied by abundant seawater/hydrothermal silica input, where comparable rates of Fe(II) oxidation and its combination with dissolved inorganic carbon promoted the simultaneous crystallization of ferrihydrite and siderite, followed by silica gel precipitation. PHREEQC geochemical simulations show that the observed coexistence of siderite and ferrihydrite with plausible Fe-Si source requires CO2-rich conditions (pCO2 ≈ 0.1–0.2 atm) and trace but non-negligible oxygen (pO2 ≈ 10−6 atm), indicating a transient redox state capturing the coprecipitation of Fe(II) and Fe(III) phases. Electrostatic attraction between oppositely charged ferrihydrite and silica nanoparticles promoted micron-scale colloidal aggregation, later preserved through diagenesis as ∼30 μm hematite–quartz clots. These findings indicate a narrow window of early Archean regional pO2 – pCO2 conditions governing Fe-Si-C-O interplay on Earth’s surface. Our calculated relatively high pO2 level suggests that the Dresser Formation may record one of Earth’s earliest local “whiffs of oxygen” through oxygenic photosynthesis and tectonic oxygen production long before the first major worldwide rise in atmospheric oxygen during the Great Oxidation Event.

title: Global control of riverine U isotopes by source and weathering processes
description: Publication date: 1 October 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta, Volume 430 Author(s): Quentin Charbonnier, Julien Bouchez, Jérôme Gaillardet, Robert G. Hilton, Edward T. Tipper, Derek Vance
abstract: The use of marine sedimentary uranium isotopes (δ238U) to investigate past variability in the redox state of the ocean–atmosphere system rests on a robust quantification of the riverine U isotope flux, the dominant U input to the ocean. However, there is no consensus on the relative importance of lithology versus fractionation during weathering in controlling the riverine U isotope flux to the ocean. Here we report the riverine dissolved and solid uranium isotope composition from fourteen of the world’s largest rivers, integrating lithologies and processes relevant at the global scale, which we compare with data from the literature. The riverine dissolved δ238U ranges from −0.47 to 0.08‰, while the solids range from −0.65 to −0.24‰. Collectively, our results indicate a dominant control by weathering processes on the global riverine U isotope flux, with the notable exception of the Mackenzie Basin. No relationship emerges between riverine dissolved U isotope and lithological tracers. Whilst river solid U isotope variability reflects different relative contributions from erosion of silicate versus organic-rich sedimentary rocks, most large rivers lie close to the silicate erosion end member, and mass balance calculations indicate that silicate rock weathering can explain the total riverine U isotope flux. In this view, elemental and isotope partitioning of U between the riverine dissolved and solid loads suggests a dominant control by weathering processes that fractionate U isotopes. This interpretation is supported by the relationship between the fraction of U remaining in solution following secondary mineral formation during weathering and riverine U isotope signatures. Finally, a complex pattern emerges between climate and U isotope fractionation and weathering intensity. However, based on data collected so far, the U isotope system appears analogous to lithium isotopes, whereby moderate weathering intensity leads to the largest shift in river dissolved load δ238U values under optimal conditions for U incorporation into secondary minerals.

title: Hydrogen in nominally anhydrous minerals from equilibrated ordinary chondrites and implications for the water budget of their parent bodies
description: Publication date: 1 October 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta, Volume 430 Author(s): S. Desikamani, L.D. Peterson, M.E. Newcombe, C.M.O’D. Alexander, J. Wang, R.D. Ash, S.G. Nielsen, P.M. Piccoli, E.S. Bullock
abstract: Nucleosynthetic isotope signatures indicate that the Earth is predominantly made from inner solar system non-carbonaceous (NC) materials. However, a major uncertainty in models of water addition to the proto-Earth is the extent to which H (calculated in this study as µg/g H2O, but present as H-bearing species) in nominally anhydrous minerals (NAMs) from NC materials could contribute to the bulk Earth water budget. The preserved water concentration of NC meteorite NAMs may also shape our understanding of processes occurring in the solar protoplanetary disk (e.g., implantation of H on the surfaces of NAM grains) and in planetesimals (e.g., metamorphism in chondrite parent bodies). Reported water contents for NAMs from the ordinary chondrites (OCs), the dominant NC material falling to Earth today, range between 100-104 µg/g H2O. In order to better constrain the potential contribution of ordinary chondrites to the Earth’s water budget we have measured water concentrations in NAMs from eight equilibrated OCs, six of which have not previously been investigated for water, and two of which (Chelyabinsk and Bensour) were previously measured in other laboratories. We find that olivine and low-Ca pyroxene from equilibrated OCs contain less than ∼10 µg/g H2O. Based on these measurements, the water content of the NAM fraction of equilibrated OCs is < 10 µg/g H2O (a factor of over 60–120 lower than prior estimates). Combining these constraints of equilibrated OC NAM water contents with published measurements of NAMs and glassy mesostases from unequilibrated OCs, we estimate that NAMs and glass in OC parent bodies could have delivered no more than ∼0.2 ocean masses of water to Earth (∼1% of an assumed total water budget of ∼18 ocean masses). Additional water could have been delivered from phyllosilicates and organics in the most primitive OC material that is not considered in our modeling. The difference in NAM water concentrations obtained here relative to some prior studies may be rooted in analytical artifacts associated with their nanoscale secondary ion mass spectrometric measurements.

title: Shock-induced hydrogen-isotope modification in apatite from the Martian meteorite Los Angeles
description: Publication date: 1 October 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta, Volume 430 Author(s): E. Dobrică, J.P. Greenwood, A.N. Krot, A.J. Brearley, E.P. Vicenzi, S. Itoh, N. Sakamoto, H. Yurimoto
abstract: Hydrogen isotopes in apatite are widely used to constrain the origin and evolution of water in Martian magmas and crustal reservoirs. However, the extent to which shock metamorphism modifies hydrogen-isotope compositions in apatites is poorly understood. In this study, we combine scanning electron microscopy (SEM), cathodoluminescence (CL), transmission electron microscopy (TEM) observations, and secondary ion mass spectrometry (SIMS) measurements of hydrogen isotopes and water contents in apatites from the Martian meteorite Los Angeles. Panchromatic CL imaging reveals distinct bright and dark domains within individual apatite grains. These domains correlate with variations in hydrogen-isotope composition, chlorine abundance, and shock metamorphic microstructures (dislocations, planar fractures, and shock-induced melting) observed at the nanoscale. Bright CL regions show higher defect densities, more abundant melt pockets, lower chlorine contents, and elevated δD values relative to dark CL regions. Defect density correlates positively with δD and melt pocket abundance but shows no systematic relationship with bulk H2O content. These observations demonstrate that hydrogen-isotope modification can occur in heavily deformed apatite without requiring complete melting or recrystallization. Shock-induced defects therefore provide pathways for hydrogen redistribution and isotopic exchange at the micron scale. The results indicate that shock metamorphism can locally modify primary hydrogen isotope signatures in Martian meteorites while preserving bulk water contents within the typical Martian apatite range. Cathodoluminescence imaging provides a rapid and non-destructive method for identifying apatite domains that can correlate with deformation-enhanced and isotopically-modified regions. These findings have important implications for interpreting Martian volatile reservoirs and for future sample-return missions such as Martian Moons eXploration (MMX).

title: Origin of nucleosynthetic isotope variability in the NC reservoir: Evidence from Ti, Cr, and Mo isotopes
description: Publication date: 1 October 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta, Volume 430 Author(s): Elias Wölfer, Christoph Burkhardt, Gerrit Budde, Christian A. Jansen, Jonas Pape, Thorsten Kleine
abstract: Nucleosynthetic isotope anomalies allow distinguishing between non-carbonaceous (NC) and carbonaceous (CC) type meteorites, and have revealed correlated isotope variations especially among NC bodies. Understanding the origin of this NC trend is important for identifying the processes that produced the NC isotope heterogeneity, and for using these isotope anomalies to reconstruct the early evolution of the solar protoplanetary disk. We report mass-independent Ti, Cr, and Mo isotope compositions for a comprehensive set of previously not or only poorly investigated meteorites, as well as acid leachates obtained from the sequential digestion of primitive ordinary chondrites. Some of the samples investigated in this study fill previously identified apparent gaps in the NC trend, suggesting these gaps reflect unrepresentative sampling of a more continuous isotopic trend. Bulk meteorites and leachates exhibit distinct isotope systematics, indicating that the NC isotope variability does not reflect selective thermal processing of presolar carriers in the disk. The NC trend also cannot reflect the continuous addition of CC dust from the outer to the inner disk, because early- and late-formed NC meteorites display largely overlapping isotopic compositions. Instead, we find that the NC isotope heterogeneity is best accounted for by fractionation and mixing among chemically and isotopically distinct dust components, similar to the processes that produced the isotopic variability among carbonaceous chondrites. On this basis we argue for the presence of substructures in the inner disk, which facilitated fractionation and mixing among distinct dust components, and helped preserve a long-lived dust reservoir from which NC planetesimals accreted over an extended period of time.

title: Fluorine and chlorine abundances in carbonatite melts and implications for REE-enrichment
description: Publication date: 1 October 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta, Volume 430 Author(s): Haihao Guo, Fabrice Gaillard, Saskia Erdmann, Zineb Nabyl, Johann Tuduri, Xiaochun Li
abstract: Carbonatites are enriched in halogens and S, and can host rare earth element (REE) and high field strength element (HFSE, e.g., Nb, Zr) deposits. Yet, the role of volatiles like fluorine (F), chlorine (Cl), and sulfur (S) in the fractionation of the carbonatite magmas and in the enrichment of their metals remain underexplored. Here, we use previously published experimental data (1) on F, Cl, S and REE partitioning between apatite and carbonatite melt; (2) use the composition of apatite from natural carbonatites to characterize the F, Cl and S contents in the coexisting melts; and (3) weigh the role of F in driving REE enrichment during carbonatite magma differentiation. In combination with previous studies, we show that the partitioning coefficients of fluorine, chlorine, and sulfur between apatite and carbonatite melt are respectively DF = 0.97 ± 0.36; DCl = 0.14 ± 0.11; and DS = 0.031 ± 0.012, across a wide range of pressures (200–800 MPa) and temperatures (725–1050 °C) and for a range of carbonatite melt compositions. Furthermore, our findings indicate no significant influence of melt F, Cl, and S concentration on the partitioning of REE between apatite and carbonatite melt. Using these partitioning constraints combined with > 700 magmatic apatite compositions from carbonatites, we estimate an average of ∼3.1 ± 1.3 wt% F and ∼0.30 ± 0.31 wt% Cl in carbonatite melts, and show that F-rich carbonatite melts do not necessarily have higher REE concentrations. Sufficient compositional data for natural apatite from carbonatites that permit a quantitative assessment of the effect of melt Cl and S concentrations on REE fractionation do not exist. We therefore posit that the degree of REE enrichment in carbonatite rocks is not primarily controlled by melt F concentrations, but may be inherited from the lithospheric mantle sources, can result from immiscibility of variably differentiated alkaline magmas, or involve concentration by hydrothermal fluids.

title: Sedimentary constraints on pelagic iron removal across the low-latitude Pacific
description: Publication date: 1 October 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta, Volume 430 Author(s): Zheyuan Zhang, Jianfan Zheng, Xuefa Shi, Weiqiang Li, Yanguang Liu, Jiahui Liu, Zhimian Cao, Tao Li, Tianyu Chen
abstract: Iron (Fe) is a crucial micronutrient that limits primary production over broad regions of the global ocean. While the external Fe inputs to the ocean have been increasingly constrained, the quantitative removal flux of Fe from the water column to the pelagic sediments remains incompletely understood, particularly in the open ocean. The low-latitude Pacific encompasses diverse hydrographic and sedimentary environments, making it a representative region for tracing Fe removal from the deep ocean. In this study, we performed Fe speciation, Fe isotope and burial flux analyses using near core-top sediments from multiple sediment cores recovered across the low-latitude Pacific, partly overlapping with the GEOTRACES GP16 transect. Our results show these sediments could effectively record Fe inputs from the Peru margin, hydrothermal vents, and Asian dust. Specifically, we identified differing Fe speciation, Fe and manganese (Mn) flux as well as δ56Fe of both reactive Fe and bulk sediment that are related to the different sedimentary provinces. In the low-latitude Pacific, δ56Fe of the acid leached reactive Fe species agree well with those of the labile particulate Fe species within the water column of the GP16 transect and the core-top hydrogenic ferromanganese crusts, suggesting the reactive Fe of these sediments represents the sink of the dissolved Fe pool in the deep ocean. Manganese essentially associates with the reactive fraction and shows highly positive correlation with reactive Fe content. Within the east region influenced by hydrothermal venting originating from the Eastern Pacific Rise (EPR), the proportion of reactive Fe oxides is higher, reaching up to 53%. The reactive δ56Fe in this region is as low as −0.5‰, implying a light Fe isotope signature from the hydrothermal endmember and consistent with modern water column studies. Sediment samples outside this hydrothermal zone show “background” Fe sedimentation flux and isotope signatures, pointing toward the influence of non-reductive dissolution from the West Pacific arcs/Asian dust and reductive dissolution from Peru margin. The scavenging residence time of dissolved Fe in the water column estimated by the reactive Fe burial flux in this region is only a few years to a few decades, indicating rapid turnover of Fe in the open ocean. Our study thus offers novel insights into the oceanic Fe sources-sink processes and could help improve biogeochemical models toward a better representation of the oceanic Fe cycle.

title: Nanoscale chemistry of magnetite framboids in the tarda meteorite: a proxy for fluid chemistry
description: Publication date: Available online 23 September 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): B.J.K. Wilson, G.A. Arcuri, T. Casagrande, C.M. Andrei, B. Langelier, K.T. Tait, M.G. Daly
abstract: Tarda is a C2-ungrouped carbonaceous chondrite that preserves a record of low-temperature aqueous alteration on its parent asteroid. While the original fluid has disappeared, constraining its composition is essential for understanding the chemical environment that influenced both secondary mineral formation and prebiotic organic chemistry. Magnetite framboids are an abundant aqueous alteration product in Tarda and likely recorded some of the chemical species from its mother solution, entrained within the framboidal magnetite grain boundaries. To investigate this, we conducted a nanoscale study on five magnetite framboids using transmission electron microscopy, energy dispersive x-ray spectroscopy, and atom probe tomography. Magnetite framboids in Tarda exhibit a wide range of textures, crystallite sizes, and packing arrangements, reflecting a progressive sequence of discrete nucleation and growth events likely occurring in isolated water droplets. Energy dispersive x-ray spectroscopy analysis of four interacting framboids reveals trace element enrichments of mostly Ti and Si along ∼5 nm thick grain boundaries, with the strongest enrichments observed in the framboids with smaller crystallites, which likely precipitated at the beginning and end of the local precipitation sequence. Using atom probe tomography, we captured a ∼5 nm thick planar feature enriched in trace abundances of Na, Mg, Ca, Mn, and Si, likely corresponding to a magnetite boundary. These findings suggest that magnetite framboids in Tarda formed from a generally alkaline fluid that contained a diverse suite of cations and evolved as water–rock interaction progressed. While the fluid composition inferred here resembles alkaline, metal-containing fluids known to promote organic synthesis on Earth, experimental work is needed to determine how such conditions could influence complex organic synthesis in asteroid environments.

title: Mercury isotopes in coral skeletons as proxies for marine Hg cycling: assessing fidelity and fractionation during biomineralization
description: Publication date: Available online 23 September 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Fei Cao, Yongquan Zhang, Ruoyu Sun, Larissa Schneider, Songjing Li, Rui Zhang, Pengfei Li, Wang Zheng, Jiubin Chen, Yi Liu
abstract: Stable mercury (Hg) isotopes provide powerful tools for tracing marine Hg sources and transformations. However, suitable geological archives that record long-term changes in seawater Hg isotopes remain scarce, limiting reconstructions of past marine Hg cycling. Here, we evaluate the potential of coral skeletons as archives of seawater Hg isotope compositions and assess the mechanisms controlling Hg incorporation during coral calcification. We systematically investigate the effectiveness and isotopic impacts of chemical cleaning protocols designed to isolate aragonite-bound Hg in coral skeletons. Sequential leaching and oxidative soaking experiments demonstrate that a substantial fraction of Hg in untreated coral skeletons is associated with non-aragonitic phases, primarily organic matter, and can be efficiently removed by optimized oxidative cleaning. These treatments result in large decreases in Hg concentrations and systematic changes in mass-dependent fractionation (MDF; δ202Hg), while mass-independent fractionation (MIF; Δ199Hg and Δ200Hg) signatures remain invariant. This indicates that cleaning selectively affects MDF without altering source-diagnostic MIF signals. Applying the optimized cleaning protocol, we analyze Hg concentrations and isotope compositions in coral skeletons collected from nearshore and offshore environments in the South China Sea. Coral skeletons preserve distinct regional differences in Hg MIF, which are consistent with published regional seawater values, reflecting contrasting contributions from atmospheric and terrestrial Hg sources. In contrast, δ202Hg values are consistently more negative than seawater by approximately 1 ‰, indicating systematic MDF during skeletal incorporation, likely driven by biologically mediated kinetic effects associated with calcification. Our results suggest that coral skeletons generally preserve seawater Hg MIF signatures while exhibiting predictable MDF during biomineralization. These findings establish coral skeletons as promising archives for reconstructing long-term changes in marine Hg cycling in response to natural variability and anthropogenic perturbations.

title: Diagenetic fluid overprinting of micrite stable isotopes: implications for paleo-elevation reconstruction
description: Publication date: Available online 23 September 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Keran Li, Anlin Ma, Xiumian Hu, Chaojin Lu, Yoseph Datu Adiatma, Lin Li, Ardiansyah Koeshidayatullah, He Zhang, Di Yang, Zhiwu Li
abstract: Lacustrine carbonate micrite is commonly treated as a reliable archive of surface-water oxygen isotopes and is widely used for paleo-elevation reconstruction in orogenic belts. However, recent evidence for shallow-burial dolomitization in lacustrine micrites raises concern that bulk sample may not preserve a single primary signal. Here we evaluate the fidelity of geochemical signals preserved in the micritic carbonates of the Eocene Gerze Basin in central Tibet. The geochemical compositions of calcite and dolomite fractions in bulk samples were isolated using sequential acetic-acid leaching and show one primary or least altered calcite end-member (Calcite EM) and two diagenetic dolomite end-members (Dolomite EM1 and EM2). Numerical simulation suggests that the higher and more variable δ 44/40Ca values in Dolomite EM2 formed under fluid-buffered conditions. In contrast, Dolomite EM1, with moderately positive δ 44/40Ca values, is a product of sediment-buffered dolomitization. Accounting for this diagenetic alteration, each 10 % increase in the proportion of Dolomite EM2 in bulk carbonates would increase the reconstructed paleo-elevation by 0.5–0.8 km. These results show that Gerze Basin micrite is not a homogeneous recorder of lake-water δ18O and that unrecognized dolomitization can substantially bias paleo-elevation reconstructions.

title: Resolving edge-site specificity of Zn sorption on montmorillonite and pyrophyllite: insights from Zn isotope fractionation
description: Publication date: Available online 22 September 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Duan Yiren, He Hongtao, Shichao An, Wei Li, Lu Xiancai
abstract: Clay minerals are major reservoirs of zinc (Zn) at Earth’s surface and exert strong control on Zn geochemical cycling through sorption reactions. However, distinguishing among structurally distinct Zn sorption environments remains challenging at heterogeneous mineral surfaces. This challenge is particularly relevant to 2:1 phyllosilicates, where permanent-charge sites, interlayer domains, and chemically heterogeneous edge sites can contribute simultaneously to Zn sorption. Here, we combine Zn isotope measurements with X-ray absorption fine structure (XAFS) spectroscopy and ab initio density functional theory calculations to constrain Zn sorption structures on montmorillonite and pyrophyllite. Zn isotope fractionation varies systematically with pH and ionic strength, consistent with shifts in the dominant sorption environment. Sorption at cation-exchange sites produces negligible isotope fractionation (Δ66Znsorbed-aqueous ≈ 0‰), whereas edge-site sorption yields large positive fractionation (Δ66Znsorbed-aqueous = +0.43‰ to + 0.48‰). XAFS links this shift to a transition from aqueous-like outer-sphere Zn to inner-sphere Zn with shorter Zn–O bonds and tetrahedral-like coordination at clay edges, but cannot uniquely identify the responsible edge functionality. Density functional theory calculations predict distinct isotope fractionations among candidate complexes: −0.20‰ for terminal ≡SiO-bound octahedral Zn, +0.06‰ to + 0.08‰ for octahedral Al-associated configurations, and large positive values for tetrahedral Zn associated with aluminol (+0.89‰) and Al–O–Si bridging sites (+0.90‰). Combined with XAFS, these results constrain the plausible edge structures to tetrahedral Zn in Al-associated environments, although the relative contributions of aluminol- and Al–O–Si bridging-associated complexes cannot be uniquely resolved. These results indicate that Zn isotope fractionation, integrated with XAFS and atomistic calculations, provides a complementary means of discriminating among plausible metal complexes at heterogeneous mineral surfaces.

title: Temperature-dependent Fe(II) thresholds for magnetite formation during Fe(II)-catalyzed ferrihydrite transformation
description: Publication date: Available online 21 September 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Jiahao Chen, Anhuai Lu, Yuefei Ding, Qishun Sun, Liao Chang, Anxu Sheng, Yurong Deng, Shan Huang, Yongheng Jiang, Yoshio Takahashe, Xinglan Cui, Liuqin Huang, Juan Liu
abstract: Fe(II)-catalyzed ferrihydrite (Fh) transformation is a critical process controlling secondary Fe mineral formation, Fe redox reactivity, and the cycling of associated nutrients and trace elements in anoxic and suboxic environments. Although aqueous Fe(II) (Fe(II)aq) availability is known to regulate Fh transformation pathways, the critical Fe(II)aq concentration required for magnetite (Mt) formation at different temperatures remains poorly understood. Here, we investigated Fe(II)-catalyzed Fh transformation at 25, 45, and 65 °C under anoxic, circumneutral pH conditions across a range of initial Fe(II)aq concentrations. Time-resolved analyses of mineral phases, Fe(II) speciation, particle morphology, and magnetic properties were combined with thermodynamic calculations to determine how temperature regulates transformation kinetics, pathway selection, and Mt formation. Increasing temperature significantly reduced the apparent Fe(II)aq threshold for Mt formation, from > 10.0 mM at 25 °C to 0.6–0.8 mM at 45 °C and 0.3–0.4 mM at 65 °C. Mineralogical evolution followed a two-stage pathway: rapid Fh dissolution and accumulation of lepidocrocite (Lp) and goethite (Gt) during Stage I, followed by Lp consumption and competitive partitioning between Gt growth and Mt formation during Stage II. Elevated temperature shifted the dominant Stage II pathway from template-directed Gt growth toward Lp-to-Mt conversion, changing the overall pathway from Fh → Lp/Gt → Gt to Fh → Lp/Gt → Mt/Gt. Thermodynamic calculations further showed that Stage I nucleation barriers favored Lp and Gt over direct Mt formation, whereas during Stage II, higher temperature enhanced the nucleation driving force and lowered the nucleation barrier for Lp-to-Mt conversion, while the corresponding thermodynamic parameters for Lp-to-Gt conversion remained nearly unchanged. Fe(II) speciation further showed that higher temperatures promoted Fe(II) adsorption and structural Fe(II) incorporation, facilitating the formation of mixed-valence Mt. The delayed appearance of Mt after Lp accumulation, together with rapid Lp consumption and enhanced Fe(II) incorporation, indicates that temperature-promoted Mt formation proceeds mainly through dissolution-reprecipitation rather than direct Fh-to-Mt solid-state conversion or oriented-attachment-dominated growth. The resulting Mt particles displayed temperature-dependent morphological and magnetic characteristics. These findings demonstrate that moderate warming expands the Fe(II)aq window for Mt formation by altering both the thermodynamic accessibility and kinetic competition of secondary mineralization pathways, providing new constraints for predicting Fe mineral phase selection in thermally dynamic biogeochemical environments

title: From source to sink: complex dual role of the Kairei hydrothermal plume in deep ocean trace metal cycling at the Central Indian Ridge
description: Publication date: Available online 21 September 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Nico Fröhberg, Katja Schmidt, Sandra Poehle, Ignacio Pedre, Maren Walter, Jonathan Mette, Sebastian Fuchs, Dieter Garbe-Schönberg, Charlotte Kleint, Andrea Koschinsky
abstract: Hydrothermal venting represents a significant source of trace metals to the deep ocean, but key aspects of these fluxes remain poorly constrained. Whether high-temperature hydrothermal venting at a particular site represents a net source for fluid-sourced trace metals to the open ocean is determined by complex processes during plume mixing, which can also make them sinks for (seawater-derived) elements. We present a comprehensive dataset of dissolved trace metals (Cd, Co, Cu, Fe, Ga, Mn, Mo, Ni, Pb, U, V, and REY) for endmember fluids and from water column profiles covering the buoyant plume and the non-buoyant plume up to 30 km away from the mixed ultramafic/mafic-hosted Kairei Hydrothermal Field (KHF) at the Central Indian Ridge and a background station at 56 km distance. The non-buoyant plume was sampled with a newly developed autonomous trace metal rosette (TMR) for contamination-free hydrocasts. The KHF acts as a significant source of Fe, Mn, Co, and to a lesser degree of Ga to the deep Indian Ocean, with size fractionation revealing Fe being present predominantly as small particles (53 % at 0.2–0.8 µm) and large colloids (28 % at 0.015–0.2 µm) which are removed quickly near the source, while the soluble fraction (<0.015 µm) is more stable and exported to the deep ocean. Similarly, Pb was found to be largely present in the small particulate fraction (95 %) close to the source and being rapidly removed as particulate sulfides with little effect on dissolved concentrations, while all other investigated elements were found largely in the soluble fraction (<0.015 µm). Conversely, the plume effectively scavenges REY, V, and notably Cd from the water column as well as the fluid-sourced contributions, with near-quantitative Cd removal observed in the plume despite ∼100-fold endmember enrichment. Copper and Ni exhibit complex non-conservative behavior, both being depleted relative to background seawater in the near-field, likely reflecting initial sulfide precipitation; Cu is subsequently re-enriched in the far-field via oxidative release during plume aging, while any comparable Ni release likely falls below our detection limit given its lower endmember concentration, making the plume an apparent net sink for Ni. The relatively low H2S/Fe ratio of 0.90 at Kairei compared to other hydrothermal systems likely favors greater metal transport to the water column. These findings demonstrate that hydrothermal contributions to marine trace metal budgets are highly system-specific, controlled by endmember chemistry and plume processes, highlighting the need for detailed multi-element investigations across diverse hydrothermal settings.

title: Metal complexions in growth-related crystal defects in pyrite
description: Publication date: Available online 20 September 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Lin Yang, Qingfei Wang, Denis Fougerouse, Steven M. Reddy, Huajian Li, Kunfeng Qiu, Qihai Shu, William D.A. Rickard, Yiwei Song, Paul Guagliardo, David W. Saxey, Chaoyi Dong, Yushan Zeng, Xiao Sun, Jun Deng
abstract: Element segregation into crystal defects formed during mineral growth rather than post-growth deformation is of fundamental interest in earth science but remains poorly understood. The micro-, to nano-scale textures and geochemical composition of pyrite from a gold deposit were studied to elucidate crystal defect-mediated element segregation. The pyrite consists of a core and a rim, with tetrahedrite inclusions distributed between the two. Our findings reveal a series of planar defects (with low angle misorientation >0.3°) consistent with plane in the pyrite rim. The characteristics of the defects indicate that they are nucleated due to the lattice mismatch during overgrowth of pyrite on the tetrahedrite. Nanoscale observations indicate the presence of a separate interstitial Sb–Cu-bearing inclusion along the planar and linear crystal defects. The interstitial inclusion has a cubic crystal structure and is enriched in Au and other trace elements like Ni, Cu, Sb, Pb, and Bi, with a combined concentrations reaching 8.6 at.%. Such composition cannot be attributed to any definitive mineral phase and is thus interpreted as phase-like, stable complexions. The thermodynamic modelling reveals that the pyrite with trace element-bearing defects formed at ∼250 °C under pH of 3.8 to 4.6 and logfO2 of –36.0 to –31.8 conditions. Lack of visible Au within the studied pyrite indicates that Au was segregated into these complexions from undersaturated ore fluids, revealing a growth-related, defect-driven incorporation mechanism of Au. These tetrahedrite and metal-rich complexions may act as a precursor for the Au nanoparticles or other sulfide inclusions in pyrite during superposed deformation and mineralization. This study highlights that the role of the growth-induced defects in the element segregation may be underestimated in previous studies

title: The role of sediments in calc-alkaline differentiation of thickened arc magmas and bulk crust compositions
description: Publication date: Available online 18 September 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Jun Wang, Chris J. Hawkesworth, Qiang Wang, Peng Sun, Wan-Long Hu, Shaohao Zou
abstract: Calc-alkaline magmas in thickened arcs (>45 km) are characterized by ultra iron (Fe) depletion, having lower FeO contents at a given MgO content than those in thinner arcs, and this is a feature of bulk continental crust. Previous interpretations of ultra-Fe depletion have focused on closed-system differentiation of mantle-derived magmas, but magmatic flare-ups during crustal thickening result in ultra-Fe depletion in open systems incorporating fertile crustal materials from retroarc underthrusting. We evaluate ultra-Fe depletion in a garnet-bearing magmatic flare-up in the Tethyan arc and a global database of arc lavas and arclogitic garnets with thermodynamic-geochemical modeling. Our case study shows that thickened arc magmas undergo sediment assimilation and garnet crystallization at ∼1 GPa. The important role of sediment assimilation in thickened arc magmas is further supported by global Sr–Nd–O isotopic data. Magma differentiation at relatively shallow depths (<45 km or 1.2 GPa) is essential for reproducing the range of Dy/Yb and La/Yb ratios observed in global thickened arc magmas, because it suppresses early garnet crystallization and limits the extent of late garnet crystallization. The late crystallization of minor amounts of garnet (<5 wt%) from low-MgO (<4 wt%) magmas exerts little effect on magma oxidation. The lack of early garnet crystallization indicates that garnet has no bearing on the early Fe depletion in high-MgO magmas. At depths of <45 km, assimilated felsic rather than more mafic sediments, would have lower densities than the basaltic magma, and this low-density sediment barrier confines magma stagnation and differentiation to this depth interval. Integrating previous interpretations of the tectono-magmatic cyclicity in Cordilleran arcs, we propose that felsic sediments were underthrust into the deep crust during crustal thickening, thereby fueling flare-ups of ultra-Fe-depleted magmas. These felsic sediments may represent residues left after the loss of mafic components from ancient retroarc continents due to prolonged chemical weathering. Our results highlight that intracrustal recycling of highly weathered, felsic sediments provides a significant control on the development of ultra-Fe-depleted calc-alkaline magmas in thickened arcs, emphasizing the role of weathering in the generation of bulk continental crust

title: Multiple lithium sites in kaolinite revealed by high-resolution 7 Li nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy and density functional theory (DFT) calculations
description: Publication date: Available online 16 September 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Yan Wang, Shifeng Dai, David French, Ian Graham, Yu Liu
abstract: Lithium (Li) is a critical metal resource underpinning the development of the new energy sector and constitutes an essential material basis for green technologies such as Li-ion batteries, energy storage systems, and electric vehicles. As the global energy system accelerates towards decarbonization, the strategic importance of Li resources and market demand continue to increase. Clay-hosted Li in coal-bearing strata has therefore attracted increasing attention as a potentially important Li reservoir. Here, we combine high-resolution 7Li magic-angle spinning nuclear magnetic resonance (7Li MAS NMR) spectroscopy with density functional theory (DFT) calculations to resolve the local environments and migration characteristics of Li in natural kaolinite from Li-enriched coal-bearing strata. The experimental 7Li MAS NMR spectra first revealed multiple distinguishable Li local environments in the natural kaolinite-bearing samples. However, because spectral deconvolution alone cannot uniquely determine the corresponding crystallographic sites, representative Li-bearing kaolinite configurations were independently constructed according to the crystal structure of kaolinite, available structural sites, Li–O coordination requirements, charge-compensation considerations, and crystal-chemical plausibility. These configurations include octahedral substitutional Li ( L i s u b ), interlayer and siloxane-hole-related Li ( L i i n t and L i h o l e ), and several defect complexes ( L i s u b + i n t , L i s u b + h o l e , L i i n t + h o l e , L i s u b + i n t + h o l e , L i s u b + 2 H ). DFT calculations were then performed to evaluate their relative binding energies, local coordination environments, migration barriers, and isotropic chemical shifts. The experimental 7Li MAS NMR spectra and peak deconvolution results were subsequently used to constrain the interpretation of the theoretically predicted Li local environments through a three-band calibration scheme spanning low-, intermediate-, and high-shift regions. The combined spectroscopic and computational results indicate that Li is predominantly hosted at octahedral substitutional sites, which define the principal Li reservoir and are characterized by low chemical shifts, strong shielding, and a relatively stable lattice framework. A smaller but spectroscopically resolvable fraction of Li occurs in interlayer/siloxane-hole-related environments and associated defect complexes, generating intermediate- to high-shift components that reflect structurally perturbed local environments governed by multisite coupling. DFT-derived migration pathways further suggest that L i s u b is the most stable and least mobile Li configuration, whereas L i i n t and L i h o l e -related environments represent subordinate configurations subject to distinct energetic and kinetic constraints. These results establish a lattice-scale framework for understanding Li storage and local migration in kaolinite from coal-bearing strata and provide new constraints on Li occurrence mechanisms and resource potential in clay-rich coal systems.

title: Microbial substrate formation via thermal alteration of organic matter in sediments of the Nankai Trough
description: Publication date: Available online 16 September 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Victoria Kürzinger, Verena B. Heuer, Christian T. Hansen, Wolfgang Bach, Shuchai Gan, Kai-Uwe Hinrichs
abstract: Deep marine sediments play a critical role in global biogeochemical cycles, serving as a vast reservoir of organic carbon. Carbon turnover in these environments is governed by biotic and abiotic processes, with high temperatures promoting the latter. To determine the upper temperature limit of life in the deep biosphere, it is necessary to distinguish between thermal limits and energy constrains. Although microorganisms are known to be able to survive at the putative temperature limit of up to 122°C, it remains unclear whether this is due to a fundamental temperature limit or to insufficient in-situ productions of metabolic substrates at higher temperatures. In particular, the temperature dependence of abiotic formation of low-molecular-weight organic compounds, which are important substrates for microbial metabolism, is essentially unknown. To investigate the abiotic formation of low-molecular-weight substrates and their implications for carbon cycling in organic-poor sediments, we conducted hydrous pyrolysis experiments under high-pressure (25 MPa) and high-temperature (150‒250°C) conditions. A sediment sample from International Ocean Discovery Program Site C0023 in the Nankai Trough was chosen for the experiments (i.e., 88°C, see “Materials and Methods”), where in-situ temperatures reach 120°C at 1.2 km sediment depth. The experimental approach was combined with geochemical analyses followed by thermodynamic modeling to rate the abiotic formation of low-molecular-weight organics as potential substrates for microbial metabolism under high-pressure and high-temperature conditions. Experimental results revealed elevated concentrations of dissolved inorganic carbon and hydrogen relative to in-situ porewaters. In contrast, acetate and CH4 concentrations remained below those measured in genuine porewater samples. Acetate appears to function both as a degradation product of longer-chain compounds and as a precursor for smaller molecules such as CO2 and CH4. The low CH4 concentrations produced during the experiments relative to in-situ conditions can be explained by the absence of active methanogenic microorganisms that convert acetate or CO2 to CH4. Furthermore, isotopic analyses revealed that CH4 produced experimentally exhibits a distinct abiotic δ 13C signature around −34‰, in contrast to the microbial CH4 observed in the Nankai Trough sediments. Dissolved organic matter shows a clear decrease in oxygen- and sulfur-bearing compounds with increasing temperature. This trend reflects enhanced thermal decarboxylation and breakdown of thiols, thioethers and thiophene structures, releasing volatile sulfur species, predominantly H2S. These results indicate that abiotic reactions in deep marine sediments can provide a limited supply of metabolic substrates even near and beyond the currently known thermal limit of life. This implies that substrate availability, rather than temperature alone, may contribute to defining the upper boundary of the deep biosphere

title: Experimental constraints on niobium mobility and pyrochlore crystallization in evolved carbonatite liquids
description: Publication date: Available online 15 September 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Qi Li, Xiao-Chun Li, Xue-Yin Yuan, Daniel E. Harlov, Hong-Rui Fan, Xian-Hua Li, Ming-Guo Zhai
abstract: Carbonatite-related niobium (Nb) deposits account for the majority of global Nb resources, with pyrochlore [(Ca,Na)Nb2O6(F,OH)] as the principal Nb-hosting phase. Pyrochlore is commonly regarded as an early-crystallized magmatic mineral in carbonatite, yet it is increasingly reported from late-stage, highly evolved lithologies. As Nb is commonly considered to be relatively immobile in H2O-rich media, the extent to which highly evolved, H2O-rich liquids enhance Nb mobility and govern pyrochlore crystallization remains poorly constrained in carbonatite systems. To address this issue, we conducted hydrothermal diamond anvil cell experiments to investigate pyrochlore dissolution and precipitation in alkali-rich (Na, K) solutions containing various salt components (carbonate, bicarbonate, fluoride, chloride, and sulfate), chemically analogous to evolved carbonatite melts. Pyrochlore was nearly insoluble in SO4 2-- and Cl--rich liquids throughout the heating process even at ∼ 850 °C. In contrast, CO3 2–- and F--rich liquids induced pyrochlore dissolution at much lower temperatures (590–705 °C). Using dissolution temperature as a qualitative indicator of Nb mobility, these results demonstrate that carbonate and fluoride are highly effective components promoting Nb mobility. For liquids containing the same type of volatile component, pyrochlore exhibited lower dissolution temperatures in K-rich than in Na-rich systems, because Na+ can stabilize the crystal lattice of pyrochlore and retard its breakdown. In experiments showing substantial Nb dissolution, Nb-rich precipitates formed upon liquid cooling were further characterized. Pyrochlore crystallized only from F- and Na-rich systems, whereas Na-rich but F-poor liquids produced lueshite (NaNbO3) and F- and Na-poor liquids yielded fersmite (CaNb2O6). Chemical variations in liquid also affect pyrochlore composition, with increased Na/Ca ratio of the liquid enhancing Na, REE, and U incorporation into pyrochlore. These findings provide the first direct experimental evidence that highly evolved carbonatite melts or brine-melts can sustain appreciable Nb mobility and precipitate pyrochlore, thereby expanding the formation window for pyrochlore beyond early magmatic crystallization.

title: Hydrothermal experiments reveal methanol, ammonia, and methylamines as tracers of pH and temperature with potential application to Enceladus, Europa, and other icy ocean worlds
description: Publication date: Available online 13 September 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Kirtland J. Robinson, Everett L. Shock, Sean P. Sylva, Jeffrey S. Seewald
abstract: Icy ocean worlds in our solar system are prime targets in the search for extraterrestrial life. Enceladus and Europa are icy moons with evidence of global subsurface oceans in contact with rocky interiors, which may provide habitable environments for chemotrophic life. However, the interaction between water and rock and any changes in fluid chemistry are poorly constrained because the icy shells of these moons inhibit direct sampling of subsurface aqueous environments. Characterization of subseafloor processes may depend on chemical signatures in materials that are transported to accessible sampling locations near the surfaces of these icy ocean worlds. Here we present a theoretical framework where organic compounds likely to be present at icy ocean worlds can be utilized as tracers of geochemistry if they approach metastable equilibrium abundances, which we test with laboratory experiments. We use thermodynamic calculations of aqueous solutions to demonstrate that abundances of methanol, ammonia, and methylamines (compounds selected based on Enceladus’ plume data) should approach steady state ratios based on reversible substitution reactions that are systematically controlled by pH and temperature. We test these calculations by performing laboratory hydrothermal experiments ranging in temperature (175-325℃) and pH (∼3.5–7.0), demonstrating that chemical concentration measurements alone can be used in predictive models to accurately constrain the different conditions across experimental systems. As examples, with experiments conducted at 250℃, we demonstrate that the chemical tracers in a pH ∼ 3.5 solution predict a pH ≤ ∼5.0 and a temperature of ∼ 225-250℃, while the tracers in a solution at pH ∼ 7.0 predict a pH of ∼ 6.0–7.5 and a temperature of ∼ 200-275℃. Notably, all of our high-temperature experiments are cooled to room temperature prior to analysis, indicating that the hydrothermal signal (i.e., the ratio of chemical species) is preserved due to the slowing of reaction kinetics at lower temperatures, which may be analogous to hydrothermal fluids that vent into icy oceans. Similarly, we also performed a partial-cooling experiment that shows a tracer signal produced at 325℃ remains largely preserved for a year after the experiment was cooled to 175℃. We compare experimental results from gold reaction vessels to experiments previously conducted in glass vessels to assess the effects of experimental vessel type and find only minor differences in product distributions over time. Overall, our findings provide additional motivation to target small organic molecules for analysis on future missions to icy ocean worlds in order to constrain subsurface geochemical parameters critical to habitability

title: Disrupted magmatic evolution controls Nb and REE co-enrichment in alkaline-carbonatite systems
description: Publication date: Available online 13 September 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Chunwan Wei, Cheng Xu, John Mavrogenes, Jindrich Kynicky, Wenlei Song, Yuhan Ma
abstract: Alkaline-carbonatite complexes host major Nb and rare earth element (REE) resources, but the two are rarely concentrated in the same lithological unit. Thus, the processes that allow their co-concentration despite their contrasting geochemical behavior remain unclear. Here we investigate the Khotgor complex, Mongolia, where Nb and REE mineralization is concentrated in calcite-rich syenite, whereas associated feldspar-dominated syenites and carbonatites are non-mineralized. Calcite and REE-bearing minerals from the mineralized syenite and carbonatites have uniform 87Sr/86Sr(i) (∼0.70373) and εNd(i) (∼+1.5), indicating a common mantle-sourced magmatic system. Pyrochlore records progressive Nb sequestration during evolution from silicate-dominated magmas to carbonate-rich liquid. Sparse, zoned Ta-Ti-Zr-rich grains associated with phenocrysts were followed by more abundant, unzoned Nb-dominant pyrochlore aggregate intergrowths of calcite and synchysite. Later hydrothermal modification produced Ba-Sr-rich domains while largely retaining Nb. Calcite grains in the mineralized unit record a shift from magmatic crystallization to REE precipitation, as shown by the decrease in La/YbCN from ∼19 in phenocryst cores to ∼6 in synchysite-bearing matrix calcite. Strong negative Ce anomalies (Ce*∼0.03) in matrix calcites and complementary positive anomalies (Ce*∼2.5) in phenocryst rims record subsequent oxidation. Low δ18O values (∼2.74 ‰) of fluid-related patchy apatite record involvement of an isotopically light meteoric fluid, whereas the increase in calcite δ18O from ∼8 ‰ in phenocryst cores to 10–25 ‰ in rims and matrix reflects calcite-fluid fractionation during cooling. Non-mineralized carbonatites (La/YbCN ∼ 0.06) represent carbonate-rich fractions formed after REE sequestration. We infer that magmatic differentiation co-concentrated Nb and REE in a carbonate-rich liquid, in which Nb precipitated as pyrochlore, while meteoric ingress triggered in situ REE precipitation without substantial Nb remobilization, thereby trapping both metals within the same mineralized unit.

title: The iron mineralogy of Bennu samples: similarities and variations among CI chondritic materials
description: Publication date: Available online 11 September 2026 Source: Geochimica et Cosmochimica Acta Author(s): Kana Amano, Jean-Christophe Viennet, Pierre Beck, Sergey Yaroslavtsev, Dimitrios Bessas, Aleksandr Chumakov, Jean-Philippe Celse, Ludovic Delbes, Tomoki Nakamura, Yuma Enokido, Kanako Sakamoto, Shogo Tachibana, Mathieu Roskosz
abstract: Recent findings from sample-return missions targeting carbonaceous asteroids suggest that CI-like (Carbonaceous Ivuna-type) small bodies are more common in the solar system than previously thought. However, the general redox characteristics and variations among CI materials remain largely unexplored due to their limited availability on Earth. Moreover, CI meteorites have likely undergone irreversible terrestrial oxidation, resulting in modifications of the iron speciation and the redox states. In this context, the iron mineralogy of samples from the carbonaceous asteroid Bennu allows us to reassess the redox conditions of CI materials during its formation. We performed X-ray diffraction and Mössbauer spectroscopy of two Bennu particles from the hummocky group, as well as Oued Chebeika 002 CI meteorite. We compare their iron speciation to that of other CI and CI-like materials, including samples from the asteroid Ryugu, Orgueil CI meteorite, and Oued Chebeika 002 CI meteorite. The results show that Bennu particles contain substantial amounts of Fe sulfides (pyrrhotite, mackinawite, and pentlandite), along with Fe oxide (magnetite) and Fe-bearing (Mg-rich) phyllosilicates, similar to Ryugu samples. Cryogenic Mössbauer analysis indicates no significant contribution from ferric oxyhydroxides (i.e., ferrihydrite) in Bennu and Oued Chebeika 002 samples, confirming the previous electron microscopy observations of those samples. These observations imply that Fe3+ forming ferrihydrite observed in historical CI meteorites (e.g., Orgueil, Alais) results from long-term terrestrial oxidation of Fe2+ in sulfides, especially submicron-sized ones. This further strengthens the view that the actual CI materials and their formation environments are less oxidizing than previously estimated from old CI meteorite falls. The Fe3+/(Fe3++Fe2+) ratios in phyllosilicates in the hummocky particles range from 50 to 70%, indicating local heterogeneity within individual particles. Whereas similar values have been reported for Bennu samples (determined by X-ray Absorption Near-Edge Structure spectroscopy), Ryugu samples, and Oued Chebeika 002 samples (i.e., ∼50–65% of Fe3+/(Fe3++Fe2+)phyllosilicates), there may be slightly Fe3+-rich sub-regions (close to ∼ 70%) in our Bennu particles. Furthermore, we found two distinct mineral assemblages among CI and CI-like materials: (i) relatively well-crystallized phyllosilicates without mackinawite but with pyrrhotite, and (ii) disordered phyllosilicates coexisting with mackinawite, a metastable Fe sulfide. The latter finding is consistent with recent studies of mackinawite in Bennu and Ryugu samples, which suggest its formation at the early stages of CI alteration. Together with previous studies of Bennu, Ryugu, and Orgueil samples, our results suggest that different phyllosilicate assemblages preserve distinct Fe valence states, potentially recording redox conditions associated with different stages of formation. The CI materials have conventionally been regarded as relatively equilibrated and homogeneous, however, our results demonstrate the potential of combining clay mineral crystallinity and Fe valence states to unravel formation histories at a finer scale.
